english: a particle used at the end of a sentence, often to soften the tone or express a mild question or suggestion. Similar to "eh?" or a gentle "okay?" in English.
cantonese_sentence: 好啊吖？
jyutping_sentence: hou2 aa1 aa1?
english_sentence: Okay, then?

english: Isn't it? / You know? / Of course! (Implies agreement or confirmation)
cantonese_sentence: 佢好叻㗎吖嘛！
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hou2 lek1 gaa3 aa1 maa3!
english_sentence: He's very talented, isn't he/you know! (Implies that this is already known or should be known)

english: Right? / Is that right? / Isn't it? (a tag question)
cantonese_sentence: 你聽日會嚟㗎吖嗱？
jyutping_sentence: nei5 ting1 jat6 wui5 lai4 gaa3 aa1 laa2?
english_sentence: You're coming tomorrow, right?

english: Sentence-final particle expressing confirmation, agreement, surprise, or mild exclamation.
cantonese_sentence: 好呀！ | hou2 aa3! | Good!
jyutping_sentence: ho2 aa3!
english_sentence: Good!

english: Used as a prefix before names or kinship terms, often to indicate familiarity or affection.
cantonese_sentence: 阿婆今日去飲茶
jyutping_sentence: aa3 po4 gam1 jat6 heoi3 jam2 caa4
english_sentence: Grandma is going to have dim sum today.

cantonese_sentence: 阿爸今日返屋企食飯。
jyutping_sentence: aa3 baa1 gam1 jat6 faan1 uk1 kei2 sik6 faan6.
english_sentence: Dad is coming home for dinner today.

english: Uncle (a polite way to address an older man, often a stranger)
cantonese_sentence: 阿伯，唔該幫我睇下呢度應該點樣搭車呀？
jyutping_sentence: aa3 baak3, m4 goi1 bong1 ngo5 tai2 haa5 ni1 dou6 jing1 goi1 dim2 joeng2 daap3 ce1 aa3?
english_sentence: Uncle, excuse me, can you help me figure out how to take the bus from here?

jyutping: aa3 bang1 giu3 gau2 – jyut6 giu3 jyut6 zau2
english: Calling a toothless man's dog - the more you call, the further it runs. (Meaning: Counterproductive, the opposite of what you want happening)
cantonese_sentence: 佢叫個仔唔好賭錢，點知佢阿崩叫狗——越叫越走，賭得仲勁。
english_sentence: He told his son not to gamble, but as they say, calling a toothless man's dog - the more you call, the further it runs. He gambles even more now.

jyutping: a3 bang1 cheui1 siu1 -- saai1 seng1 waai6 hei3
english: A buck-toothed person playing the flute - wasting breath and ruining the sound
cantonese_sentence: 你唔好再同佢講咁多啦，阿崩吹簫——嘥聲壞氣。
jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zoi3 tung4 keoi5 gong2 gam3 do1 laa1, a3 bang1 cheui1 siu1 -- saai1 seng1 waai6 hei3.
english_sentence: Don't talk to him so much anymore, it's like a buck-toothed person playing the flute - wasting breath and ruining the sound (meaning: it's a waste of time/effort).

english: Anyone and everyone; all sorts of people
cantonese_sentence: 而家啲餐廳咩人都有，阿保阿勝，唔係淨係後生仔去㗎啦。
jyutping_sentence: ji4 gaa1 di1 caan1 teng1 me1 jan4 dou1 jau5, aa3 bou2 aa3 sing3, m4 hai6 zing6 hai6 hau6 saang1 zai2 heoi3 gaa3 laa1.
english_sentence: Nowadays, restaurants have all sorts of people; it's not just young people who go there.

cantonese_sentence: 我阿大好錫我㗎。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 a3 daai6 hou2 sek3 ngo5 gaa3.
english_sentence: My eldest brother loves me very much.

english: An incompetent official; a bumbling bureaucrat; a useless administrator. (Referring to someone who holds a position but is utterly inept and ineffective, often through hereditary or political appointment).
cantonese_sentence: 佢做咗經理之後乜都唔識，真係阿斗官嚟。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 zo2 ging1 lei5 zi1 hau6 mat1 dou1 m4 sik1, zan1 hai6 a3 dau2 gun1 lai4.
english_sentence: After he became the manager, he didn't know anything; he really is an incompetent official.

english: a common nickname, often used for someone young or familiar; can be similar to "Tim" or "Danny"
cantonese_sentence: 阿丁好乖呀，成日幫手做家務。
jyutping_sentence: aa3 ding1 hou2 gwaai1 aa3, sing4 jat6 bong1 sau2 zou6 gaa1 mou6.
english_sentence: Ah Ding is very well-behaved, he always helps with chores.

cantonese_sentence: 阿仔，你今日乖唔乖呀？
jyutping_sentence: aa3 zai2, nei5 gam1 jat6 gwaai1 m4 gwaai1 aa3?
english_sentence: Son, were you good today?

english: Older sister; term of address for a slightly older woman, often a domestic helper, waitress, or vendor.
cantonese_sentence: 阿姐，唔該幫我攞多碗飯。
jyutping_sentence: aa3 je1, m4 goi1 bong1 ngo5 lo2 do1 wun2 faan6.
english_sentence: Excuse me (sister/waitress), please help me get another bowl of rice.

cantonese_sentence: 你唔好喺度阿吱阿咗啦，快啲決定啦！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 hai2 dou6 a3 zi1 a3 zo2 laa1, faai3 di1 kyut3 ding6 laa1!
english_sentence: Don't be so indecisive, make a decision quickly!

english: Anyone and everyone; any Tom, Dick, or Harry.
cantonese_sentence: 阿豬阿狗都話自己識唱歌。
jyutping_sentence: aa3 zyu1 aa3 gau2 dou1 waa6 zi6 gei2 sik1 cheong3 go1.
english_sentence: Everyone and anyone claims they know how to sing.

english: A nickname, often used affectionately for someone with a slightly chubby or fortunate appearance. Think of it as a kind of "lucky chubby."
cantonese_sentence: 阿福個樣好得意。
jyutping_sentence: aa3 fuk1 go3 joeng2 hou2 dak1 ji3.
english_sentence: Lucky Chubby's face is very cute.

english: Older brother; a respectful way to address a young man.
cantonese_sentence: 阿哥，唔該幫我攞個盒落嚟。
jyutping_sentence: a3 go1, m4 goi1 bong1 ngo5 lo2 go3 hap6 lok6 lei4.
english_sentence: Brother, please help me take that box down.

english: Go-go (referring to the Go-go dance or style, often used to describe someone dressing or dancing in a flamboyant or dated style)
cantonese_sentence: 佢着到成個阿哥哥咁，真係好核突。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zoek3 dou3 seng4 go3 aa3 go1 go1 gam2, zan1 hai6 hou2 hat6 dat1.
english_sentence: She's dressed like someone from the Go-go era, it's really awful.

cantonese_sentence: 阿姑好錫佢哋啲仔女。
jyutping_sentence: a3 gu1 hou2 sek3 keoi5 dei6 dik1 zai2 neoi5.
english_sentence: Aunt really dotes on her children.

cantonese_sentence: 阿公成日帶我去公園玩。
jyutping_sentence: aa3 gung1 sing4 jat6 daai3 ngo5 heoi3 gung1 jyun2 waan2.
english_sentence: Grandfather always takes me to the park to play.

cantonese_sentence: 我哋阿head好nice㗎。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 aa3 head hou2 nice gaa3.
english_sentence: Our supervisor is very nice.

english: Auntie (mother's sister, or a polite address for a woman of one's mother's generation)
cantonese_sentence: 阿姨，呢個包幾錢呀？
english_sentence: Auntie, how much is this bun?

cantonese_sentence: 佢成日做老細嘅阿二，幫佢做晒啲嘢。
english_sentence: He always acts as the boss's gofer, doing all the work for him.

cantonese_sentence: 我哋聽日去阿舅屋企拜年。
english_sentence: We're going to my maternal uncle's house to visit for Chinese New Year tomorrow.

cantonese_sentence: 我哋屋企嘅阿孻仔最得人錫㗎啦。
english_sentence: Our family's youngest son is the most spoiled.

cantonese_sentence: 我阿媽煮嘅餸最好食。
english_sentence: My mother's cooking is the best.

jyutping: a3 maa1 dou1 m4 jing6 dak1
english: Unrecognizably changed (even your own mother wouldn't recognize you)
cantonese_sentence: 佢化咗個咁濃嘅妝，阿媽都唔認得佢啦！
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 faa3 zo2 go3 gam3 nung4 ge3 zong1, a3 maa1 dou1 m4 jing6 dak1 keoi5 laa1!
english_sentence: She put on such heavy makeup, even her mother wouldn't recognize her!

cantonese_sentence: 你講嘅嘢咁廢，咪好似阿媽係女人咁囉！
english_sentence: What you're saying is so pointless, it's like saying your mother is a woman!

cantonese_sentence: 阿嫲煮嘅飯最好食。
jyutping_sentence: aa3 maa4 zyu2 ge3 faan6 zeoi3 hou2 sik6.
english_sentence: Grandmother's cooking is the most delicious.

english: Literally "any cat any dog," meaning anyone and everyone, referring to people of little importance or quality.
cantonese_sentence: 是但阿貓阿狗都做得掂啦！
jyutping_sentence: si6 daan6 aa3 maau1 aa3 gau2 dou1 zou6 dak1 dim6 laa1!
english_sentence: Anyone could do it! (Implying it's very easy)

english: What kind of person/What sort of person
cantonese_sentence: 佢呢個人真係唔知係阿乜人嚟㗎。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ni1 go3 jan4 zan1 hai6 m4 zi1 hai6 a3 mat1 jan4 lai4 ge3.
english_sentence: I really don't know what kind of person he is.

cantonese_sentence: 你阿茂整餅，唔使問人！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 a3 mau6 zing2 beng2, m4 sai2 man6 jan4!
english_sentence: You're acting like a fool doing your own thing without asking for advice! (Literally: You, Ah Mau, making cakes, don't need to ask people!)

cantonese: 阿茂整餅——冇嗰樣整嗰樣
jyutping: a3 mau6 zing2 beng2 — mou5 go2 joeng2 zing2 go2 joeng2
english: A-Mau making cakes - making it up as he goes along/creating something without the proper knowledge or resources, resulting in a bizarre outcome. Basically, doing something without the right skills and making a mess of it.
cantonese_sentence: 佢對電腦一竅不通，但又要自己搞，真係阿茂整餅——冇嗰樣整嗰樣。
english_sentence: He doesn't know anything about computers but he insists on fixing it himself, he's really just making it up as he goes along and making a mess.

cantonese_sentence: 阿妹，你今日好靚女喎!
jyutping_sentence: a3 mui1, nei5 gam1 jat6 hou2 leng3 neoi5 wo3!
english_sentence: Younger sister/Hey young lady, you look very pretty today!

english: A (prefix used before a nickname, often for a child or someone younger); small, thin
cantonese_sentence: 阿奀好細粒，食多啲嘢啦！
jyutping_sentence: aa3 ngan1 hou2 sai3 lap1, sik6 do1 di1 je5 laa1!
english_sentence: Little Ngan is so small, eat more!

cantonese_sentence: 阿女好乖。
jyutping_sentence: a3 neoi5 hou2 gwaai1.
english_sentence: My daughter is very well-behaved.

cantonese_sentence: 我今日扶咗個阿婆過馬路呀。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 jat6 fu4 zo2 go3 aa3 po4 gwo3 maa5 lou6 aa3.
english_sentence: I helped an old woman cross the road today.

english: Indian person (often used in a mildly derogatory way, can be considered offensive depending on context and tone)
cantonese_sentence: 唔好咁樣叫人哋阿三啦，好無禮貌㗎。
jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 gam2 joeng2 giu3 jan4 dei6 a3 saam1 laa1, hou2 mou5 lai5 maau6 gaa3.
english_sentence: Don't call people "Ah Sam" like that, it's very impolite.

english: Mr. Sang (used to address someone with the surname Sang)
cantonese_sentence: 阿生，你今日返工辛唔辛苦啊？
jyutping_sentence: aa3 sang1, nei5 gam1 jat6 faan1 gung1 san1 m4 san1 fu2 aa3?
english_sentence: Mr. Sang, was work tough for you today?

english: Younger child (often used affectionately, particularly for younger siblings or younger friends)
cantonese_sentence: 阿細，你今日想食咩呀？
jyutping_sentence: a3 sai3, nei5 gam1 jat6 soeng2 sik6 me1 aa3?
english_sentence: Little one, what do you want to eat today?

english: Auntie (a term to address middle-aged women, often used by younger people, not necessarily a direct relative)
cantonese_sentence: 唔該，阿嬸，呢個點去啊？
jyutping_sentence: m4 goi1, aa3 sam2, ni1 go3 dim2 heoi3 aa3?
english_sentence: Excuse me, Auntie, how do I get to this place?

english: (informal) Old man; old fellow; also used to address someone named "Sau" affectionately/teasingly, regardless of age. Can also be used sarcastically.
cantonese_sentence: 阿壽成日都唔聽人講嘢㗎啦。
jyutping_sentence: a3 sau6 sing4 jat6 dou1 m4 ting1 jan4 gong2 je5 ga3 laa1.
english_sentence: That old man never listens to what people say.

english: Servant, maid, someone who runs errands
cantonese_sentence: 阿四，幫我買杯奶茶啦。
jyutping_sentence: a3 sei3, bong1 ngo5 maai5 bui1 naai5 caa4 laa1.
english_sentence: Servant (or you), please help me buy a cup of milk tea.

english: Auntie (used to address or refer to older women, often in a slightly informal or even mildly disrespectful way depending on context). It can sometimes imply a lack of sophistication or being out of touch.
cantonese_sentence: 阿嬋，你唔好阻住條路啦。
jyutping_sentence: a3 caan4, nei5 m4 hou2 zo2 zyu6 tiu4 lou6 laa1.
english_sentence: Auntie, please don't block the path.

cantonese_sentence: 你做咩咁阿傻㗎？
jyutping_sentence: nei5 zou6 me1 gam3 aa3 so4 gaa3?
english_sentence: Why are you being such an idiot?

cantonese_sentence: 咪掂佢呀，阿蛇好危險㗎。
jyutping_sentence: mai5 dim6 keoi5 aa3, aa3 se4 hou2 ngai4 him2 gaa3.
english_sentence: Don't touch it, the snake is very dangerous.

cantonese_sentence: 我阿邊度識得你阿誰呀？
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 a3 bin1 dou6 sik1 dak1 nei5 a3 seoi4 aa3?
english_sentence: How would I know who you are? (Who even are you?)

english: Smelly, especially of sweat or body odor. Often used to describe children or messy situations.
cantonese_sentence: 你隻貓好阿臊喎！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 zek3 maau1 hou2 a3 sou3 wo3!
english_sentence: Your cat is really smelly!

cantonese_sentence: 阿嫂，你煮嘅飯好好味呀！
jyutping_sentence: a3 sou2, nei5 jyu2 ge3 faan6 hou2 hou2 mei6 aa3!
english_sentence: Sister-in-law, the food you cooked is very delicious!

english: Uncle (term of address for a man of one's father's generation or older, even if not related)
cantonese_sentence: 阿叔，唔該幫我攞個行李。
english_sentence: Uncle, please help me get my luggage.

english: A married woman (often used for a woman who is past her prime and perceived as acting in a way considered childish or foolish for her age/marital status). Can be considered derogatory.
cantonese_sentence: 佢咁大個人仲成日扮可愛，真係好似個阿太咁。
english_sentence: She's so old but still always pretends to be cute, she really acts like an old married woman.

english: hunchback, a person with a hunchback
cantonese_sentence: 佢細個嘅時候已經有啲阿駝
english_sentence: He had a bit of a hunchback since he was young.

jyutping: a3 to4 haang4 lou6 -- cung1 cung1 dei2
cantonese_sentence: 佢行路阿駝行路——舂舂地，好似好辛苦咁。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 haang4 lou6 a3 to4 haang4 lou6 -- cung1 cung1 dei2, hou2 ci5 hou2 san1 fu2 gam2.
english_sentence: He walks with a limp, like he's in a lot of pain.

cantonese_sentence: 佢成日笑阿差講嘢有口音。
english_sentence: He always laughs at Indians for their accent.

english: Country bumpkin, a derogatory term for mainland Chinese people.
cantonese_sentence: 你都唔好咁阿燦啦，人哋擺明呃你錢。
english_sentence: Don't be such a country bumpkin, they're clearly trying to scam you.

jyutping: aa3 chiu1 zoek3 fu3 -- guk6 zyu6
english: Stuck with it (unwillingly), Resigned to it. The situation is stifling/suffocating but unavoidable.
cantonese_sentence: 佢唔想做呢份工，但為咗搵食，阿超着褲——焗住做落去。
english_sentence: He doesn't want to do this job, but in order to make a living, he's stuck with it and has to keep doing it.

cantonese_sentence: 阿爺今日飲咗好多茶呀。
english_sentence: Grandfather drank a lot of tea today.

cantonese_sentence: 今年嘅亞姐質素好似幾好喎。
english_sentence: This year's Miss Asia contestants seem pretty good.

english: A particle indicating questioning, surprise, confirmation, or a final particle to soften the tone.
cantonese_sentence: 你食咗飯呀？
english_sentence: Have you eaten? (Expressing curiosity or confirmation)

cantonese_sentence: 哎吔！唔記得帶銀包喇！
english_sentence: Oops! I forgot to bring my wallet!

english: Oh no, (my) dad! / Oh crap, dad!
cantonese_sentence: 哎吔老竇返咗屋企，死啦，我仲未做完功課！
english_sentence: Ai1 jaa1 lou5 dau6 faan1 zo2 uk1 kei2, si2 laa1, ngo5 zung6 mei6 zou6 jyun4 gung1 fo3!

cantonese_sentence: 你唔好呃我錢呀！
english_sentence: You better not swindle my money!

cantonese_sentence: 我喺巴士站等緊你
english_sentence: Ngo5 hai2 baa1 si2 zaam6 dang2 gan2 nei5

english: Showy, boastful, impressive (often used sarcastically). Can also mean powerful or capable.
cantonese_sentence: 佢咁巴閉，咩都識做嘅。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam3 baa1 bai3, me1 dou1 sik1 zou6 ge3.
english_sentence: He's so capable, he knows how to do everything.

english: Bro, Brother, Mate (term of endearment between men)
cantonese_sentence: 今日同啲巴打去咗踢波。
jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 tung4 di1 baa1 daa1 heoi3 zo2 tek3 bo1.
english_sentence: I went to play football with the bros today.

english: Grab (a quick meal or snack); scarf down
cantonese_sentence: 我哋去茶餐廳巴揸個麵包先啦。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 heoi3 caa4 caan1 teng1 baa1 zaa1 go3 min6 baau1 sin1 laa1.
english_sentence: Let's go to the cafe to grab a quick bun first.

english: Spicy; Fiery; Hot-tempered (can describe food or a person)
cantonese_sentence: 佢個人好巴辣，你小心啲。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 go3 jan4 hou2 baa1 laat6, nei5 siu2 sam1 di1.
english_sentence: She's a very fiery person, be careful.

cantonese_sentence: 佢戴咗頂巴黎帽, 好有藝術家嘅風格。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 daai3 zo2 ding2 baa1 lai4 mou2, hou2 jau5 ngai6 seot1 gaa1 ge3 fung1 gaak3.
english_sentence: She wore a beret, giving off a very artistic vibe.

cantonese_sentence: 我想搭巴士去尖沙咀。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 soeng2 daap3 baa1 si2 heoi3 zim1 saa1 zeoi2.
english_sentence: I want to take the bus to Tsim Sha Tsui.

cantonese_sentence: 嗰間酒吧嘅吧女幾靚女㗎。
jyutping_sentence: go2 gaan1 baa1 au1 ge3 baa1 neoi5 gei2 leng3 neoi2 gaa3.
english_sentence: The barmaid at that bar is quite pretty.

english: handle; to hold; (measure word for things with handles, bunches, etc.)
cantonese_sentence: 我攞把遮
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 lo2 baa2 ze1
english_sentence: I'll take an umbrella.

english: Undecided, wavering, having difficulty making up one's mind
cantonese_sentence: 你成日都把心唔定，點做決定啊？
jyutping_sentence: nei5 seng4 jat6 dou1 baa2 sam1 m4 ding6, dim2 zou6 kyut3 ding6 aa3?
english_sentence: You're always so indecisive, how are you going to make a decision?

cantonese_sentence: 唔好再激我，唔係我會把火㗎！
jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 zoi3 gik1 ngo5, m4 hai6 ngo5 wui baa2 fo2 gaa3!
english_sentence: Don't provoke me anymore, or I'll get angry!

english: (A woman's) great-aunt (from her husband's side); Husband's paternal great aunt.
cantonese_sentence: 我奶奶嘅家姐咪就係我嘅把家姑婆囉。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 naai5 naai5 ge3 gaa1 ze1 mai1 zau6 hai6 ngo5 ge3 baa2 gaa1 gu1 po4 lo1.
english_sentence: My grandmother's older sister is my husband's great-aunt.

cantonese_sentence: 你講乜嘢把鬼呀？
jyutping_sentence: nei5 gong2 mat1 je5 baa2 gwai2 aa3?
english_sentence: What nonsense are you talking about?

english: To be overly eloquent or smooth-tongued; to be good at saying things that are pleasing or persuasive, often with insincerity. (Lit: to have one's mouth pass through oil)
cantonese_sentence: 佢把口𠺘過油，你唔好咁易信佢講嘅嘢。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 baa2 hau2 nang4 gwo3 jau4, nei5 m4 hou2 gam3 ji6 seon3 keoi5 gong2 ge3 je5.
english_sentence: He's very smooth-tongued, don't be so quick to believe what he says.

english: Loose-tongued; unable to keep secrets; having a big mouth.
cantonese_sentence: 佢把口唔修, 成日周圍唱人.
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 baa2 hau2 m4 sau1, seng4 jat6 zau1 wai4 coeng3 jan4.
english_sentence: He's loose-tongued and always blabbing about other people.

cantonese_sentence: 醫生幫我把脈，話我冇乜大礙。
english_sentence: The doctor took my pulse and said there wasn't anything seriously wrong with me.

english: To flirt; to hit on someone
cantonese_sentence: 佢琴日喺酒吧把炮把到條女。
english_sentence: He flirted with a girl at the bar yesterday.

english: To suck up to, flatter, brown-nose
cantonese_sentence: 你唔好成日喺老細面前把屁啦！
english_sentence: You shouldn't always brown-nose the boss!

cantonese_sentence: 佢揸住把舦，控制住架船嘅方向。
english_sentence: He's holding the steering wheel, controlling the direction of the boat.

english: Alright, fine, okay, let it be.
cantonese_sentence: 罷啦，由佢自己決定啦。

english: A catch (referring to a person, usually male, who is successful, wealthy, and desirable as a romantic partner)
cantonese_sentence: 我個朋友嫁咗個筍盤，住豪宅揸靚車。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 go3 pang4 jau5 ga3 zo2 go3 seon2 pun4, zyu6 hou4 zaak6 zaa1 leng3 ce1.
english_sentence: My friend married a catch; she lives in a mansion and drives a fancy car.

cantonese_sentence: 我今晚想煎啲信肉食。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 maan1 soeng2 zin1 di1 seon3 juk6 sik6.
english_sentence: Tonight I want to fry some Spam to eat.

cantonese_sentence: 隻狗好馴品㗎，唔會咬人。
jyutping_sentence: zek3 gau2 hou2 seon4 ban2 gaa3, m4 wui5 ngaau5 jan4.
english_sentence: This dog is very docile; it won't bite people.

english: Purely renting a room (as opposed to renting an entire apartment/house)
cantonese_sentence: 我哋只係純粹租房住，唔會喺度長住嘅。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 zi2 hai6 seon4 seoi6 zo1 fong2 zyu6, m4 wui5 hai2 dou6 coeng4 zyu6 ge3.
english_sentence: We are only renting a room here, we won't be staying here long-term.

cantonese_sentence: 佢個人好純情㗎，可能未拍過拖。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 go3 jan4 hou2 seon4 cing4 gaa3, ho2 nang4 mei6 paak3 gwo3 to1.
english_sentence: He/She is very innocent, probably hasn't been in a relationship before.

english: To fight alone, to single out, to play one-on-one (in sports)
cantonese_sentence: 你唔好成日單打佢啦，對佢唔公平嘅。
jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 sing4 jat6 daan1 daa2 keoi5 laa1, deoi3 keoi5 m4 gung1 ping4 ge3.
english_sentence: Don't always single him out and pick on him, it's not fair to him.

cantonese_sentence: 我哋個project好順檔呀。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 go3 project hou2 seon6 dong3 a3.
english_sentence: Our project is going really smoothly.

cantonese_sentence: 祝你一路順風順水，心想事成！
jyutping_sentence: zuk1 nei5 jat1 lou6 seon6 fung1 seon6 seoi2, sam1 soeng2 si6 sing4!
english_sentence: Wishing you smooth sailing all the way and may all your wishes come true!

english: A ride; to hitch a ride; literally "smooth wind car" (implying a ride made easy)
cantonese_sentence: 不如我哋搭順風車返屋企啦?
jyutping_sentence: bat1 jyu4 ngo5 dei6 daap3 seon6 fung1 ce1 faan1 uk1 kei2 laa1?
english_sentence: Why don't we hitch a ride home?

cantonese_sentence: 佢喺順境嘅時候都要保持謙卑。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 seon6 ging2 ge3 si4 hau6 dou1 jiu3 bo2 ci4 him1 bei1.
english_sentence: Even when he is in favorable circumstances, he must remain humble.

cantonese_sentence: 呢個名好順口。
jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 ming2 hou2 seon6 hau2.
english_sentence: This name is easy to pronounce.

cantonese_sentence: 佢講嘢好順溜。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2 je5 hou2 seon6 lau6-1.
english_sentence: He/She speaks very smoothly.

english: Agreed, to be amenable, to go along with something
cantonese_sentence: 我冇所謂，順攤啦。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 mou5 so2 wai6, seon6 taan1 laa1.
english_sentence: I don't mind, I agree.

english: To compromise, to accommodate, to meet each other halfway
cantonese_sentence: 我哋互相相就吓啦，咁樣先可以解決問題。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 wu6 soeng1 soeng1 zau6 haa5 laa1, gam2 joeng2 sin1 ho2 ji5 gaai2 kyut3 man6 tai4.
english_sentence: Let's compromise with each other so we can solve the problem.

cantonese_sentence: 呢間餐廳嘅嘢食幾相宜㗎，都幾好食。
jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 caan1 teng1 ge3 je5 sik6 gei2 soeng1 ji4 gaa3, dou1 gei2 hou2 sik6.
english_sentence: The food at this restaurant is quite reasonably priced and pretty tasty.

english: To get along with; to associate with
cantonese_sentence: 我同佢好相與㗎，成日一齊去玩。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 tung4 keoi5 hou2 soeng1 jyu5 gaa3, seng4 jat6 jat1 cai4 heoi3 waan2.
english_sentence: I get along with him very well, we often go out to play together.

english: To subtly criticize or sarcastically pick on someone; to make snide remarks.
cantonese_sentence: 佢成日都單單打打，真係好煩！
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 dou1 daan1 daan1 daa2 daa2, zan1 hai6 hou2 faan4!
english_sentence: He/She is always making snide remarks, it's so annoying!

english: It's best not to argue/bicker with someone. / Arguing is never good. (Literally: Arguing, not good mouth)
cantonese_sentence: 細路哥唔好成日相嗌唔好口, 要互相遷就吓。
jyutping_sentence: sai3 lou6 go1 m4 hou2 seng4 jat6 soeng1 aai3 m4 hou2 hau2, jiu3 wu6 soeng1 cin1 zau6 haa5.
english_sentence: Kids shouldn't argue all the time; they should be more accommodating to each other.

cantonese_sentence: 我好掛住佢，覺得好相思。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hou2 gwaa3 zyu6 keoi5, gok3 dak1 hou2 soeng1 si1.
english_sentence: I miss him/her a lot, I feel very homesick/longing for him/her.

english: Blind date; to go on a blind date
cantonese_sentence: 我聽日要去相睇，希望可以遇到好嘅對象啦！
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ting1 jat6 jiu3 heoi3 soeng1 tai2, hei1 mong6 ho2 ji5 jyu6 dou2 hou2 ge3 deoi3 zoeng6 laa1!
english_sentence: I'm going on a blind date tomorrow, I hope I can meet a good partner!

jyutping: soeng1 cing2 bat1 jyu4 ngau5 jyu6
english: Meeting by chance is better than making a formal invitation.
cantonese_sentence: 今日真係相請不如偶遇，竟然喺呢度見到你！
jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 zan1 hai6 soeng1 cing2 bat1 jyu4 ngau5 jyu6, ging2 jin4 hai2 ni1 dou6 gin3 dou2 nei5!
english_sentence: It's really a case of meeting by chance is better than making a formal invitation today, to actually see you here!

cantonese_sentence: 我唔記得咗攞箱頭筆返學。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 gei3 dak1 zo2 lo2 soeng1 tau4 bat1 faan1 hok6.
english_sentence: I forgot to bring a felt-tip marker to school.

cantonese_sentence: 呢度啲單位係商住兩用嘅，可以住又可以做生意。
jyutping_sentence: ni1 dou6 di1 daan1 wai2 hai6 soeng1 zyu6 loeng5 jung6 ge3, ho2 ji5 zyu6 jau6 ho2 ji5 zou6 saang1 ji3.
english_sentence: These units are commercial and residential mixed-use; you can live in them or run a business.

english: Businessman/Merchant/Shopkeeper (often used with a slightly negative or dismissive connotation, suggesting shrewdness or focus solely on profit)
cantonese_sentence: 個商家佬好識做生意。
jyutping_sentence: go3 soeng1 gaa1 lou2 hou2 sik1 zou6 saang1 ji3.
english_sentence: That businessman is very good at doing business.

cantonese_sentence: 嗰間商廈好多律師樓
jyutping_sentence: go2 gaan1 seong1 haa6 hou2 do1 leot6 si1 lau2
english_sentence: That commercial building has a lot of law firms.

cantonese_sentence: 今日不如我哋食商務午餐啦？
jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 bat1 jyu4 ngo5 dei6 sik6 soeng1 mou6 ng5 caan1 laa1?
english_sentence: How about we have a business lunch today?

cantonese_sentence: 今晚飲返杯雙蒸啦！
jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 jam2 faan1 bui1 soeng1 zing1 laa1!
english_sentence: Let's have a glass of double-distilled rice wine tonight!

english: Alone, single (referring to someone being the only one)
cantonese_sentence: 佢成日都自己一個單丁去食飯。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 dou1 zi6 gei2 jat1 go3 daan1 ding1 heoi3 sik6 faan6.
english_sentence: He always goes to eat alone by himself.

english: "Double non-" or "Both non-" referring to mainland Chinese parents who give birth to children in Hong Kong so the child can gain Hong Kong residency.
cantonese_sentence: 好多香港人唔鍾意雙非父母嚟香港生仔.
jyutping_sentence: ho2 do1 hoeng1 gong2 jan4 m4 zung1 ji3 soeng1 fei1 fu6 mou5 lai4 hoeng1 gong2 saang1 zai2.
english_sentence: Many Hong Kong people don't like mainland Chinese parents coming to Hong Kong to give birth to children.

english: Double sealed (typically referring to envelopes or packages)
cantonese_sentence: 呢個包裹要雙封先安全。
jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 baau1 gwo2 jiu3 soeng1 fung1 sin1 on1 cyun4.
english_sentence: This package needs to be double-sealed to be safe.

cantonese_sentence: 我想買張雙格床俾兩個仔。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 soeng2 maai5 zoeng1 soeng1 gaak3 cong4 bei2 loeng5 go3 zai2.
english_sentence: I want to buy a bunk bed for my two sons.

english: Double line (e.g., a double-lined road, writing in two lines)
cantonese_sentence: 呢條馬路係雙行線嚟嘅。
jyutping_sentence: ni1 tiu4 maa5 lou6 hai6 soeng1 hang4 sin3 lei4 ge3.
english_sentence: This road is a two-lane road (i.e., allowing traffic to travel in both directions).

cantonese_sentence: 佢著咗件雙襟嘅西裝。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zoek3 zo2 gin6 soeng1 kam1 ge3 sai1 zong1.
english_sentence: He's wearing a double-breasted suit.

english: Literally "double standing person," often refers to conjoined twins.
cantonese_sentence: 佢哋係一對雙企人，好罕見㗎。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 hai6 jat1 deoi3 soeng1 kei5 jan4, hou2 haan5 gin3 gaa3.
english_sentence: They are a pair of conjoined twins, very rare.

cantonese_sentence: 今年出雙糧，好開心呀！
jyutping_sentence: gam1 nin4 ceot1 soeng1 loeng4, hou2 hoi1 sam1 aa3!
english_sentence: Getting double pay this year, I'm so happy!

cantonese_sentence: 佢攰到連雙眼簷都擘唔大。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gui6 dou3 lin4 soeng1 ngaan5 jim4 dou1 maak3 m4 daai6.
english_sentence: He's so tired that he can't even open his eyelids properly.

cantonese_sentence: 佢天生就有對又圓又大嘅雙眼皮。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 tin1 sang1 zau6 jau5 deoi3 jau6 jyun4 jau6 daai6 ge3 soeng1 ngaan5 pei4.
english_sentence: She was born with a pair of round and big double eyelids.

english: Double loss, unemployed and lacking direction (often used to describe young people facing economic hardship).
cantonese_sentence: 我而家雙失，唔知點算好。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ji4 ga1 soeng1 sat1, m4 zi1 dim2 syun3 hou2.
english_sentence: I'm unemployed and lost now, I don't know what to do.

cantonese_sentence: 佢幫我單擋，我就可以順利入樽。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 bong1 ngo5 daan1 dong2, ngo5 zau6 ho2 ji5 seon6 lei6 jap6 zyun1.
english_sentence: He screened for me, so I was able to dunk smoothly.

cantonese_sentence: 我哋聽日坐雙體船去長洲。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei62 ting1 jat6 zo6 soeng1 tai2 syun4 heoi3 coeng4 zau1.
english_sentence: We are taking a catamaran to Cheung Chau tomorrow.

cantonese_sentence: 我下個月會用雙程證返大陸探親。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 haa6 go3 jyut6 wui5 yung6 soeng1 cing4 zing3 faan1 daai6 luk6 taam3 can1.
english_sentence: I will use the two-way permit to visit relatives in mainland China next month.

english: People with disabilities (literally: wounded and healthy people)
cantonese_sentence: 我哋應該尊重傷健人士嘅權利。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 ying1 goi1 zyun1 zung6 soeng1 gin6 jan4 si6 ge3 kuen4 lei6.
english_sentence: We should respect the rights of people with disabilities.

cantonese_sentence: 我哋影張相啦！
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 ying2 zoeng1 soeng3 laa1!
english_sentence: Let's take a photo!

cantonese_sentence: 我將啲相擺喺相簿度。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zoeng1 di1 soeng3 baai2 hai2 soeng3 bou6*2 dou6.
english_sentence: I put the photos in the album.

cantonese_sentence: 我將張相擺喺個相架度。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zoeng1 zoeng1 soeng3 baai2 hai2 go3 soeng3 gaa2 dou6.
english_sentence: I put the photo in the photo frame.

cantonese_sentence: 呢張相我影得好相底，唔好擺上網啦！
jyutping_sentence: ni1 zoeng1 soeng3 ngo5 ying2 dak1 hou2 soeng3 dai2, m4 hou2 baai2 soeng5 mong5 laa1!
english_sentence: This photo of me is really unflattering, don't post it online!

english: (I) want to stab your heart (metaphorically, to cause you deep emotional pain)
cantonese_sentence: 你講啲嘢咁難聽，真係想愴你個心！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 gong2 di1 je5 gam3 naan4 ting1, zan1 hai6 soeng2 cong3 nei5 go3 sam1!
english_sentence: You say such awful things, it really makes me want to stab your heart (make you feel really bad)!

english: To want to say; to intend to say; to be about to say
cantonese_sentence: 我哋想話聽日唔返工呀。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 soeng2 waa6 ting1 jat6 m4 faan1 gung1 aa3.
english_sentence: We wanted to say that we aren't coming to work tomorrow.

english: Fortune teller, palm reader, face reader
cantonese_sentence: 我阿媽帶我去搵相士睇相。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 aa3 maa1 daai3 ngo5 heoi3 wan2 soeng3 si6 tai2 soeng3.
english_sentence: My mom took me to find a fortune teller to read my face.

cantonese_sentence: 佢今次單刀赴會，真係好勇敢。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam1 ci3 daan1 dou1 fu6 wui2, zan1 hai6 hou2 yung5 gam2.
english_sentence: He went to the meeting alone this time, he's really brave.

jyutping: soeng5 dak1 saan1 do1 zung1 jyu6 fu2
english: If you go up the mountain often enough, you'll eventually meet a tiger. (Repeated exposure to danger eventually leads to trouble.)
cantonese_sentence: 你成日喺酒吧流連，上得山多終遇虎，小心惹到啲唔好嘅嘢。
jyutping_sentence: nei5 sing4 jat6 hai2 zau2 baa1 lau4 lin4, soeng5 dak1 saan1 do1 zung1 jyu6 fu2, siu2 sam1 je5 dou3 di1 m4 hou2 ge3 je5.
english_sentence: You always hang out in bars, keep tempting fate and be careful you don't get into trouble.

jyutping: soeng5 dak1 cong4 lei4 laai1 bei6 kam2
english: If you get into bed, pull up the covers.
cantonese_sentence: 佢好懶，成日攤喺梳化度，叫佢上得床嚟拉被冚，佢都唔肯。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hou2 laan5, seng4 jat6 taan1 hai2 so1 fa2 dou6, giu3 keoi5 soeng5 dak1 cong4 lei4 laai1 bei6 kam2, keoi5 dou1 m4 hang2.
english_sentence: He's really lazy, always lounging on the sofa, even if you tell him to get into bed and pull up the covers, he still won't.

english: To power on, to turn on (electricity)
cantonese_sentence: 喂，幫我上電個電腦呀。
jyutping_sentence: wai3, bong1 ngo5 soeng5 din6 go3 din6 nou5 aa3.
english_sentence: Hey, help me power on the computer.

english: Take up a position on a student society committee
cantonese_sentence: 今年我哋部門嘅阿明上咗莊
jyutping_sentence: gam1 nin4 ngo5 dei6 bou6 mun4 ge3 aa3 ming4 soeng5 zo2 zong1
english_sentence: This year, our department's Ah Ming has taken up a position on the student society committee.

english: Photogenic; To look good on camera/in photos
cantonese_sentence: 佢好上鏡，影相好靚。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hou2 soeng5 geng3, ying2 soeng2 hou2 leng3.
english_sentence: She is very photogenic, she looks great in photos.

cantonese_sentence: 我哋上契做兄妹啦，以後有咩事互相照應。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 soeng6 kai3 zou6 hing1 mui2 laa1, ji5 hau6 jau5 me1 si6 wu6 soeng1 ziu3 jing3.
english_sentence: Let's become sworn siblings, so we can look after each other from now on.

english: Go upstairs; to go to one's apartment/flat
cantonese_sentence: 我哋上樓飲杯嘢啦
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 soeng5 lau2 jam2 bui1 je5 laa1
english_sentence: Let's go upstairs for a drink.

english: To wind up (a clock, toy, etc.)
cantonese_sentence: 我唔記得幫隻錶上鏈，佢停咗喇。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 gei3 dak1 bong1 zek3 biu1 soeng5 lin2, keoi5 ting4 zo2 laa1.
english_sentence: I forgot to wind up the watch, it stopped.

english: To go up and down; to get on and off (a vehicle)
cantonese_sentence: 巴士站好多人上落。
jyutping_sentence: baa1 si2 zaam6 hou2 do1 jan4 soeng5 lok6.
english_sentence: There are many people getting on and off at the bus stop.

english: To get ashore; to leave a difficult situation (especially gambling or risky ventures)
cantonese_sentence: 我朋友已經上岸，唔再賭錢喇。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 pang4 jau5 ji5 ging1 soeng5 ngon6, m4 zoi3 dou2 cin2 laa1.
english_sentence: My friend has gotten out of gambling, he's no longer gambling.

cantonese_sentence: 佢派咗好多單張。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 paai3 zo2 hou2 do1 daan1 zoeng1.
english_sentence: He/She handed out a lot of flyers.

cantonese_sentence: 我哋成日去樓上舖頭行街。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 sing4 jat6 heoi3 lau4 soeng6 pou3 tau2 haang4 gaai1.
english_sentence: We often go to upstairs shops to browse.

english: To take something to heart; to take something seriously; to care about something.
cantonese_sentence: 你咁講，我會上心㗎。
jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam2 gong2, ngo5 wui5 soeng5 sam1 gaa3.
english_sentence: Since you said that, I'll take it to heart.

english: 1. To possess (by a spirit). 2. To wear (upper garment).
cantonese_sentence: 佢好似俾啲嘢上咗身咁, 行為怪異。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hou2 ci5 bei2 di1 je5 soeng5 zo2 san1 gam2, hang4 wai4 gwaai3 ji6.
english_sentence: It's like he's been possessed, his behavior is strange.

english: To be listed on the stock market, to go public
cantonese_sentence: 我哋公司計劃下年上市。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 gung1 si1 gai3 waak6 haa6 nin4 soeng5 si5.
english_sentence: Our company plans to go public next year.

english: To include (something) in a calculation, to add up to a total. It can also mean "previous amount" depending on context.
cantonese_sentence: 今個月條數上數埋上次爭落嘅錢，都幾多喎！
jyutping_sentence: gam1 go3 jyut6 tiu4 sou3 soeng6 sou3 maai4 soeng6 ci3 zaang1 lok6 ge3 cin2, dou1 gei2 do1 wo3!
english_sentence: Including the money owed from last time, this month's bill adds up to quite a lot!

english: To attend class; to go to class
cantonese_sentence: 我聽日要上堂呀。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ting1 jat6 jiu3 soeng5 tong4 aa3.
english_sentence: I have to go to class tomorrow.

english: To get on a vehicle (bus, car, train, etc.)
cantonese_sentence: 我哋快啲上車啦，就嚟遲到喇！
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 faai3 di1 soeng5 ce1 laa1, zau6 lai4 ci4 dou3 laa3!
english_sentence: Let's get on the vehicle quickly, we're going to be late!

english: To pass away; to die (euphemistic, literally "to go to the warehouse")
cantonese_sentence: 佢阿爺尋日上咗倉。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 aa3 je4 cam4 jat6 soeng5 zo2 cong1.
english_sentence: His grandfather passed away yesterday.

english: to go to bed, to sleep; (euphemistically) to have sex
cantonese_sentence: 我好眼瞓，想即刻上床瞓覺。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hou2 ngaan5 fan3, soeng2 zik1 hak1 soeng5 cong4 fan3 gaau3.
english_sentence: I'm very sleepy, I want to go to bed and sleep right away.

english: To be released in cinemas; to premiere
cantonese_sentence: 呢套戲幾時上畫呀？
jyutping_sentence: ni1 tou3 hei3 gei2 si4 soeng5 waa2 aa3?
english_sentence: When is this movie being released?

cantonese_sentence: 單係你咁講，我都唔會信。
jyutping_sentence: daan1 hai6 nei5 gam2 gong2, ngo5 dou1 m4 wui5 seon3.
english_sentence: Just because you say so, I won't believe it.

english: To get promoted; to climb the social ladder; to rise in status/position.
cantonese_sentence: 佢想盡辦法上位。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 soeng2 zeon6 baan6 faat3 soeng5 wai2.
english_sentence: He/She is trying every possible way to get promoted.

english: Mortgage/Finance (usually referring to car or property financing)
cantonese_sentence: 我諗住買車，要上會。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 lam2 zyu6 maai5 ce1, jiu3 soeng5 wui2.
english_sentence: I'm thinking of buying a car, I need to get a loan/finance it.

cantonese_sentence: 本書喺檯上便。
jyutping_sentence: bun2 syu1 hai2 toi2 soeng6 bin6.
english_sentence: The book is on the table.

cantonese_sentence: 我上晝要去銀行處理啲嘢。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 soeng6 zau3 jiu3 heoi3 ngan4 hong4 cyu5 lei5 di1 je5.
english_sentence: I need to go to the bank to handle some things in the morning.

cantonese_sentence: 嘢放喺上高喇。

jyutping_sentence: a3 po4 seng4 jat6 hai2 dou6 sou2 wun2 sou3 dip2, zan1 hai6 hou2 faan4!
english_sentence: Grandma is always here counting the bowls and plates, it's really annoying!

cantonese_sentence: 我聽日要掃地。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ting1 jat6 jiu3 sou3 dei6.
english_sentence: I need to sweep the floor tomorrow.

cantonese_sentence: 我唔識得點樣數錢
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 sik1 dak1 dim2 joeng2 sou3 cin2
english_sentence: I don't know how to count money.

cantonese_sentence: 佢日日都睇佢本數簿。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat6 jat6 dou1 tai2 keoi5 bun2 sou3 bou2.
english_sentence: He/She looks at his/her account book every day.

cantonese_sentence: 佢數口好精，好識得做生意。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sou3 hau2 hou2 zing1, hou2 sik1 dak1 zou6 sang1 ji3.
english_sentence: He has good business acumen and knows how to run a business.

english: Last few; End of the line

jyutping_sentence: ngo5 paai4 deoi2 paai4 dou3 sou3 mei1, m4 zi1 zung1 jau5 mou5 fei1 maai6.
english_sentence: I'm at the end of the line, I don't know if there are any tickets left.

jyutping: sou3 waan4 sou3 lou6 waan4 lou6

cantonese_sentence: 我哋係朋友嚟㗎，數還數路還路，唔好搞亂。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 hai6 pang4 jau5 lei4 gaa3, sou3 waan4 sou3 lou6 waan4 lou6, m4 hou2 gaau2 lyun6.

cantonese_sentence: 我哋要準備充足嘅彈藥先可以打贏場仗。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 jiu3 zeon2 bei6 zuk1 cung1 ge3 daan6 joek6 sin1 ho2 ji5 daa2 jeng4 coeng4 zoeng3.
english_sentence: We need to prepare enough ammunition to win the battle.

cantonese_sentence: 我用掃把掃地。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 jung6 sou3 baa2 sou3 dei6.
english_sentence: I use a broom to sweep the floor.

cantonese_sentence: 佢真係掃把星，去到邊度都冇好事發生。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zan1 hai6 sou3 baa2 sing1, heoi3 dou3 bin1 dou6 dou1 mou5 hou2 si6 faat1 sang1.
english_sentence: He's really a jinx, nothing good ever happens wherever he goes.

english: To go on a shopping spree/buy a lot of something (often sale items).
cantonese_sentence: 我哋聽日去掃貨！
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 ting1 jat6 heoi3 sou3 fo3!
english_sentence: Let's go on a shopping spree tomorrow!

cantonese_sentence: 過時過節我哋都會掃灰水㗎。
jyutping_sentence: gwo3 si4 gwo3 zit3 ngo5 dei6 dou1 wui5 sou3 fui1 seoi2 gaa3.
english_sentence: During holidays, we always apply whitewash.

english: To wander the streets eating street food.
cantonese_sentence: 今晚想去旺角掃街。
jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 soeng2 heoi3 wong6 gok3 sou3 gaai1.
english_sentence: Tonight I want to go to Mong Kok to eat street food.

english: To sweep the floor (literally), but more often used figuratively to mean "to dominate," "to sweep the competition," "to win big" or "to clean house."
cantonese_sentence: 佢哋喺比賽入面掃晒全場嘅獎！
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 hai2 bei2 coi3 jap6 min6 sou3 saai3 cyun4 coeng4 ge3 zoeng2!
english_sentence: They swept all the awards in the competition!

cantonese_sentence: 你數下有幾多錢？
jyutping_sentence: nei5 sou3 haa5 jau5 gei2 do1 cin2?
english_sentence: Can you count how much money there is?

cantonese_sentence: 我老公嘅叔仔好後生。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 lou5 gung1 ge3 suk1 zai2 hou2 hau6 saang1.
english_sentence: My husband's younger brother is very young.

cantonese_sentence: 聽日我哋去同叔公拜年。
jyutping_sentence: ting1 jat6 ngo5 dei6 heoi3 tung4 suk1 gung1 baai3 nin4.
english_sentence: Tomorrow we're going to wish our great-uncle a happy new year.

cantonese_sentence: 我聽日去叔婆屋企拜年。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ting1 jat6 heoi3 suk1 po4 uk1 kei2 baai3 nin4.
english_sentence: I'm going to my auntie's (father's uncle's wife) house to do Chinese New Year visiting tomorrow.

cantonese_sentence: 我細個嗰陣時成日飲阿嫲沖嘅蛋茶。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 sai3 go3 go2 zan6 si4 seng4 jat6 jam2 aa3 po4 cung1 ge3 daan6 caa4.
english_sentence: When I was little, I often drank the egg tea that my grandma made.

cantonese_sentence: 今晚我會喺你度宿一宵。
jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 ngo5 wui5 hai2 nei5 dou6 suk1 jat1 siu1.
english_sentence: Tonight I will stay overnight at your place.

english: Loser; Someone who stays at home and contributes little; Incel (though the negative connotations are stronger in the "incel" translation)
cantonese_sentence: 佢成日匿喺屋企打機，真係一個宿包。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 nik1 hai2 uk1 kei2 daa2 gei1, zan1 hai6 jat1 go3 suk1 baau1.
english_sentence: He always hides at home playing video games, he's really a loser.

english: Neat and tidy; very orderly. Often refers to things being meticulously arranged or cleaned.
cantonese_sentence: 佢間房執到宿堪堪
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gaan1 fong2 zap1 dou3 suk1 ham3 ham3
english_sentence: Her room is cleaned up very neatly.

english: Bed space (especially in a dormitory or boarding facility)
cantonese_sentence: 我想申請學校嘅宿位。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 soeng2 san1 ching2 hok6 haau6 ge3 suk1 wai2.
english_sentence: I want to apply for a bed space in the school dormitory.

english: To shrug (shoulders), to shrink back, to be avoidant (figuratively)
cantonese_sentence: 佢成日遇到困難就縮膊，好冇承擔！
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 jyu6 dou3 kwan3 naan4 zau6 suk1 bok3, hou2 mou5 sing4 daam1!
english_sentence: He always shrugs off (avoids) difficulties when he encounters them, he's very irresponsible!

cantonese_sentence: 佢份人好縮骨㗎，一毫子都唔捨得使。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 fan6 jan4 hou2 suk1 gwat1 gaa3, jat1 hou4 zi2 dou1 m4 se2 dak1 sai2.
english_sentence: He's a very stingy person, he doesn't even want to spend a dime.

cantonese_sentence: 我把縮骨遮唔見咗，聽日落雨就麻煩啦。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 baa2 suk1 gwat1 ze1 m4 gin3 zo2, ting1 jat6 lok6 jyu5 zau6 maa4 faan4 laa1.
english_sentence: I lost my folding umbrella, it'll be troublesome if it rains tomorrow.

cantonese_sentence: 你縮開啲啦，咁逼嘅！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 suk1 hoi1 di1 laa1, gam3 bik1 ge3!
english_sentence: Move over a bit, it's so cramped!

english: Cuddled up together (often implying small, huddled, and sometimes in a frightened or uncomfortable way)
cantonese_sentence: 佢哋凍到縮埋一嚿喺個角落頭。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 dung3 dou3 suk1 maai4 jat1 gau6 hai2 go3 gok3 lok6 tau4.
english_sentence: They were so cold they huddled together in the corner.

cantonese_sentence: 佢一路都縮埋一二角，唔敢出聲。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat1 lou6 dou1 suk1 maai4 jat1 ji6 gok3, m4 gam2 cheut1 seng1.
english_sentence: He was huddled in a corner the whole time, not daring to speak.

cantonese_sentence: 我好鍾意食蛋卷。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hou2 zung1 ji3 sik6 daan6 gyun2.
english_sentence: I really like to eat egg rolls.

english: Stingy; to become cheap or stingy. Also, to chicken out.
cantonese_sentence: 佢真係好縮皮，請食飯都唔捨得叫多個餸。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zan1 hai6 hou2 suk1 pei4, cheng2 sik6 faan6 dou1 m4 se2 dak1 giu3 do1 go3 sung3.
english_sentence: He's really stingy; he's unwilling to order an extra dish even when treating someone to a meal.

english: to chicken out, to back down (from fear or pressure)
cantonese_sentence: 佢一見到差佬就縮沙嘞。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat1 gin3 dou3 caai1 lou2 zau6 suk1 saa1 laak3.
english_sentence: He chickened out as soon as he saw the police.

jyutping_sentence: gin6 saam1 sai2 jyun4 suk1 zo2 seoi2.

english: Shrinking apartment (refers to newly built apartments that are smaller than advertised, often due to inflated floor space measurements or shared spaces)

jyutping_sentence: ni1 di1 suk1 seoi2 lau2 zan1 hai6 hou2 m4 dai2 maai5.
english_sentence: These shrinking apartments are really not worth buying.

english_sentence: These mangoes are very ripe.

english_sentence: I bought some cooked food from the supermarket to eat at home.

english: Regular/trusted vendor or shop; familiar place of business.

jyutping_sentence: ngo5 sing4 jat6 hai2 go2 gaan1 suk6 dong3 maai5 je5.

cantonese_sentence: 佢喺呢行好熟行㗎。

cantonese_sentence: 我哋熟落咗之後，成日一齊去飲嘢。

english_sentence: We're very familiar with each other, we often go for drinks together.

jyutping_sentence: ngo5 bok3 tau4 hou2 ngaang6, soeng2 heoi3 sung1 haa5 gwat1.

cantonese_sentence: 我今日食咗兩個蛋筒。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 jat6 sik6 zo2 loeng5 go3 daan6 tung2.

english: To leave, to scram, to take off (often implying a quick or secretive departure)
cantonese_sentence: 聽日考試，我哋要早啲鬆人，返去溫書。

english: A hazy, unfocused, or unclear state, often used to describe a feeling of being out of it or not thinking clearly.

english_sentence: Her poodle is very clingy.

english: To be eager, restless, and excited (often in a mischievous way)
cantonese_sentence: 細路仔聽日去旅行，成晚鬆毛鬆翼瞓唔著。

english_sentence: The kid is going on a trip tomorrow, and he was so excited and restless all night that he couldn't sleep.

english: Fluffy (often describes texture of bread, cake, or cotton)
cantonese_sentence: 呢個蛋糕好鬆婄呀!
jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 daan6 gou1 hou2 sung1 pou2 aa3!
english_sentence: This cake is very fluffy!

cantonese_sentence: 1. Jyutping: sung1 lung1 lung1 (鬆容容)
jyutping_sentence: 2. Brief English meaning: Very loose, very relaxed (often used to describe overly loose-fitting clothes). Can also be used to describe someone who is too lenient or doesn't take things seriously enough.

english: to give (as a gift), to send, to see off
cantonese_sentence: 我送你返屋企啦。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 sung3 nei5 faan1 uk1 kei2 laa1.
english_sentence: I'll see you home.

cantonese_sentence: 我哋要將啲食物送檢睇下係咪安全。

cantonese_sentence: 我買咗啲送口果去探阿婆。

cantonese_sentence: 今晚煮咗咩餸呀？

english: Tanka people (a historically boat-dwelling ethnic group in Southern China)
cantonese_sentence: 佢哋祖先係蜑家人。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 zou2 sin1 hai6 daan6 gaa1 jan4.
english_sentence: Their ancestors were Tanka people.

cantonese_sentence: 今日飲茶啲鱅魚好新鮮啊！
jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 jam2 caa4 di1 jung4 jyu2 hou2 san1 sin1 aa3!
english_sentence: The bighead carp served at dim sum today is very fresh!

cantonese_sentence: 我哋公司嘅書記好幫得手㗎。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 gung1 si1 ge3 syu1 gei3 hou2 bong1 dak1 sau2 gaa3.
english_sentence: Our company's clerk is very helpful.

cantonese_sentence: 我成日去圖書館借書。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 sing4 jat6 heoi3 tou4 syu1 gun2 ze3 syu1.
english_sentence: I often go to the library to borrow books.

cantonese_sentence: 我同啲書友成日喺圖書館見面。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 tung4 di1 syu1 jau5 sing4 jat6 hai2 tou4 syu1 gun2 gin3 min6.
english_sentence: I often meet with my book-loving friends at the library.

english: Academy; College (often refers to older, traditional institutions or halls of learning, but can also refer to some modern institutions)
cantonese_sentence: 我哋以前嘅書院喺山上。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 ji5 cin4 ge3 syu1 jyun2 hai2 saan1 soeng6.

cantonese_sentence: 我喺書枱度做功課。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hai2 syu1 toi2 dou6 zou6 gung1 fo3.
english_sentence: I am doing homework at the desk.

cantonese_sentence: 佢細個嘅時候已經係個書蟲。

english: Be careful; Watch out (doing something); Proceed with caution

jyutping_sentence: nei5 ge3 tai2 faat3 hai6 dim2 aa3?

english: To watch the stove (especially while cooking), to tend the fire.

english: To work a shift (security, caregiving, etc.), to watch over a place.

english: To think highly of; to look up to; to value

jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hou2 tai2 hei2 keoi5 ge3 gung1 zok3 nang4 lik6.

english: To be optimistic about, to favor, to think highly of
cantonese_sentence: 我睇好佢今次考試會攞A
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 tai2 hou2 keoi5 gam1 ci3 haau2 si5 wui5 lo2 ei1

jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 syu1 fuk6, yiu3 tai2 yi1 sang1.
english_sentence: I'm not feeling well, I need to see a doctor.

english: To view a property for sale or rent; to go apartment hunting

jyutping_sentence: keoi5 tai2 lok6 hou2 ci5 hou2 hoi1 sam1 gam2.
english_sentence: He/She looks like he/she is very happy.

english: Can't stand to look at; can't bear to see; find something awful/unacceptable
cantonese_sentence: 佢份人咁衰格，我睇唔過眼。

english_sentence: He's such a jerk, I can't stand him/I can't bear to see how he acts.

english_sentence: I've taken a liking to that bag./ I've got my eye on that bag.

english: Keep a close eye on, watch carefully

jyutping_sentence: nei5 bong1 ngo5 tai2 sat6 go3 doi2 aa3
english_sentence: Can you help me keep a close eye on the bag?

english: Keep a close watch on, keep an eye on, supervise
cantonese_sentence: 你睇實啲細路，唔好俾佢哋周圍走。
jyutping_sentence: nei5 tai2 sat6 di1 sai3 lou6, m4 ho2 bei2 keoi5 dei6 zau1 wai4 zau2.
english_sentence: Keep a close watch on the kids, don't let them run around everywhere.

english_sentence: I want to go fortune-telling tomorrow.

english_sentence: Keep watch for us, if someone comes, let us know.

english: To review/check the accounts; to do bookkeeping

jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam1 maan5 jiu3 hai2 uk1 kei2 tai2 sou3.

english: To cook according to what ingredients are available; To make do with what you have; To live within one's means.

jyutping_sentence: ngo5 tai2 daam6 gam1 nin4 lau4 si5.
english_sentence: I am bearish on the property market this year.

english: Something to look forward to; prospects; impressive; potential. Can refer to appearance, future prospects, or general quality.

jyutping_sentence: keoi5 fan6 jan4 gei2 jau5 tai2 tau4 gaa3.
english_sentence: He/She has a lot of potential/promise.

english_sentence: The children are playing ring game in the park.

cantonese_sentence: 佢輸晒啲錢，諗住吞槍自殺。

english_sentence: Be careful, when reversing, be sure to look clearly behind you.

english: To help; to lend a hand
cantonese_sentence: 佢哋一齊搭手整好咗個櫃。

english_sentence: They worked together to fix the cabinet.

english: To be overly generous; excessively giving; foolishly generous. (Implies someone is being taken advantage of.)

english: To get something done, to finish a task, to sort out a problem.

cantonese_sentence: 我哋要斬柴嚟煮飯。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 jiu3 zaam2 caai4 lai4 zyu2 faan6.
english_sentence: We need to chop firewood to cook rice.

english: Driver (often used to describe someone who drives others around a lot)
cantonese_sentence: 你又做埋柴可夫，車晒佢哋去飲嘢。
jyutping_sentence: nei5 jau6 zou6 maai4 caai4 ho2 fu1, ce1 saai3 keoi5 dei6 heoi3 jam2 je5.
english_sentence: You're being a driver again, driving them all to have drinks.

english: To create a negative or awkward atmosphere, often by saying something inappropriate or making an unhelpful comment that dampens the mood. It can also refer to making a joke that falls flat. Think "killing the vibe" or being a "buzzkill."
cantonese_sentence: 你唔好再柴台啦，講啲開心嘢吖！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zoi3 caai4 toi2 laa1, gong2 di1 hoi1 sam1 je5 aa1!
english_sentence: Please stop killing the vibe, say something cheerful!

english: Touch Base Policy (in immigration contexts, a policy where illegal immigrants who make it past a certain point or stay for a certain period are allowed to remain)
cantonese_sentence: 以前嘅抵壘政策令到好多人湧入香港。
jyutping_sentence: ji5 cin4 ge3 dai2 leoi5 zing3 caak3 ling6 dou3 hou2 do1 jan4 jung2 jap6 hoeng1 gong2.
english_sentence: The Touch Base Policy in the past caused many people to flood into Hong Kong.

english: Messy; unorganized; untidy (often referring to hair or a cluttered room)
cantonese_sentence: 你間房好柴哇哇，執執佢啦！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 gaan1 fong2 hou2 caai4 waa1 waa1, zap1 zap1 keoi5 laa1!
english_sentence: Your room is so messy, tidy it up!

cantonese_sentence: 我哋請咗個測量師嚟幫我哋度間屋嘅尺寸。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 ceng2 zo2 go3 cak1 loeng4 si1 lai4 bong1 ngo5 dei6 dok6 gaan1 uk1 ge3 cek3 cyun3.
english_sentence: We hired a surveyor to help us measure the dimensions of the house.

cantonese_sentence: 個牆身開始坼喇。
jyutping_sentence: go3 coeng4 san1 hoi1 ci2 caak3 laa3.
english_sentence: The wall is starting to crack.

cantonese_sentence: 佢哋準備拆咗間舊屋。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 zeon2 bei6 caak3 zo2 gaan1 gau6 uk1.
english_sentence: They are preparing to tear down the old house.

english: To close a business; to break up (a partnership).
cantonese_sentence: 佢哋生意唔好，所以決定拆檔。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 saang1 ji3 m4 hou2, so2 ji5 kyut3 ding6 caak3 dong3.
english_sentence: Their business wasn't doing well, so they decided to close it/break up the partnership.

english: To ruin one's reputation; to lose credibility; to close down (a business)
cantonese_sentence: 佢間公司做埋啲咁嘅嘢，遲早都要拆招牌。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gaan1 gung1 si1 zou6 maai4 di1 gam3 ge3 je5, ci4 zou2 dou1 jiu3 caak3 ziu1 paai4.
english_sentence: His company is doing things like that, sooner or later they will ruin their reputation (or be forced to close down).

english: To sabotage a relationship, to break up a couple, to "steal" someone's partner.
cantonese_sentence: 佢專登拆人哋嘅家，真係好冇品.
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zyun1 dang3 caak3 jan4 dei6 ge3 gaa1, zan1 hai6 hou2 mou5 ban2.
english_sentence: He deliberately breaks up other people's relationships, he's really bad.

cantonese_sentence: 阿媽好叻拆骨，啲雞好快就食得
jyutping_sentence: aa3 maa1 hou2 lek1 caak3 gwat1, di1 gai1 hou2 faai3 zau6 sik6 dak1
english_sentence: My mom is very good at deboning, the chicken can be eaten very quickly.

english: To debone (meat) / To remove the bones from (meat)
cantonese_sentence: 阿媽成日買雞返屋企拆肉煲湯
jyutping_sentence: aa3 maa1 seng4 jat6 maai5 gai1 faan1 uk1 kei2 caak3 juk6 bou1 tong1
english_sentence: My mom often buys chicken and brings it home to debone it for soup.

english: I'll tear down your house! (figuratively means "I'll destroy you" or "I'll mess you up")
cantonese_sentence: 你再嘈我拆你屋呀！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 zoi3 cou4 ngo5 caak3 nei5 uk1 aa3!
english_sentence: If you keep making noise, I'll mess you up!

english: Worth considering, reasonable, a good deal
cantonese_sentence: 呢個方法都幾抵諗㗎，不如試下？
jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 fong1 faat3 dou1 gei2 dai2 nam2 gaa3, bat1 jyu4 si3 haa5?
english_sentence: This method is quite worth considering, why don't we give it a try?

english: Interbank offered rate (HIBOR, specifically the cost for banks to borrow short-term funds from each other)
cantonese_sentence: 最近嘅拆息升得好快，好多人都擔心會影響到樓價。
jyutping_sentence: zeoi3 gan6 ge3 caak3 sik1 sing1 dak1 hou2 faai3, hou2 do1 jan4 dou1 daam1 sam1 wui5 ying2 heong2 dou3 lau4 gaa3.
english_sentence: Recently, the interbank offered rate has been rising very quickly, and many people are worried that it will affect property prices.

cantonese_sentence: 佢衰到要拆祠堂咁滯
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seoi1 dou3 jiu3 caak3 ci4 tong4 gam3 zai6
english_sentence: He's so awful, it's as if he's going to demolish the ancestral hall. (Implying he's done something extremely shameful and disgraceful.)

cantonese_sentence: 佢好鍾意策騎，每個星期都去馬場
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hou2 zung1 ji3 caak3 ke4, mui5 go3 sing1 kei4 dou1 heoi3 maa5 coeng4
english_sentence: He/She likes horse riding a lot and goes to the racecourse every week.

english: Thief father; used as an insult to suggest someone's father is a thief or of bad character. A harsher insult than just calling someone a thief.
cantonese_sentence: 你咁衰嘅，真係賊阿爸！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam3 seoi1 ge3, zan1 hai6 caak6 aa3 baa1!
english_sentence: You're so awful, you're really a thief-father! (Implying a lineage of bad character)

cantonese_sentence: 個賊仔偷咗我個銀包
jyutping_sentence: go3 caak6 zai2 tau1 zo2 ngo5 go3 ngan2 baau1
english_sentence: That little thief stole my wallet.

cantonese_sentence: 佢哋俾差人喺佢屋企搜到好多賊贓。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 bei2 caa1 jan4 hai2 keoi5 uk1 kei2 sau1 dou2 ho2 do1 caak6 zong1.
english_sentence: The police found a lot of stolen goods in their house.

cantonese_sentence: 個賊公偷咗我部電話。
jyutping_sentence: go3 caak6 gung1 tau1 zo2 ngo5 bou6 din6 waa2.
english_sentence: That thief stole my phone.

cantonese_sentence: 個賊佬喺條巷仔度搶嘢。
jyutping_sentence: go3 caak6 lou2 hai2 tiu4 hong2 zai2 dou6 coeng2 je5.
english_sentence: The thief robbed someone in the alley.

english: A thief testing a clay pot. (Meaning someone who is testing something out with the intention of stealing/damaging/taking advantage of it later.)
cantonese_sentence: 佢成日走嚟問呢樣問嗰樣，擺明賊佬試沙煲啦！
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 zau2 lei4 man6 ni1 joeng2 man6 go2 joeng2, baai2 ming4 caak6 lou2 si3 saa1 bou1 laa1!
english_sentence: He always comes over asking about this and that, it's obvious he's just scoping things out to take advantage later!

cantonese_sentence: 我哋不如返去同屋企人參詳吓先啦。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 bat1 jyu4 faan1 heoi3 tung4 uk1 kei2 jan4 caam1 soeng4 haa5 sin1 laa1.
english_sentence: How about we go back and discuss it with our family first?

english: Cannot resist, cannot help but argue back, can't help but talk back, can't help but contradict.
cantonese_sentence: 佢忍唔住抵唔住頸，同阿媽嘈咗幾句。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jan2 m4 zyu6 dai2 m4 zyu6 geng2, tung4 a3 maa1 caau2 zo2 gei2 geoi3.
english_sentence: He couldn't help but argue back, and had a few arguments with his mom.

cantonese_sentence: 考試唔合格，真係好慘呀！
jyutping_sentence: haau2 si3 m4 gok3 gaak3, zan1 hai6 hou2 caam2 aa3!
english_sentence: Failing the exam is really awful!

english: Green youth; inexperienced, naive young man, often with romantic yearnings
cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺度扮慘綠少年，諗住氹啲女仔。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 hai2 dou6 baan6 caam2 luk6 siu3 nin4, nam2 zyu6 tam5 di1 neoi5 zai2.
english_sentence: He's always pretending to be a naive young man, hoping to trick some girls.

english: Melodramatic; overly sentimental; tragic (in a romantic or emotional way)
cantonese_sentence: 套戲嘅結局真係好慘情，睇到我眼濕濕。
jyutping_sentence: tou3 hei3 ge3 git3 guk6 zan1 hai6 hou2 caam2 cing4, tai2 dou3 ngo5 ngaan5 sap1 sap1.
english_sentence: The ending of that movie was really melodramatic, it made me teary-eyed.

cantonese_sentence: 佢頭上插住支銀篸。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 tau4 soeng6 caap3 zyu6 zi1 ngan4 caam1.
english_sentence: She has a silver hairpin in her hair.

cantonese_sentence: 呢度有好多杉樹。
jyutping_sentence: ni1 dou6 jau5 hou2 do1 saam1 syu6.
english_sentence: There are a lot of fir trees here.

cantonese_sentence: 我細個養過蠶蟲。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 sai3 go3 joeng5 gwo3 caam4 cung4.
english_sentence: I raised silkworms when I was little.

english: A sycophant, a brown-noser, someone who is obsequious and excessively flattering to superiors, often for personal gain. (Literally "silkworm advisor/master")
cantonese_sentence: 唔好做埋啲蠺蟲師爺嘅嘢啦，咁樣好肉酸㗎。
jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 zou6 maai4 di1 caam4 cung4 si1 je2 ge3 je5 laa1, gam2 joeng2 hou2 juk6 saan1 gaa3.
english_sentence: Don't act like such a brown-noser, it's so embarrassing.

cantonese_sentence: 佢拎把刀去㔆
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ling1 baa2 dou1 heoi3 dim2
english_sentence: He took the knife to be sharpened.

cantonese_sentence: 我哋出去食餐飯啦。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 ceot1 heoi3 sik6 caan1 faan6 laa1.
english_sentence: Let's go out for a meal.

cantonese_sentence: 我想睇吓個餐單。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 soeng2 tai2 haa5 go3 caan1 daan1.
english_sentence: I want to see the menu.

english: Good value for money; Worth it
cantonese_sentence: 呢個價錢幾抵手㗎。
jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 gaa3 cin2 gei2 dai2 sau2 gaa3.
english_sentence: This price is quite a good deal/worth it.

cantonese_sentence: 我哋間公司做餐飲嘅。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 gaan1 gung1 si1 zou6 caan1 jam2 ge3.
english_sentence: Our company is in the catering business.

cantonese_sentence: 俾份餐牌我睇下。
jyutping_sentence: bei2 fan6 caan1 paai4 ngo5 tai2 haa5.
english_sentence: Give me the menu to have a look.

cantonese_sentence: 我哋去餐室食晏晝茶啦。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 heoi3 caan1 sat1 sik6 aan3 zau3 caa4 laa1.
english_sentence: Let's go to the cafe for afternoon tea.

jyutping: caan1 wan2 caan1 sik6 -- caan1 caan1 cing1
english: Live hand-to-mouth / Live from paycheck to paycheck (literally: earn meal eat meal - every meal clear)
cantonese_sentence: 佢份人工唔高，餐搵餐食——餐餐清，根本儲唔到錢。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 fan6 jan4 gung1 m4 gou1, caan1 wan2 caan1 sik6 -- caan1 caan1 cing1, gan1 bun2 cou5 m4 dou2 cin2.
english_sentence: His salary isn't high, he lives hand-to-mouth, and basically can't save any money.

english: to shave, to scrape off, to bulldoze
cantonese_sentence: 佢剷咗個頭。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 caan2 zo2 go3 tau4.
english_sentence: He shaved his head.

cantonese_sentence: 架剷泥車喺度剷緊啲泥。
jyutping_sentence: gaa3 caan2 nai4 ce1 hai2 dou6 caan2 gan2 di1 nai4.
english_sentence: The bulldozer is bulldozing the dirt.

english: A bright and cheerful girl; often used affectionately or playfully, especially for a young or youthful woman.
cantonese_sentence: 佢個女好似個燦妹咁，成日笑咪咪。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 go3 neoi5 hou2 ci5 go3 caan3 mui2 gam2, seng4 jat6 siu3 mi1 mi1.
english_sentence: Her daughter is like a bright and cheerful girl, always smiling.

cantonese_sentence: 張枱好殘。
jyutping_sentence: zoeng1 toi2 hou2 caan4.
english_sentence: This table is very broken down/damaged.

cantonese_sentence: 地上執到好多玻璃殘片。
jyutping_sentence: dei6 soeng6 zap1 dou2 hou2 do1 bo1 lei1 caan4 pin3.
english_sentence: I picked up a lot of glass fragments from the floor.

cantonese_sentence: 攞個罉嚟煮嘢食。
jyutping_sentence: lo2 go3 caang1 lai4 zyu2 je5 sik6.
english_sentence: Get a pot to cook something to eat.

english: Deserving of death/Serves you right/That's what you get. Often used playfully or sarcastically.
cantonese_sentence: 你成日唔聽人講，抵死啦!
jyutping_sentence: nei5 seng4 jat6 m4 ting1 jan4 gong2, dai2 sei2 laa1!
english_sentence: You never listen to people, serves you right!

cantonese_sentence: 佢喺碼頭撐艇出海。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 maa5 tau4 caang1 teng5 ceot1 hoi2.
english_sentence: He rows a boat out to sea from the pier.

cantonese_sentence: 𥋇吓豉油食
jyutping_sentence: dim1 haa5 si6 jau4 sik6
english_sentence: Dip it in soy sauce to eat.

cantonese_sentence: 我撐你呀！
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 caang1 nei5 aa3!
english_sentence: I support you!

english: To freeload, sponge off someone, live off someone else's expense, eat for free (often implying frequently and shamelessly).
cantonese_sentence: 我成日去佢屋企**撐抬腳**。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 seng4 jat6 heoi3 keoi5 uk1 kei2 **caang1 toi4 goek3**.
english_sentence: I often go to his/her house to freeload/sponge off him/her.

english: To support a person or event by being present; to show face
cantonese_sentence: 我哋今晚會去撐場㗎！
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei62 gam1 maan5 wui5 heoi3 caang1 coeng4 gaa3!
english_sentence: We'll go and show our support tonight!

cantonese_sentence: 佢個人咁鋹雞，點會夠膽去跳降落傘啊？
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 go3 jan4 gam3 caan2 gai1, dim2 wui5 gau3 daam2 heoi3 tiu3 gong3 lok6 saan3 aa3?
english_sentence: He's such a sissy, how would he dare to go skydiving?

cantonese_sentence: 佢講嘢嘅姿態好似鋹雞婆咁。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2 je5 ge3 zi1 taai3 hou2 ci5 caan2 gai1 po4*2 gam2.
english_sentence: The way he speaks is like an effeminate man.

english: To open one's eyes wide (often in surprise or astonishment)
cantonese_sentence: 佢聽到個消息，振眼望住我。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ting1 dou2 go3 siu1 sik1, zan3 ngaan5 mong6 zyu6 ngo5.
english_sentence: When he heard the news, he stared at me with wide eyes.

cantonese_sentence: 插支花喺個花樽度
jyutping_sentence: caap3 zi1 faa1 hai2 go3 faa1 zeon1 dou6
english_sentence: Stick a flower in the vase

english: To interrupt; to butt in; to chime in
cantonese_sentence: 佢哋傾緊偈，你唔好插把嘴啦！
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 king1 gan2 gai2, nei5 m4 hou2 chaap3 baa2 zeoi2 laa1!
english_sentence: They are chatting, don't interrupt!

english: Cheap and good (value for money), large portion
cantonese_sentence: 間餐廳啲嘢抵食夾大件，好多人排隊㗎。
jyutping_sentence: gaan1 caan1 teng1 di1 je5 dai2 sik6 gaap3 daai6 gin6, hou2 do1 jan4 paai4 deoi2 gaa3.
english_sentence: The food in that restaurant is cheap and good and the portions are large, so a lot of people are queuing.

english: To dive; to embellish a foul/flop (in sports, especially football)
cantonese_sentence: 佢又插水扮俾人踢跌，想博十二碼！
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jau6 caap3 seoi2 baan6 bei2 jan4 tek3 dit3, soeng2 bok3 sap6 ji6 maa5!
english_sentence: He's faking a foul again, pretending to be tripped, trying to get a penalty!

cantonese_sentence: 我差啲唔記得咗插蘇
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 caa1 di1 m4 gei3 dak1 zo2 caap3 sou1
english_sentence: I almost forgot to plug it in.

cantonese_sentence: 佢用毛巾擦乾淨張枱
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jung6 mou4 gan1 caat3 gon1 zing6 zoeng1 toi2
english_sentence: He/She used a towel to wipe the table clean.

cantonese_sentence: 借你個擦紙膠用吓得唔得呀？
jyutping_sentence: je3 nei5 go3 caat3 zi2 gaau1 yung6 haa5 dak1 m4 dak1 aa3?
english_sentence: Can I borrow your eraser for a moment?

cantonese_sentence: 佢好鍾意擦老細鞋
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hou2 zung1 ji3 caat3 lou5 sai3 haai4
english_sentence: He really likes to brown-nose the boss.

cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺老細面前擦鞋
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 hai2 lou5 sai3 min6 cin4 caat3 haai4
english_sentence: He is always bootlicking in front of the boss.

english: To copy an idea/plan; to plagiarize
cantonese_sentence: 唔好抄人哋啲橋啦，自己諗下啦！
jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 caau1 jan4 dei6 di1 kiu2 laa1, zi6 gei2 lam2 haa5 laa1!
english_sentence: Don't copy other people's ideas, think for yourself!

english: To issue a parking ticket; to write down a license plate number (typically for a traffic violation)
cantonese_sentence: 差人抄牌呀！
jyutping_sentence: caa1 jan4 caau1 paai4 aa3!
english_sentence: The police are giving out parking tickets!

cantonese_sentence: 我今晚想炒飯。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 maan1 soeng2 caau2 faan6.
english_sentence: I want to stir-fry rice tonight.

cantonese_sentence: 我想食碟乾炒牛河。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 soeng2 sik6 dip6 gon1 caau2 ngau4 ho2.
english_sentence: I want to eat a plate of dry-fried beef noodles.

cantonese_sentence: 個盒嘅底爛咗。
jyutping_sentence: go3 hap6 ge3 dai2 laan6 zo2.
english_sentence: The bottom of the box is broken.

english: Speculator (often in the context of property or stocks)
cantonese_sentence: 佢係一個出名嘅炒家。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 jat1 go3 ceot1 ming4 ge3 caau2 gaa1.
english_sentence: He is a famous speculator.

english: To be messy and unorganized (literally: fry shrimp and tear crab)
cantonese_sentence: 佢份人成日都炒蝦拆蟹，啲嘢亂晒籠。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 fan6 jan4 seng4 jat6 dou1 caau2 haa1 caak3 haai5, di1 je5 lyun6晒籠。
english_sentence: He is a messy person, his things are always in a jumble.

cantonese_sentence: 佢俾老細炒魷魚喇
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 bei2 lou5 sai3 caau2 jau4 jyu2 laa3
english_sentence: He got fired by the boss.

english: Rummaging up old news; rehashing old ideas; beating a dead horse
cantonese_sentence: 你唔好成日炒冷飯啦，都講咗幾百次㗎喇！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 sing4 jat6 caau2 laang5 faan6 laa1, dou1 gong2 zo2 gei2 baak3 ci3 gaa3 laa3!
english_sentence: Don't keep rehashing old news, you've said it hundreds of times already!

english: To fire one's boss (literally: to fry the boss's squid)
cantonese_sentence: 佢忍唔住炒咗老細魷魚，唔撈喇。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jan2 m4 zyu6 caau2 zo2 lou5 sai3 yau4 yu2, m4 laau1 laa3.
english_sentence: He couldn't take it anymore and fired his boss, quitting his job.

english: Put (everything) together; Mix everything up; Make a mess
cantonese_sentence: 你唔好再搞啦，你再搞落去就炒埋一碟㗎啦！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zoi3 gaau2 laa1, nei5 zoi3 gaau2 lok6 heoi3 zau6 caau2 maai4 jat1 dip6 gaa3 laa1!
english_sentence: Don't touch it anymore! If you keep messing with it, you're going to make a mess of everything!

cantonese_sentence: 我今晚想食炒米。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 maan5 soeng2 sik6 caau2 mai5.
english_sentence: I want to eat fried rice tonight.

english: Fried rice crisp / Fried rice cracker
cantonese_sentence: 我細個成日食炒米餅。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 sai3 go3 seng4 jat6 sik6 caau2 mai5 beng2.
english_sentence: When I was little, I often ate fried rice crisps.

english: Car crash; to crash a car; to fail spectacularly (in a task)
cantonese_sentence: 佢頭先揸車炒咗車呀！
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 tau4 sin1 zaa1 ce1 caau2 zo2 ce1 aa3!
english_sentence: He just crashed his car a while ago!

english: Scalping tickets (buying tickets at face value and reselling them at a higher price)
cantonese_sentence: 唔好炒黃牛啦，貴咁多！
