english_sentence: I'm going to get a perm tomorrow, I want to try some new hairstyles.

cantonese_sentence: 熱到死，開大啲部電風扇啦!
jyutping_sentence: jit6 dou3 si2, hoi1 daai6 di1 bou6 din6 fung1 saan3 laa1!
english_sentence: It's so hot, turn the electric fan on louder!

cantonese_sentence: 架車冇電油，行唔到呀！
jyutping_sentence: gaa3 ce1 mou5 din6 jau4, haang4 m4 dou2 aa3!
english_sentence: The car has no gasoline, it can't go!

english: Mesmerizing eyes; a look of intense focus; radar eyes (sharp eyesight)
cantonese_sentence: 佢對電眼好吸引人呀。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 deoi3 din6 ngaan5 hou2 kap1 jan4 aa3.
english_sentence: Her mesmerizing eyes are very attractive.

cantonese_sentence: 我部手機粒電芯舊咗，好快冇電。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 bou6 sau2 gei1 lap1 din6 sam1 gau6 zo2, hou2 faai3 mou5 din6.
english_sentence: My phone battery is old, it runs out of power quickly.

cantonese_sentence: 我聽日會搭電船過海。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ting1 jat6 wui5 daap3 din6 syun4 gwo3 hoi2.
english_sentence: I will take the ferry across the harbour tomorrow.

cantonese_sentence: 攞個電筒嚟照下。
jyutping_sentence: lo2 go3 din6 tung2 lai4 ziu3 haa5.
english_sentence: Bring the flashlight over here to shine it.

cantonese_sentence: 佢打緊麻雀，擲緊粒丁。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 daa2 gan2 maa4 zoek2, zaak6 gan2 lap1 ding1.
english_sentence: He's playing mahjong, throwing the dice.

cantonese_sentence: 我鍾意用丁香嚟炆豬肉。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zung1 ji3 yung6 ding1 hoeng1 lai4 man1 zyu1 juk6.
english_sentence: I like to use cloves to braise pork.

english: Small House Policy entitlement (in Hong Kong)
cantonese_sentence: 佢哋嘅村想用丁權起多幾間屋。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 ge3 cyun1 soeng2 yung6 ding1 kyun4 hei2 do1 gei2 gaan1 uk1.
english_sentence: Their village wants to use their Small House Policy entitlements to build a few more houses.

english: Village House (a type of house in the New Territories of Hong Kong only granted to male indigenous villagers)
cantonese_sentence: 我哋村嗰度起咗好多丁屋。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 cyun1 go2 dou6 hei2 zo2 hou2 do1 ding1 uk1.
english_sentence: A lot of village houses have been built in our village.

english: Ding (onomatopoeic, sound of a bell or microwave)
cantonese_sentence: 叮一聲，微波爐好啦。
jyutping_sentence: ding1 jat1 seng1, mei1 bo1 lou4 hou2 laa1.
english_sentence: Ding! The microwave is done.

english: Ding ding (onomatopoeia for the sound a bell makes), tram
cantonese_sentence: 我喺叮叮上面瞓著咗。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hai2 ding1 ding1 soeng6 min6 fan3 zoek3 zo2.
english_sentence: I fell asleep on the tram.

cantonese_sentence: 你聽日記得準時交功課，唔好叮噹馬頭先嚟做呀！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 ting1 jat6 gei3 dak1 zeon2 si4 gaau1 gung1 fo3, m4 hou2 ding1 dong1 maa5 tau4 sin1 lai4 zou6 aa3!
english_sentence: Remember to hand in your homework on time tomorrow, don't do it at the last minute!

cantonese_sentence: 你頂住先，我好快返嚟幫你。
jyutping_sentence: nei5 ding2 zyu6 sin1, ngo5 hou2 faai3 faan1 lei4 bong1 nei5.
english_sentence: Endure/Hold on for a bit, I'll be back soon to help you.

english: To take the blame for someone else, to be a scapegoat
cantonese_sentence: 佢撞車之後，搵咗個朋友嚟頂包。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zong6 ce1 zi1 hau6, wan2 zo2 go3 pang4 jau5 lai4 ding2 baau1.
english_sentence: After he crashed his car, he found a friend to take the blame.

english: to hold the fort, to cover, to temporarily take over (a responsibility or role)
cantonese_sentence: 我今日要幫同事頂檔。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 jat6 jiu3 bong1 tung4 si6 ding2 dong3.
english_sentence: I need to cover for my colleague today.

cantonese_sentence: 佢個人好頂趾，講咩都唔聽。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 go3 jan4 hou2 deng2 zi2, gong2 me1 dou1 m4 teng1.
english_sentence: He is a very stubborn person, he doesn't listen to anything you say.

cantonese_sentence: 佢喺法庭頂證佢嘅同謀。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 faat3 ting4 ding2 zing3 keoi5 ge3 tung4 mau4.
english_sentence: He testified against his accomplice in court.

english: To talk back; to argue with (someone superior)
cantonese_sentence: 唔好咁頂頸啦！
jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 gam2 ding2 geng2 laa1!
english_sentence: Don't be so argumentative!

english: Addictive, enjoyable to the point of addiction, intensely satisfying
cantonese_sentence: 呢隻劇真係好頂癮，我一晚煲哂成季。
jyutping_sentence: ni1 zek3 kek6 zan1 hai6 hou2 ding2 jan5, ngo5 jat1 maan5 bou1 saai2 sing4 gwai3.
english_sentence: This drama is really addictive; I binged the whole season in one night.

cantonese_sentence: 呢間餐廳嘅食材全部都係頂級嘅。
jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 caan1 teng1 ge3 sik6 coi4 cyun4 bou6 dou1 hai6 ding2 gap1 ge3.
english_sentence: The ingredients at this restaurant are all top-notch.

cantonese_sentence: 我頂籠得閒一個鐘
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ding2 lung4 dak1 haan4 jat1 go3 zung1
english_sentence: At most, I'm only free for an hour.

english: Damn you; Screw you; Go to hell (literally: "I top your lungs")
cantonese_sentence: 你再講啲咁嘅嘢，我真係頂你個肺！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 zoi3 gong2 di1 gam2 ge3 je5, ngo5 zan1 hai6 ding2 nei5 go3 fai3!
english_sentence: If you say anything like that again, I'll really tell you to go to hell!

english: Can't take it anymore, can't handle it, can't stand it.
cantonese_sentence: 我真係頂唔住咁多嘢做呀!
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zan1 hai6 ding2 m4 zyu6 gam3 do1 je5 zou6 aa3!
english_sentence: I really can't handle doing so much stuff!

english: Can't take it anymore/Can't handle it/Reached my limit
cantonese_sentence: 我真係頂唔順日日OT到咁夜啦！
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zan1 hai6 ding2 m4 seon6 jat6 jat6 OT dou3 gam3 je6 laa1!
english_sentence: I really can't take it anymore working overtime so late every day!

english: To grit your teeth and bear it/to tough it out/to push through despite difficulty.
cantonese_sentence: 冇時間喇，頂硬上啦！
jyutping_sentence: mou5 si4 gaan3 laa1, ding2 ngaang6 soeng5 laa1!
english_sentence: There's no time, just tough it out!

english: To hold the fort; to tough it out; to cope with a difficult situation
cantonese_sentence: 我今日唔舒服，要你幫我頂硬檔喇。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 jat6 m4 syu1 fuk6, jiu3 nei5 bong1 ngo5 ding2 ngaang6 dong2 laa3.
english_sentence: I'm not feeling well today, I need you to hold the fort for me.

english: Annoying; irritating; frustrating (literally: hitting the heart, hitting the lungs)
cantonese_sentence: 佢講嘢成日都頂心頂肺，真係唔想同佢傾偈。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2 je5 seng4 jat6 dou1 ding2 sam1 ding2 fai3, zan1 hai6 m4 soeng2 tung4 keoi5 king1 gai2.
english_sentence: What he says is always so irritating, I really don't want to talk to him.

english: A person who is obstructive, deliberately difficult, or a thorn in one's side.
cantonese_sentence: 佢擺明係頂心杉，事事都唱反調。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 baai2 ming4 hai6 ding2 sam1 saan1, si6 si6 dou1 coeng3 faan2 diu6.
english_sentence: He is clearly a thorn in our side, disagreeing with everything.

english: Salary ceiling/Top of the pay scale
cantonese_sentence: 佢做到頂薪點都走，一定係對公司好失望。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 dou3 ding2 san1 dim2 dou1 zau2, jat1 ding6 hai6 deoi3 gung1 si1 hou2 sat1 mong6.
english_sentence: He left even though he reached the salary ceiling, he must be very disappointed with the company.

english: To take over a business (usually with existing debts or obligations)
cantonese_sentence: 我想頂手嗰間茶餐廳。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 soeng2 ding2 sau2 go2 gaan1 caa4 caan1 teng1.
english_sentence: I want to take over that 'cha chaan teng' (Hong Kong style cafe).

english: To offset an amount (like a debt) with work or goods; to do something in lieu of payment.
cantonese_sentence: 我幫你做嘢嚟頂數啦。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 bong1 nei5 zou6 je5 lai4 ding2 sou3 laa1.
english_sentence: I'll help you do some work to offset the debt.

english: First in line; the person who takes on the initial or hardest part of a task; lead; the first to do something.
cantonese_sentence: 等我嚟頂頭陣啦，你哋休息下先。
jyutping_sentence: dang2 ngo5 lai4 ding2 tau4 zan6 laa1, nei5 dei6 jau1 sik1 haa5 sin1.
english_sentence: Let me take the lead, you guys rest first.

cantonese_sentence: 佢用頂頭槌撞到佢暈低。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jung6 ding2 tau4 ceoi4 zong6 dou3 keoi5 wan4 dai1.
english_sentence: He used a headbutt and knocked him unconscious.

cantonese_sentence: 呢個糯米雞好頂肚呀！
jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 no6 mai5 gai1 hou2 ding2 dou5 aa3!
english_sentence: This sticky rice chicken is very filling!

english: Feeling slightly hungry/To curb hunger/To fill the stomach temporarily
cantonese_sentence: 我食啲餅頂肚餓先啦。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 sik6 di1 beng2 ding2 tou5 ngo6 sin1 laa1.
english_sentence: I'll eat some biscuits to curb my hunger first.

cantonese_sentence: 我諗住聽日去行山，但係未定。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 nam2 zyu6 ting1 jat6 heoi3 haang4 saan1, daan6 hai6 mei6 ding6.
english_sentence: I'm thinking of going hiking tomorrow, but it's not definite yet.

cantonese_sentence: 啲車厘茄連椗都好新鮮嘅。
jyutping_sentence: di1 ce1 lei2 ge3 lin4 deng3 dou1 hou2 san1 sin1 ge3.
english_sentence: The cherry tomatoes are fresh, even with their stems.

cantonese_sentence: 你決定咗去邊度未啊？
jyutping_sentence: nei5 kyut3 ding6 zo2 heoi3 bin1 dou6 mei6 aa3?
english_sentence: Have you decided where to go yet?

cantonese_sentence: 你咁努力，定必會成功嘅。
jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam3 nou5 lik6, ding6 bit1 wui5 sing4 gung1 ge3.
english_sentence: You're working so hard, you're bound to succeed.

cantonese_sentence: 我哋喺定點集合。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 hai2 ding6 dim2 zaap6 hap6.
english_sentence: Let's meet at the designated meeting point.

cantonese_sentence: 我定當盡力幫你
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ding6 dong3 zeon6 lik6 bong1 nei5
english_sentence: I will definitely try my best to help you.

english: Absolutely certain; more stable than holding a bottle of oil
cantonese_sentence: 佢份人定過抬油，講得出就一定做得到。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 fan6 jan4 ding6 gwo3 toi4 jau4, gong2 dak1 ceot1 zau6 jat1 ding6 zou6 dak1 dou3.
english_sentence: He is a man of his word, if he says he will do it, he will definitely do it.

cantonese_sentence: 你想食飯定係麵呀？
jyutping_sentence: nei5 soeng2 sik6 faan6 ding6 hai6 min6 aa3?
english_sentence: Do you want to eat rice or noodles?

cantonese_sentence: 佢嘅定力好夠，就算面對再大嘅挑戰都唔會放棄。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ge3 ding6 lik6 hou2 gau3, zau6 syun3 min6 deoi3 zoi3 daai6 ge3 tiu1 zin3 dou1 m4 wui5 fong3 hei3.
english_sentence: His willpower is strong, even if he faces big challenges he won't give up.

cantonese_sentence: 我哋要俾定銀先至可以hold住呢間屋.
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 jiu3 bei2 ding6 ngan2 sin1 zi3 ho2 ji5 hold1 zyu6 ni1 gaan1 uk1.
english_sentence: We need to pay a deposit first to hold this house.

cantonese_sentence: 份合約已經定晒形，唔可以再改㗎喇。
jyutping_sentence: fan6 hap6 joek3 ji5 ging1 ding6 saai3 jing4, m4 ho2 ji5 zoi3 gaai2 gaa3 laa3.
english_sentence: The contract is already finalized, it can't be changed anymore.

english: Regularly; at a fixed time and place
cantonese_sentence: 我哋定時定候喺公園門口見。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 ding6 si4 ding6 hau6 hai2 gung1 jyun2 mun4 hau2 gin3.
english_sentence: We meet regularly at the park entrance.

cantonese_sentence: 我想食個牛肉定食。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 soeng2 sik6 go3 ngau4 juk6 ding6 sik6.
english_sentence: I want to eat a beef set meal.

english: To finalize, to settle on, to make a decision regarding a specific item or matter.
cantonese_sentence: 我哋定條聽日食邊間餐廳啦.
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 ding6 tiu4 ting1 jat6 sik6 bin1 gaan1 can1 teng1 laa1
english_sentence: Let's decide on which restaurant to eat at tomorrow.

cantonese_sentence: 我要一隻碟嚟裝啲嘢食。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 jiu3 jat1 zek3 dip6 lai4 zong1 di1 je5 sik6.
english_sentence: I want a plate to put some food on.

english: Rice dish served on a plate
cantonese_sentence: 今日我想食個叉燒碟頭飯。
jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 ngo5 soeng2 sik6 go3 caa1 siu1 dip6 tau4 faan6.
english_sentence: Today I want to eat a char siu (barbecue pork) rice plate.

english: To be certain; to be set on something; to be completely decided; to have your mind made up.
cantonese_sentence: 我已經疊埋心水，今年一定要去旅行。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ji5 ging1 dip6 maai4 sam1 seoi2, gam1 nin4 jat1 ding6 jiu3 heoi3 leoi5 hang4.
english_sentence: I've already made up my mind; I'm definitely going on a trip this year.

english: Lose money (usually in investments or gambling)
cantonese_sentence: 今日炒股跌咗好多，跌咗紙呀!
jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 caau2 gu2 dit3 zo2 hou2 do1, dit3 zo2 zi2 aa3!
english_sentence: I lost a lot of money investing in stocks today!

cantonese_sentence: 我跌咗條鎖匙。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dit3 zo2 tiu4 so2 si4.
english_sentence: I lost my keys.

cantonese_sentence: 部手機跌價跌得好犀利啊！
jyutping_sentence: bou6 sau2 gei1 dit3 gaa3 dit3 dak1 hou2 sai1 lei6 aa3!
english_sentence: This phone's price has dropped drastically!

english: To fall, to trip and fall
cantonese_sentence: 佢行路唔小心，跌咗一跤。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 haang4 lou6 m4 siu2 sam1, dit3 zo2 jat1 gaau3.
english_sentence: He/She wasn't careful walking and fell.

jyutping: dit3 lok6 dei6 laa2 faan1 zaa2 saa1
english: When you fall on the ground, grab a handful of sand (to save face/make something of a bad situation)
cantonese_sentence: 佢做錯咗嘢仲要死撐，真係跌落地揦翻拃沙。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 co3 zo2 je5 zung6 jiu3 si2 caang1, zan1 hai6 dit3 lok6 dei6 laa2 faan1 zaa2 saa1.
english_sentence: He messed up and still tries to justify it, he's really grabbing a handful of sand after falling on the ground.

english: Be surprised; Be shocked; Have one's expectations overturned (literally: drop glasses)
cantonese_sentence: 估唔到佢真係會贏，跌晒眼鏡。
jyutping_sentence: gu2 m4 dou3 keoi5 zan1 hai6 wui5 wing4, dit3 saai3 ngaan5 geng2.
english_sentence: I didn't expect him to actually win, it was a real shock!

cantonese_sentence: 佢最近好似跌咗watt咁，做嘢冇晒心機。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zeoi3 gan6 hou2 ci5 dit3 zo2 wat1 gam2, zou6 je5 mou5晒 sam1 gei1.
english_sentence: He seems to have lost his enthusiasm lately, and isn't motivated to work anymore.

english: To abandon and leave fallow/uncultivated (usually farmland, but can also apply to skills or knowledge)
cantonese_sentence: 啲田丟荒咗好耐。
jyutping_sentence: di1 tin4 diu1 fong1 zo2 hou2 noi6.
english_sentence: Those fields have been abandoned for a long time.

cantonese_sentence: 你喺咁多人面前唔認得我，真係好丟架呀!
jyutping_sentence: nei5 hai2 gam3 do1 jan4 min6 cin4 m4 jing6 dak1 ngo5, zan1 hai6 hou2 diu1 gaa3 aa3!
english_sentence: You didn't recognize me in front of so many people, it's really embarrassing!

english: To embarrass oneself, to lose face, to make a fool of oneself.
cantonese_sentence: 你唔好再咁樣，真係好丟生㗎！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zoi3 gam2 joeng2, zan1 hai6 hou2 diu1 saang1 gaa3!
english_sentence: Don't act like that again, it's really embarrassing!

english: To be careless; to overlook; to be negligent
cantonese_sentence: 你咁丟疏，遲早出事㗎！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam3 diu1 so1, ci4 zou2 ceot1 si6 gaa3!
english_sentence: You're so careless, sooner or later something bad will happen!

english: To show off one's knowledge; to flaunt one's education (often negatively, implying arrogance)
cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺人哋面前丟書包，真係好乞人憎。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 hai2 jan4 dei6 min6 cin4 diu1 syu1 baau1, zan1 hai6 hou2 hat1 jan4 zang1.
english_sentence: He always shows off his knowledge in front of others, it's really annoying.

english: Fussy, picky, difficult to please, often describes someone (usually a child) being demanding and annoying.
cantonese_sentence: 個細路仔好刁喬扭擰，乜嘢都要跟佢心意。
jyutping_sentence: go3 sai3 lou6 zai2 hou2 diu1 kiu4 nau2 ning6, mat1 je5 dou1 jiu3 gan1 keoi5 sam1 ji3.
english_sentence: That kid is so fussy; everything has to be according to his/her wishes.

cantonese_sentence: 個女仔好刁蠻，成日扭計。
jyutping_sentence: go3 neoi5 zai2 hou2 diu1 maan4, seng4 jat6 nau2 gai2.
english_sentence: That girl is very spoiled and willful, she always throws tantrums.

english: Picky; particular; fussy (especially about food or drink)
cantonese_sentence: 佢好刁時，乜嘢都唔啱食。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hou2 diu1 si4, mat1 je5 dou1 m4 ngaam1 sik6.
english_sentence: He's very picky; he doesn't like anything.

cantonese_sentence: 你做乜撚嘢呀，屌你老母！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 zou6 mat1 ne1 je5 aa3, diu2 nei5 lou5 mou2!
english_sentence: What the fuck are you doing, fuck your mother!

english: A very rude and vulgar Cantonese profanity, roughly translating to "fuck your mother." It is considered extremely offensive.
cantonese_sentence: 你做乜撚嘢呀？屌那媽！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 zou6 mat1 ne1 je5 aa3? diu2 naa1 maa1!
english_sentence: What the fuck are you doing? Fuck your mother!

cantonese_sentence: 你再嘈，我就屌你老母！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 zoi3 cou4, ngo5 zau6 diu2 nei5 lou5 mou2!
english_sentence: If you keep being noisy, I'll fuck your mother!

english: Credit account; Being in debt; Running a tab
cantonese_sentence: 我哋熟客，可以吊帳嘅。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 suk6 haak3, ho2 ji5 diu3 zoeng3 ge3.
english_sentence: We're regular customers, we can run a tab.

english: Hanging bell; also a type of flower (Enkianthus quinqueflorus)
cantonese_sentence: 棵吊鐘開咗好多花。
jyutping_sentence: po1 diu3 zung1 hoi1 zo2 hou2 do1 faa1.
english_sentence: That Enkianthus quinqueflorus has bloomed many flowers.

cantonese_sentence: 我哋要叫架吊雞車嚟先至可以將呢舊嘢吊起。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 jiu3 giu3 gaa3 diu3 gai1 ce1 lai4 sin1 zai3 ho2 ji5 zoeng1 ni1 gau6 je5 diu3 hei2.
english_sentence: We need to call a crane truck to be able to lift this thing.

cantonese_sentence: 佢因為欠債而吊頸自殺。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 yan1 wai6 him3 jai3 yi4 diu3 geng2 zi6 saat3.
english_sentence: He hanged himself because of his debts.

jyutping: diu3 geng2 dou1 jiu3 tau3 hei3
english: Even when hanging yourself, you still need to breathe. (Even in dire situations, one still needs a break or some leeway.)
cantonese_sentence: 你做嘢唔好咁chur，吊頸都要透氣，休息吓先啦。
jyutping_sentence: nei5 zou6 je5 m4 hou2 gam3 chur1, diu3 geng2 dou1 jiu3 tau3 hei3, jau1 sik1 haa5 sin1 laa1.
english_sentence: Don't push yourself so hard with work. Even when hanging yourself, you need to breathe. Take a break first.

english: Too short, ankle-revealing (referring to pants or clothing)
cantonese_sentence: 條褲吊腳到呢！
jyutping_sentence: tiu4 fu3 diu3 goek3 dou3 ni1!
english_sentence: These pants are way too short!

cantonese_sentence: 廚房個吊櫃裝滿晒嘢。
jyutping_sentence: chu4 fong2 go3 diu3 gwai6 zong1 mun5 saai3 je5.
english_sentence: The wall cabinet in the kitchen is full of stuff.

english: To make something seem more desirable or valuable than it actually is; to artificially inflate demand. Often used sarcastically.

english: Flourishing anniversary; A prosperous anniversary. Often used to wish businesses a successful and thriving anniversary.

jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 zau1 nin4 wong6 soeng3, sang1 ji3 hing1 lung4!
english_sentence: May your company have a prosperous anniversary and a thriving business!

english: Covered in bling/jewelry; dressed to the nines (often implying it's excessive or gaudy)
cantonese_sentence: 佢今日周身八寶咁，去邊度呀？
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam1 jat6 zau1 san1 baat3 bou2 gam2, heoi3 bin1 dou6 aa3?
english_sentence: Where is she going dressed up to the nines today? (literally: Where is she going so covered in bling today?)

jyutping: zau1 san1 dou1 - mou5 zoeng1 lei6
english: Jack of all trades, master of none.
cantonese_sentence: 佢周身刀冇張利，樣樣都識啲，但係冇樣精。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zau1 san1 dou1 mou5 zoeng1 lei6, joeng2 joeng2 dou1 sik1 di1, daan6 hai6 mou5 joeng2 zing1.
english_sentence: He is a jack of all trades, master of none; he knows a little about everything, but isn't proficient in anything.

english: Itchy all over, having a strong urge to do something (often something slightly naughty or undesirable)
cantonese_sentence: 我今日周身癮，好想去行街買嘢。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 jat6 zau1 san1 jan5, hou2 seong2 heoi3 haang4 gaai1 maai5 ye5.
english_sentence: I'm really itching to go shopping and buy things today.

english: A person who is unable to accumulate wealth; someone who quickly spends or loses money.
cantonese_sentence: 佢份人周身唔聚財，一出糧就好快用晒。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 fan6 jan4 zau1 san1 m4 zeoi6 coi4, jat1 ceot1 loeng4 zau6 hou2 faai3 jung6 saai3.
english_sentence: He's the type of person who can't hold onto money; he spends it all quickly after getting paid.

english: Feeling itchy all over (literally: "ants all over the body")
cantonese_sentence: 唔好搞我，周身蟻呀！
jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 gaau2 ngo5, zau1 san1 ngai5 aa3!
english_sentence: Don't bother me, I'm feeling itchy all over!

english: Covered in shit, figuratively means "always in trouble" or "a troublemaker"
cantonese_sentence: 你條友仔周身屎，次次都搞搞震！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 tiu4 jau5 zai2 zau1 san1 si2, ci3 ci3 dou1 gaau2 gaau2 zan3!
english_sentence: You're always causing trouble! (You troublemaker, always causing trouble!)

english: Often; frequently; from time to time
cantonese_sentence: 佢周時遲到。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zau1 si4 ci4 dou3.
english_sentence: He/She is often late.

cantonese_sentence: 佢周時無日都唔做嘢，淨係喺度瞓覺。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zau1 si4 mou4 jat6 dou1 m4 zou6 je5, zing6 hai6 hai2 dou6 fan3 gaau3.
english_sentence: He often doesn't do any work, he just sleeps all the time.

cantonese_sentence: 我週日會去飲茶。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zau1 jat6 wui5 heoi3 jam2 caa4.
english_sentence: I will go to yum cha on Sunday.

english: to leave; to go; to run
cantonese_sentence: 我哋走先啦!
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 zau2 sin1 laa1!
english_sentence: We're leaving first!

cantonese_sentence: 佢好叻走籃，成日都入到波。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hou2 lek1 zau2 laam2, seng4 jat6 dou1 jap6 dou2 bo1.
english_sentence: He's very good at layups, he scores a lot.

english: To drive an unlicensed taxi (without proper permits and insurance)
cantonese_sentence: 佢走白牌，俾差佬捉咗，罰咗好多錢。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zau2 baak6 paai4, bei2 chaai1 lou2 zuk1 zo2, fat6 zo2 hou2 do1 chin2.
english_sentence: He drove an unlicensed taxi, got caught by the police, and was fined a lot of money.

english: Bad luck on top of bad luck / To be in a situation where things are already bad, and then they get even worse.
cantonese_sentence: 我今日已經遲到，點知架車又壞埋，真係走兵遇到賊！
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 jat6 ji5 ging1 ci4 dou3, dim2 ji1 gaa3 ce1 jau6 waai6 maai4, zan1 hai6 zau2 bing1 jyu6 dou6 caak6!
english_sentence: I was already late today, and then my car broke down, it's really bad luck on top of bad luck!

english: To miss out on a good deal; to let a treasure slip through your fingers; to miss a bargain.
cantonese_sentence: 我琴日喺二手市場度走咗寶，本來想買嘅古董花瓶畀人買咗。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 kam4 jat6 hai2 ji5 sau2 si5 coeng4 dou6 zau2 zo2 bou2, bun2 loi4 soeng2 maai5 ge3 gu2 dung2 faa1 ping4 bei2 jan4 maai5 zo2.
english_sentence: I missed out on a great deal at the flea market yesterday. The antique vase I wanted to buy was bought by someone else.

english: to dine and dash, to leave without paying
cantonese_sentence: 佢食完嘢走咗單，好冇品呀！
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sik6 jyun4 je5 zau2 zo2 daan1, hou2 mou5 ban2 aa3!
english_sentence: He ate and then dined and dashed; how rude!

jyutping: zau2 dak1 faai3 hou2 sai3 gaai3
english: Run quickly to find a better world (lit: Running fast makes for a good world)
cantonese_sentence: 做唔掂咪走囉，走得快好世界。
jyutping_sentence: zou6 m4 dim6 mai1 zau2 lo1, zau2 dak1 faai3 hou2 sai3 gaai3.
english_sentence: If you can't handle it, just leave, running quickly is a good thing!

cantonese_sentence: 今日買咗隻走地雞返屋企整豉油雞。
jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 maai5 zo2 zek3 zau2 dei6 gai1 faan1 uk1 kei2 zeng2 si6 jau4 gai1.
english_sentence: Today, I bought a free-range chicken to bring home and make soy sauce chicken.

cantonese_sentence: 佢嚇到即刻走趯。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hak1 dou3 zik1 hak1 zau2 dek3.
english_sentence: He was so scared he ran away immediately.

cantonese_sentence: 部電飯煲走電呀，好危險！
jyutping_sentence: bou6 din6 faan6 bou1 zau2 din6 aa3, hou2 ngai4 him2!
english_sentence: The rice cooker has an electrical leak, it's very dangerous!

english: To default on a debt, to skip out on paying
cantonese_sentence: 佢爭人好多錢，而家走咗債。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zaang1 jan4 hou2 do1 cin2, ji4 gaa1 zau2 zo2 zaai3.
english_sentence: He owes people a lot of money and has now defaulted on his debts.

english: Escape blame/responsibility; Shirk responsibility; Pass the buck
cantonese_sentence: 佢成日走盞，做錯嘢就賴其他人。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 zau2 zaan2, zou6 co3 je5 zau6 laai6 kei4 taa1 jan4.
english_sentence: He always shirks responsibility, blaming others when he does something wrong.

cantonese_sentence: 佢喺度走走趯趯，唔知搞乜。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 dou6 zau2 zau2 tek1 tek1, m4 zi1 gaau2 mat1.
english_sentence: He/She's bustling about here, I don't know what he/she is doing.

english: To try and get away with something (often by being sly or cunning); to try to take advantage; to shirk responsibility.
cantonese_sentence: 佢成日都想走精面，唔想做多嘢。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 dou1 soeng2 zau2 zing1 min6, m4 soeng2 zou6 do1 je5.
english_sentence: He always tries to get away with things and doesn't want to do extra work.

cantonese_sentence: 佢走咗去英國啦
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zau2 zo2 heoi3 jing1 gwok3 laa1
english_sentence: He/She has gone to England.

cantonese_sentence: 嗰個走犯啱啱喺呢頭出現過。
jyutping_sentence: go2 go3 zau2 faan6 ngaam1 ngaam1 hai2 ni1 tau2 ceot1 jin6 gwo3.
english_sentence: That escaped prisoner just appeared around here.

english: To exploit a loophole in the law; to find a legal loophole
cantonese_sentence: 佢哋走法律罅避稅。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 zau2 faat3 leut6 laai3 bei6 seoi3.
english_sentence: They avoided taxes by exploiting a legal loophole.

cantonese_sentence: 佢因為走粉俾警察拉咗.
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jan1 wai6 zau2 fan2 bei2 ging2 caat3 laai1 zo2.
english_sentence: He was arrested by the police for smuggling drugs.

english: To travel to different cities or towns, usually for work or business; to be on the road.
cantonese_sentence: 佢成日要走埠，好少喺屋企。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 jiu3 zau2 bou6, hou2 siu2 hai2 uk1 kei2.
english_sentence: He has to travel a lot, and is rarely at home.

english: Accidental discharge (of a firearm); also used metaphorically for things going wrong or awry.
cantonese_sentence: 佢唔小心走咗火，差啲射親人。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 m4 siu2 sam1 zau2 zo2 fo2, caa1 di1 se6 can1 jan4.
english_sentence: He accidentally discharged the gun, almost shooting someone.

cantonese_sentence: 成日有人撳鐘搞到走火警, 好煩呀!
jyutping_sentence: sing4 jat6 jau5 jan4 gam6 zung1 gaau2 dou3 zau2 fo2 ging2, hou2 faan4 aa3!
english_sentence: It's so annoying when people keep pressing the fire alarm and causing false alarms!

cantonese_sentence: 喺走火通道唔可以擺放雜物。
jyutping_sentence: hai2 zau2 fo2 tung1 dou6 m4 ho2 ji5 baai2 fong3 zaap6 mat6.
english_sentence: You can't put clutter in the fire exit.

english: To wander around the streets; to go window shopping; to stroll
cantonese_sentence: 今日冇嘢做，我哋去走街啦。
jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 mou5 je5 zou6, ngo5 dei6 heoi3 zau2 gaai1 laa1.
english_sentence: I have nothing to do today, let's go stroll around.

english: Leave without stopping; To leave in a hurry without rest. (Implies being extremely busy or wanting to escape quickly)
cantonese_sentence: 我今日忙到走夾唔唞。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 jat6 mong4 dou3 zau2 gaap3 m4 tau2.
english_sentence: I was so busy today I didn't have a moment's rest.

english: The bird flew away / The game has slipped away / An opportunity has been lost.
cantonese_sentence: 唉，差啲贏波，點知最後走雞。
jyutping_sentence: ai1, caa1 di1 wing4 bo1, dim2 zi1 zeoi3 hau6 zau2 gai1.
english_sentence: Ah, we were almost winning the game, but unexpectedly we lost the opportunity at the end.

english: to cancel/clear an alarm; to call off an alert
cantonese_sentence: 唔使驚，已經走咗警報喇。
jyutping_sentence: m4 sai2 geng1, ji5 ging1 zau2 zo2 ging2 bou3 laa3.
english_sentence: Don't worry, the alarm has been cancelled already.

english: Run away from the authorities (typically vendors evading law enforcement)
cantonese_sentence: 差人嚟啦，快啲走鬼呀！
jyutping_sentence: caa1 jan4 lai4 laa1, faai3 di1 zau2 gwai2 aa3!
english_sentence: The cops are coming, run away quickly!

english: wardrobe malfunction, revealing underwear or parts of the body
cantonese_sentence: 佢今日條裙太短，行路嘅時候差啲走光。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam1 jat6 tiu4 kwan4 taai3 dyun2, haang4 lou6 ge3 si4 hau6 caa1 dik1 zau2 gwong1.
english_sentence: Her skirt is too short today, she almost had a wardrobe malfunction when she was walking.

english: To leave, to take off, to scram
cantonese_sentence: 我走人先啦，拜拜！
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zau2 jan4 sin1 laa1, baai1 baai3!
english_sentence: I'm leaving first, bye bye!

cantonese_sentence: 佢走甩咗，唔知去咗邊。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zau2 lat1 zo2, m4 zi1 heoi3 zo2 bin1.
english_sentence: He/She escaped, (I) don't know where (he/she) went.

english: To miss something; to overlook; to fail to notice
cantonese_sentence: 我頭先走漏眼，冇見到你喺度。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 tau4 sin1 zau2 lau6 ngaan5, mou5 gin3 dou2 nei5 hai2 dou6.
english_sentence: I missed you earlier, I didn't see you were here.

cantonese_sentence: 我哋行路去旺角。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 haang4 lou6 heoi3 wong6 gok3.
english_sentence: Let's walk to Mong Kok.

cantonese_sentence: 聽講間走馬樓啲嘢食好貴。
jyutping_sentence: ting1 gong2 gaan1 zau2 maa5 lau4 di1 je5 sik6 hou2 gwai3.
english_sentence: I heard the food at that revolving restaurant is very expensive.

english: To lose its original flavor; to go stale; to taste different and usually not in a good way. Often used for food or drinks.
cantonese_sentence: 呢杯咖啡擺咗咁耐，走晒味啦。
jyutping_sentence: ni1 bui1 gaa3 fe1 baai2 zo2 gam3 noi6, zau2 saai3 mei6 laa1.
english_sentence: This cup of coffee has been sitting out for so long, it's completely lost its flavor.

cantonese_sentence: 聽日打風，我哋要走難去朋友屋企。
jyutping_sentence: ting1 jat6 daa2 fung1, ngo5 dei6 jiu3 zau2 naan6 heoi3 pang4 jau5 uk1 kei2.
english_sentence: There's a typhoon tomorrow, we need to seek refuge at our friend's house.

english: Trend, direction, momentum (often in finance, markets, or sports)
cantonese_sentence: 呢隻股票嘅走勢唔錯，睇嚟仲有得升。
jyutping_sentence: ni1 zek3 gu2 piu3 ge3 zau2 sai3 m4 co3, tai2 lai4 zung6 jau5 dak1 sing1.
english_sentence: The trend of this stock is good, it looks like it will still go up.

cantonese_sentence: 佢成日走水貨去大陸賺錢
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 zau2 seoi2 fo3 heoi3 daai6 luk6 zaan6 cin2
english_sentence: He always smuggles goods to mainland China to make money.

english: Smuggler (specifically one who avoids paying taxes or customs duties by carrying goods across the border, often in small quantities and frequently)
cantonese_sentence: 最近好多人喺羅湖做走水客。
jyutping_sentence: zeoi3 gan6 hou2 do1 jan4 hai2 lo4 wu4 zou6 zau2 seoi2 hak3.
english_sentence: Recently, many people are being smugglers in Lo Wu.

english: to skip out on paying a bill, to welch on a debt
cantonese_sentence: 佢成日走數，冇人想借錢俾佢。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 zau2 sou3, mou5 jan4 soeng2 ze3 cin2 bei2 keoi5.
english_sentence: He often skips out on paying his debts, no one wants to lend him money.

english: No way out; to be in a hopeless situation
cantonese_sentence: 佢賭到走投無路，唯有走佬。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dou2 dou3 zau2 tau4 mou4 lou6, wai4 jau5 zau2 lou2.
english_sentence: He gambled until he had no way out, so he could only run away.

cantonese_sentence: 佢成日走堂，所以考試肥佬。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 zau2 tong4, so2 ji5 haau2 si5 fei4 lou2.
english_sentence: He often skips class, so he failed the exam.

english: Gigging (performing at multiple venues, often referring to singers or performers)
cantonese_sentence: 佢成日走場，好辛苦㗎。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 zau2 coeng4, hou2 san1 fu2 gaa3.
english_sentence: He gigs all the time, it's very tiring.

english: Liquor Sample (usually a small bottle or portion for tasting)
cantonese_sentence: 我想拎啲酒辦返屋企試吓。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 soeng2 ling1 di1 zau2 baan6 faan1 uk1 kei2 si3 haa5.
english_sentence: I want to take some liquor samples back home to try.

english: Wine starter (a mixture of yeast and rice flour used to ferment rice wine)
cantonese_sentence: 我用酒餅嚟整甜酒釀。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 jung6 zau2 beng2 lai4 zing2 tim4 zau2 joeng6.
english_sentence: I use wine starter to make sweet fermented rice.

english: Rosacea (a skin condition causing redness and visible blood vessels in the face)
cantonese_sentence: 佢塊面紅卜卜，好似有酒渣噉。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 faai3 min6 hung4 buk1 buk1, hou2 ci5 jau5 zau2 zaa1 gam2.
english_sentence: Her face is very red, it seems like she has rosacea.

cantonese_sentence: 佢個鼻紅卜卜，好似有酒糟鼻噉。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 go3 bei6 hung4 bok1 bok1, hou2 ci5 jau5 zau2 zou1 bei6 gam2.
english_sentence: His nose is very red, it looks like he has rosacea.

cantonese_sentence: 我哋今晚去酒家飲茶啦。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 gam1 maan5 heoi3 zau2 gaa1 jam2 caa4 laa1.
english_sentence: Let's go to the restaurant for dim sum tonight.

english: Restaurant (specifically a traditional Cantonese restaurant serving dim sum and typically larger than a "cha chaan teng")
cantonese_sentence: 我哋聽日去酒樓飲茶啦。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 ting1 jat6 heoi3 jau2 lau4 jam2 chaa4 laa1.
english_sentence: Let's go to a restaurant for dim sum tomorrow.

cantonese_sentence: 今晚我哋去酒廊飲嘢啦。
jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 ngo5 dei6 heoi3 zau2 long4 jam2 ye5 laa1.
english_sentence: Let's go to the lounge for a drink tonight.

english: Distillers' rice, rice specifically for brewing alcohol
cantonese_sentence: 我哋買啲酒米嚟整糯米酒啦。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 maai5 di1 zau2 mai5 lai4 zing2 no6 mai5 zau2 laa1.
english_sentence: Let's buy some distillers' rice to make glutinous rice wine.

english: Dregs of liquor, small amount of leftover liquor
cantonese_sentence: 飲埋啲酒尾佢啦，唔好嘥。
jyutping_sentence: jam2 maai4 di1 zau2 mei5 keoi5 laa1, m4 hou2 saai1.
english_sentence: Drink up the dregs of the liquor, don't waste it.

cantonese_sentence: 佢笑起上嚟有個酒凹，好得意㗎。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 siu3 hei2 soeng5 lei4 jau5 go3 zau2 nap1, hou2 dak1 ji3 gaa3.
english_sentence: When she smiles, she has a dimple, it's very cute.

cantonese_sentence: 我哋今晚去嗰間酒吧有酒牌㗎。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 gam1 maan5 heoi3 go2 gaan1 zau2 baa1 jau5 zau2 paai4 gaa3.
english_sentence: The bar we're going to tonight has a liquor license.

cantonese_sentence: 今晚我請你哋飲酒水啦。
jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 ngo5 ceng2 nei5 dei6 jam2 zau2 seoi2 laa1.
english_sentence: I'm treating you all to drinks tonight.

cantonese_sentence: 攞啲皺紙抹下個口啦。
jyutping_sentence: lo2 di1 zau3 zi2 mut3 haa5 go3 hau2 laa1.
english_sentence: Take some tissue paper to wipe your mouth.

english: then, just, regarding, already (a versatile word with many nuances)
cantonese_sentence: 我就嚟到喇。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zau6 lai4 dou3 laa3.
english_sentence: I'm arriving soon.

english: To be careful (of someone/something); to be mindful; to yield; to give way. Often implies doing something less vigorously to avoid harming someone or something.
cantonese_sentence: 你細個，我就住你玩啦。
jyutping_sentence: nei5 sai3 go3, ngo5 zau6 zyu6 nei5 waan2 laa1.
english_sentence: You're young, I'll play carefully with you (not too rough).

cantonese_sentence: 就快落雨喇。
jyutping_sentence: zau6 faai3 lok6 jyu5 laa3.
english_sentence: It's going to rain soon.

english: I doubt it, if...then it's a lie.
cantonese_sentence: 如果佢話佢唔知，咁就假嘅。
jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 keoi5 waa6 keoi5 m4 zi1, gam2 zau6 gaa2 ge3.
english_sentence: If he says he doesn't know, then that's a lie.

cantonese_sentence: 間餐廳喺地鐵站隔離，好就腳。
jyutping_sentence: gaan1 caan1 teng1 hai2 dei6 tit3 zaam6 gaak3 lei4, hou2 zau6 goek3.
english_sentence: That restaurant is next to the subway station, it's very conveniently located.

cantonese_sentence: 我諗就係呢個原因喇。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 lam2 zau6 hai6 ni1 go3 jyun4 yan1 laa3.
english_sentence: I think that's exactly the reason.

cantonese_sentence: 我哋就嚟到喇
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 zau6 lai4 dou3 laa3
english_sentence: We are almost there/arriving soon.

cantonese_sentence: 呢支筆就手啲，用呢支啦。
jyutping_sentence: ni1 zi1 bat1 zau6 sau2 di1, jung6 ni1 zi1 laa1.
english_sentence: This pen is handier, use this one.

english: Indicating agreement; just saying; that's what I'm saying
cantonese_sentence: 我咪就話佢唔會嚟囉
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 mai1 zau6 waa6 keoi5 m4 wui5 lai4 lo1
english_sentence: That's what I was saying, he wouldn't come!

cantonese_sentence: 我唔記得咗戴袖口鈕，件衫好似差咁啲嘢。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 gei3 dak1 zo2 daai3 sau3 hau2 nau2, gin6 saam1 hou2 ci5 caa1 gam2 di1 je5.
english_sentence: I forgot to wear cufflinks, the shirt feels like it's missing something.

cantonese_sentence: 拎遮出街啦，今日落大雨呀！
jyutping_sentence: ling1 ze1 ceot1 gaai1 laa1, gam1 jat6 lok6 daai6 jyu5 aa3!
english_sentence: Take an umbrella with you when you go out, it's raining heavily today!

cantonese_sentence: 個遮柄爛咗。
jyutping_sentence: go3 ze1 beng3 laan6 zo2.
english_sentence: The umbrella handle is broken.

cantonese_sentence: 呢把遮嘅遮骨斷咗。
jyutping_sentence: ni1 baa2 ze1 ge3 ze1 gwat1 dyun3 zo2.

english_sentence: He lost his temper and scolded me badly.

english: To become rich; to strike it rich
cantonese_sentence: 佢買咗隻股票，依家發𤷪𤺧喇！
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 maai5 zo2 zek3 gu2 piu3, ji1 gaa1 faat3 lung3 dip1 laa3!
english_sentence: He bought a stock, and now he's struck it rich!

english: To be fiercely ill-tempered, to be a violent bully, to throw a tantrum.
cantonese_sentence: 佢成日發狼戾，冇人敢惹佢。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 faat3 long4 lai6, mou5 jan4 gam2 jo2 keoi5.
english_sentence: He's always throwing tantrums, no one dares to provoke him.

english: Not even in your wildest dreams (it's not even close to happening)
cantonese_sentence: 你諗住唔做嘢就發達，發夢冇咁早！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 lam2 zyu6 m4 zou6 je5 zau6 faat3 daat6, faat3 mung6 mou5 gam3 zo2!
english_sentence: You think you can get rich without working, not even in your wildest dreams!

english: To be scared, to be creeped out, to feel uneasy/repulsed
cantonese_sentence: 我諗起嗰件事就發毛。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 lam2 hei2 go2 gin6 si6 zau6 faat3 mou4.
english_sentence: I feel creeped out whenever I think about that incident.

english: To be stunned or dazed; to be unresponsive or blank.
cantonese_sentence: 佢聽完個消息之後，即刻發哂木獨，乜都唔識反應。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ting1 jyun4 go3 siu1 sik1 zi1 hau6, zik1 hak1 faat3 saai3 muk6 duk6, mat1 dou1 m4 sik1 faan2 ying3.
english_sentence: After hearing the news, he immediately became stunned and couldn't react to anything.

cantonese_sentence: 佢聽完之後，成個人發晒懵。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ting1 jyun4 zi1 hau6, seng4 go3 jan4 faat3 saai3 mung2.
english_sentence: After he heard that, he was completely dazed.

english: To dream (literally, to issue/emit a dream)
cantonese_sentence: 你發夢呀？唔好再講埋啲咁離譜嘅嘢啦！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 faat3 mung6 aa3? m4 hou2 zoi3 gong2 maai4 di1 gam3 lei4 pu2 ge3 je5 laa1!
english_sentence: Are you dreaming? Stop saying such outrageous things!

english: to get angry, to be angry
cantonese_sentence: 你唔好激嬲佢，佢好易發嬲㗎。
jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 gik1 nau1 keoi5, keoi5 hou2 ji6 faat3 nau1 gaa3.
english_sentence: Don't provoke him/her, he/she gets angry easily.

cantonese_sentence: BB仔成日發牙痕，咬啲嘢嚟止痕。
jyutping_sentence: BB zai2 sing4 jat6 faat3 ngaa4 han4, ngaau5 di1 je5 lai4 zi2 han4.
english_sentence: Babies often have itchy gums when teething, so they bite things to relieve the itch.

cantonese_sentence: 你又喺度發噏風，唔好再講啦。
jyutping_sentence: nei5 jau6 hai2 dou6 faat3 aap1 fung1, m4 hou2 zoi3 gong2 laa1.
english_sentence: You're talking nonsense again, stop talking.

english: To space out, daydream, be in a daze; to be a bit slow on the uptake.
cantonese_sentence: 你做咩發吽哣呀？
jyutping_sentence: nei5 zou6 me1 faat3 hong1 dau6 aa3?
english_sentence: Why are you spacing out? / What are you daydreaming about? / Why are you being so slow?

cantonese_sentence: 唔好用咁多發泡膠盒裝外賣，好唔環保㗎。
jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 yung6 gam3 do1 faat3 paau1 gaau1 hap6 zong1 ngoi6 mai6, hou2 m4 waan4 bou2 gaa3.
english_sentence: Don't use so many styrofoam boxes for takeout, it's very environmentally unfriendly.

english: To lose it, to go ballistic, to go completely mad
cantonese_sentence: 佢一聽到輸晒錢，即刻發晒茅。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat1 ting1 dou2 syu1 saai3 cin2, zik1 hak1 faat3 saai3 maau4.
english_sentence: When he heard he lost all the money, he immediately went ballistic.

cantonese_sentence: 佢啲頭髮濕嘅時候會發散開
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 di1 tau4 faat3 sap1 ge3 si4 hau6 wui5 faat3 saan3 hoi1
english_sentence: Her hair spreads out when it's wet.

english: To go crazy, to act erratically, to lose one's mind
cantonese_sentence: 你做乜嘢發神經啊？
jyutping_sentence: nei5 zou6 mat1 je5 faat3 san4 ging1 aa3?
english_sentence: What are you doing? Are you crazy?

english: First sale of the day; to open for business with a sale.
cantonese_sentence: 今日發市都未，唔知好唔好賣呢?
jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 faat3 si5 dou1 mei6, m4 zi1 hou2 m4 hou2 maai6 ne1?
english_sentence: Haven't had our first sale today, I wonder if business will be good today?

cantonese_sentence: 我琴日開始發燒，好唔舒服。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 kam4 jat6 hoi1 si2 faat3 siu1, hou2 m4 syu1 fuk6.
english_sentence: I started having a fever yesterday and feel very unwell.

cantonese_sentence: 佢係攝影發燒友，買咗好多昂貴嘅器材。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 se3 ying2 faat3 siu1 jau5, maai5 zo2 hou2 do1 ngong4 gwai3 ge3 hei3 choi4.
english_sentence: He is a photography enthusiast and has bought a lot of expensive equipment.

english: 1. Inflate, usually by adding water; 2. Overestimate, exaggerate; 3. (Food) To rehydrate dried ingredients.
cantonese_sentence: 啲豬肉發咗好多水，煮完縮到得返咁少。
jyutping_sentence: di1 zyu1 juk6 faat3 zo2 hou2 do1 seui2, zyu2 jyun4 suk1 dou3 dak1 faan1 gam3 siu2.
english_sentence: The pork inflated a lot, after cooking it shrunk and only a little bit remained.

cantonese_sentence: 香港嘅發鈔銀行有三間。
jyutping_sentence: hoeng1 gong2 ge3 faat3 caau1 ngan4 hong4 jau5 saam1 gaan1.
english_sentence: Hong Kong has three issuing banks.

english: glow green/greenish (often implying something is bad, unwell, or unnatural)
cantonese_sentence: 佢塊面發青光，睇嚟病得好犀利。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 faai3 min6 faat3 ceng1 gwong1, tai2 lai4 beng6 dak1 hou2 sai1 lei6.
english_sentence: His/Her face is glowing green; it seems like he/she is very sick.

cantonese_sentence: 佢成日諗住點樣發達，真係發錢寒。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 lam2 zyu6 dim2 joeng2 faat3 daat6, zan1 hai6 faat3 cin2 hon4.
english_sentence: He's always thinking about how to get rich, he's really money-hungry.

english: Wishing you prosperity and a flourishing business (often said during Chinese New Year)
cantonese_sentence: 新年發財好市，生意興隆!
jyutping_sentence: san1 nin4 faat3 coi4 hou2 si5, saang1 ji3 hing1 lung4!
english_sentence: Happy New Year! Wishing you prosperity, flourishing business, and thriving trade!

english: To break free, to break out of a difficult situation, to expand one's horizons
cantonese_sentence: 佢想喺新公司發圍，所以好努力做嘢。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 soeng2 hai2 san1 gung1 si1 faat3 wai4, so2 ji5 hou2 nou5 lik6 zou6 je5.
english_sentence: He wants to make a breakthrough in the new company, so he works very hard.

english: To be crazy/insane; to act foolishly; to have a tantrum; to be acting up (especially applies to children or sometimes pets)
cantonese_sentence: 你做乜嘢發瘟呀？
jyutping_sentence: nei5 zou6 mat1 je5 faat3 wan1 aa3?
english_sentence: What are you doing, acting crazy?

english: To have an epileptic seizure, to faint, or to suddenly lose consciousness
cantonese_sentence: 佢喺地鐵站突然發羊吊，嚇死人。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 dei6 tit3 zaam6 dat6 jin4 faat3 joeng4 diu3, haak3 sei2 jan4.
english_sentence: He suddenly had a seizure at the subway station, it scared people to death.

cantonese_sentence: 佢髮腳好高，好似就嚟甩頭髮噉。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 faat3 goek3 hou2 gou1, hou2 ci5 zau6 lai4 lat1 tau4 faat3 gam2.
english_sentence: His hairline is very high, it seems like he's about to lose his hair.

cantonese_sentence: 我聽日要去髮型屋剪頭髮。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ting1 jat6 jiu3 heoi3 faat3 ying4 uk1 jin2 tau4 faat3.
english_sentence: I'm going to the hair salon tomorrow to get a haircut.

cantonese_sentence: 佢戴咗個髮笠去游水。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 daai3 zo2 go3 faat3 lap1 heoi3 jau4 seoi2.
english_sentence: She wore a swimming cap to go swimming.

cantonese_sentence: 我晏晝會去髮廊剪頭髮。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 aan3 zau3 wui5 heoi3 faat3 long4-2 zin2 tau4 faat3.
english_sentence: I'm going to the hair salon to get a haircut this afternoon.

english: Hair ends (the ends of one's hair)
cantonese_sentence: 我想剪一剪啲髮尾。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 soeng2 zin2 jat1 zin2 di1 faat3 mei5.
english_sentence: I want to trim the ends of my hair a bit.

cantonese_sentence: 佢揮手同我講再見。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 fai1 sau2 tung4 ngo5 gong2 zoi3 gin3.
english_sentence: He waved his hand to say goodbye to me.

english: Lunar New Year decoration (typically red paper with auspicious phrases written on them)
cantonese_sentence: 我哋每年過年都會喺屋企門口貼揮春。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 mui5 nin4 gwo3 nin4 dou1 wui5 hai2 uk1 kei2 mun4 hau2 tip3 fai1 ceon1.
english_sentence: Every year during Lunar New Year, we paste 揮春 decorations on our home's door.

cantonese_sentence: 你咁廢嘅？乜都做唔掂！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam3 fai3 ge3? mat1 dou1 zou6 m4 dim6!
english_sentence: Are you so useless? You can't do anything right!

english: Useless youth, bum, loser (term used to describe young people perceived as lacking ambition and contributing little to society)
cantonese_sentence: 咪做個廢青，搵啲嘢做下啦！
jyutping_sentence: mai1 zou6 go3 fai3 cing1, wan2 di1 je5 zou6 haa5 laa1!
english_sentence: Don't be a useless youth, find something to do!

english: Troublesome; to go to the trouble of; not worth the effort
cantonese_sentence: 都係費事出去食飯，喺屋企煮啦。
jyutping_sentence: dou1 hai6 fai3 si6 ceot1 heoi3 sik6 faan6, hai2 uk1 kei2 zyu2 laa1.
english_sentence: It's troublesome to go out to eat, let's just cook at home.

english: dividing (something of benefit) into small portions; usually referring to benefits or profits. Often carries a negative connotation suggesting unfair or insufficient distribution.
cantonese_sentence: 啲老細成日分餅仔分到得返碎濕濕。
jyutping_sentence: di1 lou5 sai3 seng4 jat6 fan1 beng2 zai2 fan1 dou3 dak1 faan1 seoi3 sap1 sap1.
english_sentence: The boss always divides the profits into such small portions that we only get crumbs.

english: to split profits/revenue; to share the spoils
cantonese_sentence: 我哋傾掂數點樣分賬啦。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 king1 dim6 sou3 dim2 joeng2 fan1 zoeng3 laa1.
english_sentence: Let's discuss how we split the profits.

english: to take sides; to play favorites; to be biased.
cantonese_sentence: 你唔好咁分莊閒啦，對個個都公平啲咪好囉。
jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 gam3 fan1 zong1 haan4 laa1, deoi3 go3 go3 dou1 gung1 ping4 di1 mai6 hou2 lo1.
english_sentence: Don't play favorites like that, just be fairer to everyone, wouldn't that be better?

cantonese_sentence: 公司派花紅好似分豬肉咁，個個都有份。
jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 paai3 faa1 hung4 hou2 ci5 fan1 zyu1 juk6 gam2, go3 go3 dou1 jau5 fan6.
english_sentence: The company distributes bonuses like pork-barreling, everyone gets a share.

cantonese_sentence: 我分分鐘辭職
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 fan1 fan1 zung1 ci4 zik1
english_sentence: I might quit any minute now / I'm very likely to quit.

english: To share both the sweet and the bitter (i.e., to share joys and sorrows)
cantonese_sentence: 我哋係好朋友，一定會分甘同味。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 hai6 hou2 pang4 jau5, jat1 ding6 wui5 fan1 gam1 tung4 mei6.
english_sentence: We are good friends, we will definitely share both the sweet and the bitter.

cantonese_sentence: 佢哋分居咗一年幾，差唔多要離婚。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 fan1 geoi1 zo2 jat1 nin4 gei2, caa1 m4 do1 jiu3 lei4 fan1.
english_sentence: They've been separated for over a year, and are almost getting divorced.

cantonese_sentence: 我哋簽咗分居紙，準備離婚。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 cim1 zo2 fan1 geoi1 zi2, zeon2 bei6 lei4 fan1.
english_sentence: We signed a separation agreement, preparing for divorce.

english: Distributing spoils (often unfairly or in a way that benefits cronies)
cantonese_sentence: 公司年尾分豬肉，個個都有份，但係分多定分少就睇關係。
jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 nin4 mei5 fan1 zyu1 juk6, go3 go3 dou1 jau5 fan6, daan6 hai6 fan1 do1 ding6 fan1 siu2 zau6 tai2 gwaan1 hai6.
english_sentence: At the end of the year, the company distributes spoils, everyone gets a share, but whether you get a lot or a little depends on your connections.

english: Easily; very quickly; in no time; almost certainly
cantonese_sentence: 我分分鐘搞掂佢。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 fan1 fan1 zung1 gaau2 dim6 keoi5.
english_sentence: I can easily take care of him/her/it.

english: Share the sweet and the bitter; share joys and sorrows.
cantonese_sentence: 我哋一齊創業，一定要分甘同味。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 jat1 cai4 cong3 jip6, jat1 ding6 jiu3 fan1 gam1 tung4 mei6.
english_sentence: We're starting a business together, so we must share both the joys and the sorrows.

english: Separate (as in living separately from a spouse/partner)
cantonese_sentence: 佢哋感情唔好，決定咗分居。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 gam2 cing4 m4 hou2, kyut3 ding6 zo2 fan1 geoi1.
english_sentence: Their relationship wasn't good, so they decided to separate.

cantonese_sentence: 佢哋簽咗分居紙，準備離婚。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6-2 cim1 zo2 fan1 geoi1 zi2, zeon2 bei6 lyun1 fan1.
english_sentence: They signed a separation agreement, preparing for divorce.

cantonese_sentence: 佢今次考試攞到好好嘅分數。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam1 ci3 haau2 si5 lo2 dou3 hou2 hou2 ge3 fan1 sou3.
english_sentence: He/She got a very good mark/grade in the exam this time.

cantonese_sentence: 我喺街度收到一份分書，講緊新餐廳開張。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hai2 gaai1 dou6 sau1 dou2 jat1 fan6 fan1 syu1, gong2 gan2 san1 caan1 teng1 hoi1 zoeng1.
english_sentence: I received a handout on the street advertising the opening of a new restaurant.

english: to split off, to spin off, to break up (a company or organization)
cantonese_sentence: 我哋公司打算將業務分拆出嚟上市。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 gung1 si1 daa2 syun3 zoeng1 jip6 mou6 fan1 caak3 chut1 lai4 soeng5 si5.
english_sentence: Our company plans to spin off the business and list it on the stock market.

cantonese_sentence: 佢哋分咗妻好耐喇
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 fan1 zo2 cai1 hou2 noi6 laa3
english_sentence: They divorced a long time ago.

cantonese_sentence: 我沖完個分蘭浴，個人精神好多。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 cung1 jyun4 go3 fan1 laan4 yuk6, go3 jan4 zing1 san4 hou2 do1.
english_sentence: After taking a shower, I feel much more refreshed.

cantonese_sentence: 佢攞咗好多勳銜，好犀利㗎！
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 lo2 zo2 ho2 do1 hun1 haam4, hou2 sai1 lei6 gaa3!
english_sentence: He/She received many honors, very impressive!

english: powder; noodles (usually made from rice flour)
cantonese_sentence: 我想食碗牛腩河粉。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 soeng2 sik6 wun2 ngau4 naam5 ho4 fan2.
english_sentence: I want to eat a bowl of beef brisket rice noodles.

cantonese_sentence: 佢今日化咗好厚嘅粉底
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam1 jat6 faa3 zo2 hou2 hau5 ge3 fan2 dai2
english_sentence: She put on a lot of foundation today.

english: Short, thin rice noodles (often served in soup)
cantonese_sentence: 我想食碗粉仔
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 soeng2 sik6 wun2 fan2 zai2
english_sentence: I want to eat a bowl of *fan zai*.

cantonese_sentence: 呢條粉蕉好甜呀！
jyutping_sentence: ni1 tiu4 fan2 jiu1 hou2 tim4 aa3!
english_sentence: This lady finger banana is so sweet!

cantonese_sentence: 我好鍾意食粉角。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hou2 zung1 ji3 sik6 fan2 gok3.
english_sentence: I really like eating pinched noodles.

cantonese_sentence: 阿Sir寫啲字喺粉牌上面。
jyutping_sentence: aa3 sir4 se2 di1 zi6 hai2 fan2 paai4 soeng6 min6.
english_sentence: The teacher wrote some words on the chalkboard.

cantonese_sentence: 我用粉撲上粉底
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 jung6 fan2 pok3 soeng5 fan2 dai2
english_sentence: I use a powder puff to apply foundation.

cantonese_sentence: 阿婆用粉線袋裝住啲橙。
jyutping_sentence: aa3 po4 jung6 fan2 sin3 doi2 zong1 zyu6 di1 caang2.
english_sentence: The old woman is using a mesh bag to hold the oranges.

english: Rice noodle roll raft (a playful term for a lot of rice noodle rolls, suggesting they are stacked or arranged like a raft)
cantonese_sentence: 我買咗好多粉艇，真係好似一排粉艇咁。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 maai5 zo2 hou2 do1 fan2 teng5, zan1 hai6 hou2 ci5 jat1 paai4 fan2 teng5 gam2.
english_sentence: I bought a lot of rice noodle rolls, it really looks like a raft of them.

english: Eraser (often referring to a whiteboard eraser specifically)
cantonese_sentence: 你幫我攞埋個粉擦嚟。
jyutping_sentence: nei5 bong1 ngo5 lo2 maai4 go3 fan2 caat3 lei4.
english_sentence: Can you help me grab the eraser?

cantonese_sentence: 我塊面好多粉刺呀！
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 faai3 min6 hou2 do1 fan2 ci3 aa3!
english_sentence: I have a lot of pimples on my face!

english: Pig's small intestine (often stir-fried or used in congee)
cantonese_sentence: 我今日想食碟豉油王炒粉腸。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 jat6 soeng2 sik6 dip6 si6 jau4 wong4 caau2 fan2 coeng2.
english_sentence: I want to eat a plate of pig's small intestine stir-fried with soy sauce today.

cantonese_sentence: 我好眼瞓呀，想瞓覺。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hou2 ngaan5 fan3 aa3, soeng2 fan3 gaau3.
english_sentence: I'm very sleepy, I want to sleep.

english: To sleep on the street; to be homeless
cantonese_sentence: 佢冇錢交租，搞到要瞓街。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 mou5 cin2 gaau1 zou1, gaau2 dou3 jiu3 fan3 gaai1.
english_sentence: He has no money to pay rent, resulting in him having to sleep on the street.

cantonese_sentence: 我好眼瞓，想瞓覺。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hou2 ngaan5 fan3, soeng2 fan3 gaau3.
english_sentence: I'm very sleepy, I want to sleep.

cantonese_sentence: 我尋日瞓得唔好，而家瞓捩頸呀。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 cam4 jat6 fan3 dak1 m4 hou2, ji4 gaa1 fan3 lai2 geng2 aa3.
english_sentence: I didn't sleep well yesterday, and now I have a stiff neck.

english: To go all-in; to devote oneself wholeheartedly; to throw oneself into something.
cantonese_sentence: 佢今次瞓身投資落呢個項目，希望可以賺大錢。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam1 ci3 fan3 san1 tau4 zi1 lok6 ni1 go3 hong6 muk6, hei1 mong6 ho2 ji5 zaan6 daai6 cin2.
english_sentence: This time he's going all-in investing in this project, hoping to make big money.

jyutping: fan4 tau4 so2 daai6 dou1 -- haak3 gwai2
english: Showboating on a grave - scaring ghosts (meaning: a useless or pointless display)
cantonese_sentence: 你做咁多嘢都係墳頭耍大刀——嚇鬼啫!
jyutping_sentence: nei5 zou6 gam3 do1 je5 dou1 hai6 fan4 tau4 so2 daai6 dou1 -- haak3 gwai2 ze1!
english_sentence: All this work you're doing is just showboating - it's completely useless!

cantonese_sentence: 佢揈揈下個頭
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 fuk1 fuk1 haa5 go3 tau4
english_sentence: He swung his head back and forth.

cantonese_sentence: 佢忽然後退咗一步.
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 fat1 jin4 hau6 teoi3 zo2 jat1 bou6.
english_sentence: He suddenly stepped back a step.

english: Discard, throw away, to get rid of something. Often used for small, unwanted items.
cantonese_sentence: 唔要嘅嘢就㧾咗佢啦！
jyutping_sentence: m4 jiu3 ge3 je5 zau6 lut1 zo2 keoi5 laa1!
english_sentence: Throw away the things you don't want!

cantonese_sentence: 佢喺個窿窟度匿埋。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 go3 lung1 fat1 dou6 nik1 maai4.

cantonese_sentence: 今晚飲嘅係金山翅，唔係真翅。
jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 jam2 ge3 hai6 gam1 saan1 ci3, m4 hai6 zan1 ci3.
english_sentence: Tonight we're having imitation shark fin soup, not real shark fin.

jyutping: gam1 sau2 zi2 - duk1 jan4 bui3 zek3
english: Backstabber; someone who betrays or undermines others behind their back. (Note: 金手指 usually refers to "golden finger," meaning a Midas touch or someone lucky/skilled, but combined with 篤人背脊, it creates this specific meaning)
cantonese_sentence: 阿明成日金手指——篤人背脊，所以冇人信佢。
jyutping_sentence: a3 ming4 sing4 jat6 gam1 sau2 zi2 - duk1 jan4 bui3 zek3, so2 ji5 mou5 jan4 seon3 keoi5.
english_sentence: Ah Ming is always backstabbing people, so nobody trusts him.

english: Money; funds (often referring to available financial resources)
cantonese_sentence: 我哋公司最近金水唔夠，可能要裁員。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 gung1 si1 zeoi3 gan6 gam1 seoi2 m4 gau3, ho2 nang4 jiu3 coi4 jyun4.
english_sentence: Our company doesn't have enough money recently, we might have to lay off staff.

cantonese_sentence: 過咗身之後，屋企人會將佢嘅骨灰放入金塔。
jyutping_sentence: gwo3 zo2 san1 zi1 hau6, uk1 kei5 jan4 wui2 zoeng1 keoi5 ge3 gwat1 fui1 fong3 jap6 gam1 taap3.
english_sentence: After someone passes away, their family will put their ashes into a cremation urn.

cantonese_sentence: 我細個嘅時候好鍾意食金錢餅。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 sai3 go3 ge3 si4 hau6 hou2 zung1 ji3 sik6 gam1 cin4 beng2.
english_sentence: When I was a child, I really liked to eat golden coin cookies.

cantonese_sentence: 佢攞咗好多金唱片獎。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 lo2 zo2 hou2 do1 gam1 cheung3 pin2 zoeng2.
english_sentence: He/She has won many Gold Record awards.

cantonese_sentence: 呢個生果好甘。
jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 sang1 gwo2 hou2 gam1.
english_sentence: This fruit is very sweet.

cantonese_sentence: 我今日買咗幾條甘筍煮餸。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 jat6 maai5 zo2 gei2 tiu4 gam1 syun2 zyu2 sung3.
english_sentence: I bought a few carrots today to cook with.

cantonese_sentence: 佢做咗甘草演員好多年喇。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 zo2 gam1 cou2 jin2 jyun4 hou2 do1 nin4 laa3.
english_sentence: He's been a character actor for many years.

cantonese_sentence: 噉咪得囉!
jyutping_sentence: gam2 mai1 dak1 lo1!
english_sentence: Then that's fine!

english: Like this; in this way; this way
cantonese_sentence: 你唔可以噉樣做嘢㗎。
jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 ho2 ji5 gam2 joeng2 zou6 je5 gaa3.
english_sentence: You can't do things this way.

english: To influence (someone) for the better; to reform
cantonese_sentence: 我哋希望可以感化到佢，令佢唔好再做壞事。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 hei1 mong6 ho2 ji5 gam2 faa3 dou3 keoi5, ling6 keoi5 m4 hou2 zoi3 zou6 waai6 si6.
english_sentence: We hope we can influence him for the better, so he won't do bad things again.

cantonese_sentence: 佢後生嗰陣犯過事，依家社署派咗個感化官跟佢。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hau6 saang1 go2 zan6 faan6 gwo3 si6, ji1 gaa1 se5 cyu5 paai3 zo2 go3 gam2 faa3 gun1 gan1 keoi5.
english_sentence: He committed a crime when he was young, and now the Social Welfare Department has assigned him a probation officer.

cantonese_sentence: 佢衰到入咗感化院。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seoi1 dou3 jap6 zo2 gam2 faa3 yun2.
english_sentence: He was so bad he ended up in reform school.

cantonese_sentence: 今日咁熱，小心感暑呀！
jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 gam3 jit6, siu2 sam1 gam2 syu2 aa3!
english_sentence: It's so hot today, be careful of getting heatstroke!

cantonese_sentence: 咁樣做唔係幾好喎。
jyutping_sentence: gam2 joeng2 zou6 m4 hai6 gei2 hou2 wo3.
english_sentence: Doing it like this isn't very good.

english: A lot; a great deal; quite a bit
cantonese_sentence: 我仲有咁大把嘢要做。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zung6 jau5 gam3 daai6 baa2 je5 jiu3 zou6.
english_sentence: I still have a lot of things to do.

english: Almost; practically; pretty much; close to
cantonese_sentence: 我頭先飲咗兩罐啤酒，有啲醉咁滯。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 tau4 sin1 jam2 zo2 loeng5 gun3 be1 zau2, jau5 di1 zeoi3 gam2 zai6.
english_sentence: I drank two cans of beer earlier, I'm almost drunk.

english: So tall and big / So big (emphasizing height and size)
cantonese_sentence: 佢而家變得咁高咁大喇！
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ji4 gaa1 bin3 dak1 gam3 gou1 gam3 daai6 laa3!
english_sentence: He's become so tall and big now!

cantonese_sentence: 我申請咗張禁區紙，可以入去嗰度做嘢。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 san1 cing2 zo2 zoeng1 gam3 keoi1 zi2, ho2 ji5 jap6 heoi3 go2 dou6 zou6 je5.
english_sentence: I applied for a restricted area permit so I can go in there to work.

cantonese_sentence: 撳個掣 | gam6 go3 zai3
jyutping_sentence: Press the button.
english_sentence: gam6 go3 zai3 | Press the button

english: Floor Swimming (pretending to swim on the floor)
cantonese_sentence: 你唔好喺度撳地游水啦，起身做功課！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 hai2 dou6 gam6 dei6 jau4 seoi2 laa1, hei2 san1 zou6 gung1 fo3!
english_sentence: Don't pretend to swim on the floor, get up and do your homework!

english: To thumb-tack, to pin (with a thumb-tack)
cantonese_sentence: 我用撳釘將張poster 撳喺牆上面。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 jung6 gam6 ding1 zoeng1 zoeng1 poster gam6 hai2 coeng4 soeng6 min6.
english_sentence: I used thumb-tacks to pin the poster on the wall.

cantonese_sentence: BB好鍾意我撳鷓鴣佢㗎。
jyutping_sentence: bi1 bi1 hou2 zung1 ji3 ngo5 gam6 zuk1 gu1 keoi5 gaa3.
english_sentence: The baby really likes me to play peek-a-boo with them.

english: To press the doorbell/ring a bell
cantonese_sentence: 麻煩你撳鐘通知佢落嚟啦。
jyutping_sentence: maa4 faan4 nei5 gam6 zung1 tung1 zi1 keoi5 lok6 lai4 laa1.
english_sentence: Please ring the bell to let him know to come down.

english: Hold someone's head down; Hold someone back (metaphorically)
cantonese_sentence: 佢成日撳住頭唔俾我出頭
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 gam6 zyu6 tau4 m4 bei2 ngo5 ceot1 tau4
english_sentence: He always holds me back and doesn't let me get ahead.

cantonese_sentence: 我去撳機攞錢。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 heoi3 gam6 gei1 lo2 cin2.
english_sentence: I'm going to use the ATM to withdraw money.

cantonese_sentence: 我跟佢一齊去睇戲
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gan1 keoi5 jat1 cai4 heoi3 tai2 hei3
english_sentence: I'm going to the movies with him/her.

cantonese_sentence: 我哋跟大隊去食飯啦。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 gan1 daai6 deoi2 heoi3 sik6 faan6 laa1.
english_sentence: Let's follow the group to eat.

english: A wife who always follows her husband around, sometimes to an excessive or bothersome degree. Often used to describe a clingy or possessive wife.
cantonese_sentence: 佢老婆好跟得夫人㗎，去邊都要跟住佢。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 lou5 po2 hou2 gan1 dak1 fu4 yan2 gaa3, heoi3 bin1 dou6 dou1 jiu3 gan1 zoek6 keoi5.
english_sentence: His wife is very much a "跟得夫人", she has to follow him everywhere he goes.

cantonese_sentence: 我會跟進呢件事。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 wui5 gan1 zeon3 ni1 gin6 si6.
english_sentence: I will follow up on this matter.

english: To follow the trend; jump on the bandwagon
cantonese_sentence: 好多人都跟風去日本旅行。
jyutping_sentence: hou2 do1 jan4 dou1 gan1 fung1 heoi3 jat6 bun2 leoi5 hang4.
english_sentence: Many people are following the trend to travel to Japan.

english: To keep an eye on; to supervise briefly.
cantonese_sentence: 你幫我跟下眼啲嘢，我出去一陣。
jyutping_sentence: nei5 bong1 ngo5 gan1 haa5 ngaan5 di1 je5, ngo5 cheot1 heoi3 jat1 zan6.
english_sentence: Help me keep an eye on things; I'll be back in a moment.

english: To be opportunistic; to side with the powerful or popular; to be a bandwagoner
cantonese_sentence: 佢呢個人最鍾意跟紅頂白，邊個得勢就黐邊個。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ni1 go3 jan4 zeoi3 zung1 ji3 gan1 hung4 ding2 baak6, bin1 go3 dak1 sai3 zau6 ci1 bin1 go3.
english_sentence: This person is the most opportunistic, whoever is powerful he sticks to them.

english: To be with a Western man (often with romantic or sexual implications; can carry a negative connotation depending on context)
cantonese_sentence: 佢成日跟佬去蒲。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 gan1 lou2 heoi3 pou4.
english_sentence: She often goes out partying with Western men.

english: To follow closely behind; to tag along
cantonese_sentence: 佢成日跟尾，好煩呀！
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 gan1 mei5, hou2 faan4 aa3!
english_sentence: He/She always tags along, it's so annoying!

cantonese_sentence: 你唔好做跟尾狗啦，自己諗下計仔啦。
jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zou6 gan1 mei5 gau2 laa1, zi6 gei2 nam2 haa5 gai3 zai2 laa1.
english_sentence: Don't be a tag-along, think of a plan yourself.

cantonese_sentence: 我煮完飯跟手就洗碗。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zyu2 jyun4 faan6 gan1 sau2 zau6 sai2 wun2.
english_sentence: I'll wash the dishes immediately after finishing cooking.

english: to tidy up, to clear up after someone, to handle the aftermath of something
cantonese_sentence: 你做嘢唔好咁求其啦，要跟手尾㗎！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 zou6 je5 m4 hou2 gam3 kau4 kei4 laa1, jiu3 gan1 sau2 mei1 gaa3!
english_sentence: Don't be so careless when you do things, you need to tidy up after yourself!

english: To follow, to track down, to trace
cantonese_sentence: 警察跟尋咗成個禮拜，終於捉到個賊。
jyutping_sentence: ging2 caat3 gan1 cam4 zo2 sing4 go3 lai5 baai1, zung1 jyu1 zuk1 dou2 go3 caak6.
english_sentence: The police tracked [him] for a whole week, and finally caught the thief.

english: tightly, urgent, in the process of
cantonese_sentence: 我趕緊做緊功課。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gon2 gan2 zou6 gan2 gung1 fo3.
english_sentence: I'm hurrying to do my homework.

english: Worrywart; someone who easily gets nervous or anxious.
cantonese_sentence: 佢考試之前成日都好似緊張大師咁。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 haau2 si5 zi1 cin4 seng4 jat6 dou1 hou2 ci5 gan2 zoeng1 daai6 si1 gam2.

cantonese_sentence: 聽日考試，溫書好緊要㗎！
jyutping_sentence: ting1 jat6 haau2 si3, wan1 syu1 hou2 gan2 jiu3 gaa3!
english_sentence: There's an exam tomorrow, studying is very important!

cantonese_sentence: 條褲太細，着到緊捋捋。
jyutping_sentence: tiu4 fu3 taai3 sai3, zoek3 dou3 gan2 lut1 lut1.

cantonese_sentence: 呢條褲好緊身，著得唔舒服。

english_sentence: These pants are very tight-fitting, they're not comfortable to wear.

cantonese_sentence: 我哋有緊事要傾。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 jau5 gan2 si6 jiu3 king1.
english_sentence: We have an important matter to discuss.

cantonese_sentence: 我近住間銀行住。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gan6 zyu6 gaan1 ngan4 hong4 zyu6.
english_sentence: I live near the bank.

cantonese_sentence: 佢近身保護個總統。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gan6 san1 bou2 wu6 go3 zung2 tung2.
english_sentence: He protects the president at close quarters.

english: Female close friend, confidante (often implying a deep, possibly romantic, connection)
cantonese_sentence: 佢係我嘅近身妹，咩心事都同佢講。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 ngo5 ge3 gan6 san1 mui2, me1 sam1 si6 dou1 tung4 keoi5 gong2.
english_sentence: She's my close female friend, I tell her everything.

english: "Near the kitchen, you get food"; proximity to a resource allows you to benefit from it.

cantonese_sentence: 我好鍾意飲粟米羹。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hou2 zung1 ji3 jam2 suk1 mai5 gang1.
english_sentence: I really like drinking corn soup.

cantonese_sentence: 我梗係會幫你啦!
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gang2 hai6 wui2 bong1 nei5 laa1!
english_sentence: Of course I will help you!

jyutping_sentence: keoi5 go3 jan4 hou2 gang2 baan2, m4 sik1 bin3 tung1 ge3.
english_sentence: He's a very inflexible person, he doesn't know how to be adaptable.

english: Private Room (usually in a karaoke or restaurant)

jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 gam1 maan5 heoi3 coeng3 K jiu3 buk1 ding6 gaan1 gaang2 fong2.
english_sentence: We need to book a private room for karaoke tonight.

cantonese_sentence: 佢個人好梗頸，講極都唔聽。

english_sentence: He is very stubborn, he won't listen no matter how much you tell him.

jyutping_sentence: lou5 sai3 gam2 do1 nin4 dou1 gaang2 san1, zan1 hai6 hou2 gu1 hon1!

cantonese_sentence: 你部電話壞咗，不如更之部新嘅啦。

english_sentence: Your phone is broken, why not replace it with a new one?

cantonese_sentence: 唔該，幫我叫白車，好急呀!

english_sentence: Excuse me, please call an ambulance for me, it's very urgent!

english: Hasty plan; ad-hoc solution; a quick fix.
cantonese_sentence: 佢哋臨急臨忙諗咗個急計出嚟應付。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 lam4 gap1 lam4 mong4 nam2 zo2 go3 gap1 gai3 chut1 lai4 ying3 fu6.
english_sentence: They hastily came up with a quick fix to deal with it.

cantonese_sentence: 佢急急腳走咗，唔知趕去邊。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gap1 gap1 goek3 zau2 zo2, m4 zi1 gon2 heoi3 bin1.
english_sentence: He left in a hurry, I don't know where he was rushing off to.

english: Hastily, hurriedly, speaking quickly. Often implies a slightly anxious or rushed tone.
cantonese_sentence: 佢急急口咁講完就走咗。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gap1 gap1 hau2 gam2 gong2 jyun4 zau6 zau2 zo2.
english_sentence: He spoke quickly and hastily and then left.

cantonese_sentence: 你唔好咁急驚啦，慢慢嚟啦。
jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 gam3 gap1 geng1 laa1, maan6 maan2 lai4 laa1.
english_sentence: Don't be so anxious, take it easy.

cantonese_sentence: 佢成日都講唔掂急口令。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 dou1 gong2 m4 dim6 gap1 hau2 ling6.
english_sentence: He always can't say tongue twisters properly.

cantonese_sentence: 我阿嫲話蛤蚧對醫哮喘好有效。

cantonese_sentence: 我琴日喺海灘執到好多蛤𧊅。

english: Frog, or a greedy person who wants to take advantage of others (often used as "frog wanting to eat swan meat" meaning someone with unrealistic ambitions).
cantonese_sentence: 佢想溝嗰個女仔靚到蛤乸隨時想踎低.
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 soeng2 kau1 go2 go3 neoi5 zai2 leng3 dou3 gap3 naa2 ceoi4 si4 soeng2 mau1 dai1.
english_sentence: The girl he wants to get with is so beautiful that even a frog would instantly want to prostrate itself (i.e. she is so beautiful, even the most unlikely admirer would be captivated).

english: To stare, to ogle, to gaze intently
cantonese_sentence: 佢一路行一路𥄫女仔。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat1 lou6 haang4 jat1 lou6 lam1 neoi5 zai2.
english_sentence: He was staring at girls the whole way.

english: To stare at something/someone with intention, often with a scrutinizing or lecherous look.
cantonese_sentence: 你唔好咁𥄫嘢啦，好核突呀！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 gam2 ngam6 je5 laa1, hou2 hat6 dat6 aa3!
english_sentence: Don't stare like that, it's disgusting!

cantonese_sentence: 新年流流，講啲吉利嘢啦！
jyutping_sentence: san1 nin4 lau4 lau4, gong2 di1 gat1 lei6 je5 laa1!
english_sentence: It's the New Year, say some auspicious things!

cantonese_sentence: 我想食吉列豬扒飯。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 soeng2 sik6 gat1 lit6 zyu1 pa1 faan6.
english_sentence: I want to eat a breaded pork cutlet rice.

english: Custard; also refers to the filling inside a Pineapple Bun (菠蘿包)
cantonese_sentence: 我想買個吉士包。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 soeng2 maai5 go3 gat1 si6-2 baau1.
english_sentence: I want to buy a custard bun.

cantonese_sentence: 我好鍾意食桔。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hou2 zung1 ji3 sik6 gat1.
english_sentence: I really like to eat tangerines/oranges.

english: cut with a sharp instrument; slice (often implies a single, quick action)
cantonese_sentence: 佢一刀㓤落去。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat1 dou1 gwaat3 lok6 heoi3.
english_sentence: He sliced down with a knife.

cantonese_sentence: 佢俾人㓤喉，死咗喇。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 bei2 jan4 gat6 hau4, sei2 zo2 laa3.
english_sentence: He had his throat slit and died.

cantonese_sentence: 佢成日都趷高睇演唱會
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 dou1 gat6 gou1 tai2 jin2 coeng3 wui2
english_sentence: She always stands on tiptoes to watch concerts.

cantonese: 趷起條尾就知你屙屎定屙尿
jyutping: gat1 hei2 tiu4 mei1 zau6 zi1 nei5 o1 si2 ding6 o1 niu6

cantonese_sentence: 你唔好喺度扮嘢啦，趷起條尾就知你屙屎定屙尿！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 hai2 dou6 baan6 je5 laa1, gat1 hei2 tiu4 mei1 zau6 zi1 nei5 o1 si2 ding6 o1 niu6!

english: To walk on tiptoes, to tip-toe
cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺屋企趷路，唔知做乜鬼。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 hai2 uk1 kei2 gat6 lou6, m4 zi1 zou6 mat1 gwai2.
english_sentence: He/She is always tip-toeing around at home, I don't know what he/she is doing.

english: To stand on tiptoes; To crane one's neck
cantonese_sentence: 佢趷高個頭想睇吓發生咩事。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gat6 gou1 go3 tau4 soeng2 tai2 haa5 faat3 sang1 me1 si6.
english_sentence: He stood on tiptoes/craned his neck to see what happened.
