cantonese_sentence: 佢嘅腳板堂好痕。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ge3 geok3 baan2 tong4 hou2 han4.
english_sentence: The soles of his/her feet are very itchy.

english: To be clumsy, to be uncoordinated (especially with one's legs/feet)
cantonese_sentence: 佢個人好腳綁，成日撞到嘢。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 go3 jan4 hou2 goek3 bong2, seng4 jat6 zong6 dou3 je5.
english_sentence: He/She is very clumsy and always bumps into things.

cantonese_sentence: 你嘅腳帶鬆咗，快啲綁返好佢啦。
jyutping_sentence: nei5 ge3 goek3 daai2 sung1 zo2, faai3 di1 bong2 faan1 hou2 keoi5 laa1.
english_sentence: Your shoelace is loose, quickly tie it back up.

cantonese_sentence: 我對高踭鞋刮到我隻腳踭好痛。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 deoi3 gou1 zaang1 haai4 gwaat3 dou3 ngo5 zek3 goek3 zaang1 hou2 tung3.
english_sentence: My high heels are rubbing and making my heel very painful.

cantonese_sentence: 踩腳掣停車
jyutping_sentence: caai2 goek3 zai3 ting4 ce1
english_sentence: Step on the brake to stop the car.

cantonese_sentence: 我唔小心踢到枱腳，痛到我嘅腳趾公。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 siu2 sam1 tek3 dou2 toi2 goek3, tung3 dou3 ngo5 ge3 goek3 zi2 gung1.
english_sentence: I accidentally kicked the table leg, my big toe hurts so much.

cantonese_sentence: 我唔鍾意啲沙痴住喺腳趾罅。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 zung1 ji3 di1 saa1 ci1 zyu6 hai2 goek3 zi2 laa3.
english_sentence: I don't like sand sticking between my toes.

cantonese_sentence: 唔小心撞到櫃桶，隻腳趾尾好痛啊！
jyutping_sentence: m4 siu2 sam1 zong6 dou3 gwai6 tung2, zek3 geok3 zi2 mei1 hou2 tung3 aa3!
english_sentence: I accidentally bumped into the drawer, my little toe really hurts!

cantonese_sentence: 佢踢波啲腳法好鬼勁!
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 tek3 bo1 di1 goek3 faat3 hou2 gwai2 ging6!
english_sentence: His footwork in soccer is really awesome!

cantonese_sentence: 佢嘅腳甲好長，要剪喇。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ge3 goek3 gaap3 hou2 coeng4, jiu3 zin2 laa1.
english_sentence: His/Her toenails are very long, needs to be cut.

cantonese_sentence: 我扭親隻腳骹，好痛呀！
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 nau2 can1 zek3 goek3 gaau3, hou2 tung3 aa3!
english_sentence: I twisted my ankle, it really hurts!

cantonese_sentence: 隻狗嘅腳爪好污糟。
jyutping_sentence: zek3 gau2 ge3 goek3 zaau2 hou2 wu1 zou1.
english_sentence: The dog's paws are very dirty.

english: Chicken feet with black bean sauce
cantonese_sentence: 我喺飲茶嘅時候最鍾意食豉汁蒸鳳爪呀。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hai2 jam2 caa4 ge3 si4 hau6 zeoi3 zung1 ji3 sik6 si6 zap1 zing1 fung6 zaau2 aa3.
english_sentence: When I have dim sum, my favorite thing to eat is steamed chicken feet with black bean sauce.

english: Leg bones; ability to walk/move around
cantonese_sentence: 佢行路唔方便，因為啲腳骨唔好。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 haang4 lou6 m4 fong1 bin6, jan1 wai6 di1 goek3 gwat1 m4 hou2.
english_sentence: He has difficulty walking because his leg bones are not good.

cantonese_sentence: 佢行山好有腳骨力，成日都行最遠嗰條路線。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 haang4 saan1 hou2 jau5 goek3 gwat1 lik6, seng4 jat6 dou1 haang4 zeoi3 jyun5 go2 tiu4 lou6 sin3.
english_sentence: He has good stamina for hiking, always taking the longest route.

cantonese_sentence: 佢對波鞋著咗成年都冇洗，真係好腳香。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 deoi3 bo1 haai1 zoek3 zo2 sing4 nin4 dou1 mou5 sai2, zan1 hai6 hou2 goek3 hoeng1.
english_sentence: He's worn those sneakers for a year without washing them, they really have foot odor.

english: Legs feel weak/wobbly, legs giving out
cantonese_sentence: 行咗咁耐，我開始有啲腳軟喇。
jyutping_sentence: haang4 zo2 gam3 noi6, ngo5 hoi1 chi2 jau5 di1 goek3 jyun5 laa3.
english_sentence: I've been walking for so long, my legs are starting to feel a bit weak.

cantonese_sentence: 坐低擘大隻腳，擺個腳橋。
jyutping_sentence: zo6 dai1 maak3 daai6 zek3 goek3, baai2 go3 goek3 kiu2.
english_sentence: Sit down with your legs spread wide and make a criss-cross applesauce (position).

cantonese_sentence: 我踢波踢到腳面都腫咗
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 tek3 bo1 tek3 dou3 goek3 min6 dou1 zung2 zo2
english_sentence: I played soccer so much that my instep is swollen.

cantonese_sentence: 扭親隻腳眼好痛呀！
jyutping_sentence: nau2 can1 zek3 goek3 ngaan5 hou2 tung3 aa3!
english_sentence: I sprained my ankle, it really hurts!

cantonese_sentence: 我踢波踢到腳坳咗。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 tek3 bo1 tek3 dou3 goek3 au3 zo2.
english_sentence: I sprained my ankle playing football.

cantonese_sentence: 我行咗成日路，而家腳肚好攰。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 haang4 zo2 seng4 jat6 lou6, ji4 gaa1 goek3 tou5 hou2 gui6.
english_sentence: I walked all day, now my calves are very tired.

jyutping: goeng1 taai3 gung1 fung1 san4 – lau6 zo2 zi6 gei2
english: Jiang Taigong appointing gods – forgetting himself (a figure of speech for someone who is so busy or focused on helping others that they forget to take care of themselves)
cantonese_sentence: 佢成日幫人，到頭來薑太公封神——漏咗自己，自己都病埋。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 bong1 jan4, dou3 tau4 loi4 goeng1 taai3 gung1 fung1 san4 – lau6 zo2 zi6 gei2, zi6 gei2 dou1 beng6 maai4.
english_sentence: He always helps others, and in the end, like Jiang Taigong forgetting himself, he even got sick himself.

english: Ginger Vinegar (a traditional Cantonese dish eaten after childbirth, believed to help restore the mother's health)
cantonese_sentence: 我阿媽啱啱生完BB，日日都食薑醋。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 aa3 maa1 ngaam1 ngaam1 saang1 jyun4 be1 bi1, jat6 jat6 dou1 sik6 goeng1 zoek3.
english_sentence: My mother just gave birth to a baby, and she eats ginger vinegar every day.

english: Ginger and vinegar trotters (a Cantonese dish traditionally eaten to celebrate a baby's first month)
cantonese_sentence: 我阿媽煲咗好多薑醋，派比親戚朋友。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 aa3 maa1 bou1 zo2 ho2 do1 goeng1 cou3, paai3 bei2 can1 cik1 pang4 jau5.
english_sentence: My mom cooked a lot of ginger and vinegar trotters and distributed it to relatives and friends.

cantonese_sentence: 今日好焗聲呀！
jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 hou2 guk6 seng1 aa3!
english_sentence: It's so stifling hot today!

english: Right of abode in the UK (literally: reside-England-right)
cantonese_sentence: 好多香港人因為政治因素而申請居英權。
jyutping_sentence: hou2 do1 hoeng1 gong2 jan4 jan1 wai6 zing3 chi5 jyun4 sok3 ji4 san1 cing2 geoi1 jing1 kyun4.
english_sentence: Many Hongkongers applied for right of abode in the UK due to political factors.

cantonese_sentence: 我哋抽到居屋喇!
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 cau1 dou2 geoi1 uk1 laa3!
english_sentence: We got a Home Ownership Scheme flat!

cantonese_sentence: 佢阿爺以前喺英軍做啹喀兵。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 aa3 je4 ji5 cin4 hai2 jing1 gwan1 zou6 guk1 gaak3 bing1.
english_sentence: His grandfather used to be a Gurkha soldier in the British Army.

english: To report (a crime, wrongdoing, etc.), to inform on
cantonese_sentence: 佢舉報咗佢老闆貪污。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 geoi2 bou3 zo2 keoi5 lou5 baan2 taam1 wu1.
english_sentence: He reported his boss for corruption.

english: To wholeheartedly agree; to give something a resounding endorsement
cantonese_sentence: 我舉腳贊成你嘅建議。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 geoi2 goek3 zaan3 sing4 nei5 ge3 gin3 ji5.
english_sentence: I wholeheartedly agree with your suggestion.

cantonese_sentence: 我等咗你成個句鐘喇！
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dang2 zo2 nei5 sing4 go3 geoi3 zung1 laa3!
english_sentence: I've been waiting for you for a whole hour!

english: Huge, gigantic; often refers to a Big Mac
cantonese_sentence: 我啱啱食咗個巨無霸，飽到行唔郁。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ngaam1 ngaam1 sik6 zo2 go3 geoi6 mou4 baa3, baau2 dou3 haang4 m4 juk1.
english_sentence: I just ate a Big Mac, I'm so full I can't walk.

english: Deserving of bad luck; serves you right (usually said with annoyance)
cantonese_sentence: 你唔聽人講，而家衰咗，該衰啦！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 ting1 jan4 gong2, ji4 gaa1 seoi1 zo2, gaai1 seoi1 laa1!
english_sentence: You didn't listen to what people said, and now you're in trouble, serves you right!

english: Serves you right; good riddance (often with a feeling of schadenfreude). Note: can be quite harsh.
cantonese_sentence: 佢抵死，該煨啦！
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dai2 si2, goi1 wai1 laa1!
english_sentence: He deserved it, serves him right!

cantonese_sentence: 我想改名做Mary。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 soeng2 goi2 ming2 zou6 Mary.
english_sentence: I want to change my name to Mary.

english: Beauty is in the eye of the beholder.
cantonese_sentence: 佢咁都覺得靚，真係各花入各眼喇。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam2 dou1 gok3 dak1 leng3, zan1 hai6 gok3 faa1 jap6 gok3 ngaan5 laa3.
english_sentence: He/She even thinks that's beautiful, it really is beauty in the eye of the beholder.

cantonese_sentence: 今次比賽咁難，大家唯有各施各法啦。
jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 bei2 coi3 gam3 naan4, daai6 ga1 wai4 jau5 gok3 si1 gok3 faat3 laa1.
english_sentence: This competition is so difficult, everyone can only use their own methods.

english: Each finds its own niche; everyone fits in where they belong.
cantonese_sentence: 呢個世界就係各適其適，唔需要強求。
jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 sai3 gaai3 zau6 hai6 gok3 sik1 kei4 sik1, m4 seoi1 jiu3 koeng5 kiu4.
english_sentence: This world is about everyone finding their niche, there's no need to force things.

jyutping: gok3 cyu3 hoeng1 cyun1 gok3 cyu3 lai6
cantonese_sentence: 你都唔好咁執著啦，各處鄉村各處例嚟㗎嘛。
jyutping_sentence: nei5 dou1 m4 hou2 gam3 zap1 zoek6 laa1, gok3 cyu3 hoeng1 cyun1 gok3 cyu3 lai6 lai4 gaa3 maa3.
english_sentence: Don't be so fixated, different places have different customs.

cantonese_sentence: 呢個角頭好多人
jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 gok3 tau4 hou2 do1 jan4
english_sentence: This corner has a lot of people.

english: Little fried dumpling (often made during Lunar New Year)
cantonese_sentence: 今年屋企整咗好多角仔
jyutping_sentence: gam1 nin4 uk1 kei2 zing2 zo2 hou2 do1 gok3 zai2
english_sentence: This year, my family made a lot of little fried dumplings.

cantonese_sentence: 我喺角落頭度搵到我本漫畫。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hai2 gok3 lok6 tau2 dou6 wan2 dou3 ngo5 bun2 maan6 waa2.
english_sentence: I found my comic book in the corner.

cantonese_sentence: 啲嘢放喺閣仔度。
jyutping_sentence: di1 je5 fong3 hai2 gok3 zai2 dou6.
english_sentence: The things are put in the attic.

english: Uncomfortable to look at; Visually displeasing; Offputting to the eye
cantonese_sentence: 佢件衫嘅顏色好覺眼。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gin6 saam1 ge3 ngaan5 sik1 hou2 gok3 ngaan5.
english_sentence: The colors of her shirt are very visually displeasing.

cantonese_sentence: 佢好鍾意夜晚飲杯干邑
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hou2 zung1 ji3 je6 maan5 jam2 bui1 gon1 jaap1
english_sentence: He likes to drink a glass of Cognac at night.

cantonese_sentence: 條毛巾仲係濕嘅，攞去曬乾佢啦。
jyutping_sentence: tiu4 mou1 gan1 zung6 hai6 sap1 ge3, lo2 heoi3 saai3 gon1 keoi5 laa1.
english_sentence: The towel is still wet, take it out to dry it.

english: Dry winter, wet year (meaning a dry winter typically presages a rainy/wet year)
cantonese_sentence: 今年乾東濕年，聽日落狗屎都唔出奇。
jyutping_sentence: gam1 nin4 gon1 dung1 sap1 nin4, ting1 jat6 lok6 gau2 si2 dou1 m4 ceot1 kei4.
english_sentence: This year is a dry winter, wet year, it wouldn't be surprising if it rained cats and dogs tomorrow.

english: Dry and stiff; lacking moisture; often used to describe food that is overcooked or clothing that is overly starched.
cantonese_sentence: 呢嚿叉燒乾朾朾，一啲都唔好食。
jyutping_sentence: ni1 gau6 caa1 siu1 gon1 caang1 caang1, jat1 di1 dou1 m4 hou2 sik6.
english_sentence: This piece of char siu is dry and stiff, not delicious at all.

english: Clean and tidy; spick and span
cantonese_sentence: 間房要保持乾淨企理呀！
jyutping_sentence: gaan1 fong2 jiu3 bou2 ci4 gon1 zing6 kei5 lei5 aa3!
english_sentence: The room needs to be kept clean and tidy!

cantonese_sentence: 我用乾瑤柱煲粥，好鮮味㗎！
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 yung6 gon1 jiu4 zyu2 bou1 zuk1, hou2 sin1 mei6 gaa3!
english_sentence: I used dried scallops to cook congee, it's very delicious!

english: To swallow dryly; to choke on something dry because of lack of saliva or liquid to help it go down.
cantonese_sentence: 我食緊塊餅乾太乾，乾哽咗一下。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 sik6 gan2 faai3 beng2 gon1 taai3 gon1, gon1 gang2 zo2 jat1 haa5.
english_sentence: I was eating a biscuit that was too dry and I choked on it a little (swallowed it dryly).

english: Dry and difficult to swallow; choking
cantonese_sentence: 啲餅乾好乾骾骾，飲啖水先。
jyutping_sentence: di1 beng2 gon1 hou2 gon1 gang2 gang2, yam2 daam6 seoi2 sin1.
english_sentence: These crackers are very dry and hard to swallow, drink some water first.

english: A meager or paltry gift; a gift given without sincerity.
cantonese_sentence: 我唔想要佢啲乾禮，擺明係敷衍我啫。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 soeng2 jiu3 keoi5 di1 gon1 lai5, baai2 ming4 hai6 fu1 jin2 ngo5 ze1.
english_sentence: I don't want his meager gifts; it's clearly just a formality to appease me.

cantonese_sentence: 我沖完涼要抺乾身先出嚟。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 cung1 jyun4 loeng4 jiu3 maat3 gon1 san1 sin1 ceot1 lai4.
english_sentence: I need to dry myself after showering before coming out.

cantonese_sentence: 今日落雨，記得着返件乾濕褸啊！
jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 lok6 jyu5, gei3 dak1 zoek3 faan1 gin6 gon1 sap1 lau1 aa3!
english_sentence: It's raining today, remember to put on your trench coat!

english: To do something quickly and cleanly, without leaving a mess or any lingering issues; to be efficient and decisive.
cantonese_sentence: 佢做事乾手淨腳，好可靠㗎。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 si6 gon1 sau2 zeng6 goek3, hou2 ho2 kaau3 gaa3.
english_sentence: He/She does things quickly and efficiently, very reliable.

cantonese_sentence: 我尋日炒股炒到乾塘。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 cam4 jat6 caau2 gu2 caau2 dou3 gon1 tong4.
english_sentence: I lost all my money on stocks yesterday.

cantonese_sentence: 我想食乾炒牛河。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 soeng2 sik6 gon1 caau2 ngau4 ho2.
english_sentence: I want to eat dry-fried beef noodles.

english: Pig Herder, someone who is out of touch, behind the times. (Figuratively used to describe someone naive or unaware.)
cantonese_sentence: 你咁講嘢，成個趕豬郎咁！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam2 gong2 je5, seng4 go3 gon2 jyu1 long4 gam2!
english_sentence: Talking like that, you sound like a real pig herder (naive)!

cantonese_sentence: 我趕住返工，唔得閒同你傾偈。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gon2 zyu6 faan1 gung1, m4 dak1 haan4 tung4 nei5 king1 gai2.
english_sentence: I'm in a hurry to go to work, I don't have time to chat with you.

english: In a big rush to reincarnate (implying someone is rushing around recklessly and might die soon)
cantonese_sentence: 你趕住去投胎呀？行慢啲啦！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 gon2 zyu6 heoi3 tau4 toi1 aa3? haang4 maan6 di1 laa1!
english_sentence: Are you rushing to reincarnate? Walk slower!

cantonese_sentence: 唔好咁趕急，慢慢嚟啦。
jyutping_sentence: m4 ho2 gam3 gon2 gap1, maan6 maan2 lai4 laa1.
english_sentence: Don't be so rushed, take your time.

english: Dog-Chasing Stick (usually referring to a stick used to shoo away stray dogs)
cantonese_sentence: 佢拎住條趕狗棒，行過條後巷。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ling1 zyu6 tiu4 gon2 gau2 paang5, haang4 gwo3 tiu4 hau6 hong2.
english_sentence: He/She was carrying a dog-chasing stick and walking through the back alley.

cantonese_sentence: 我哋要趕工先可以準時交貨。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 jiu3 gon2 gung1 sin1 ho2 ji5 zeon2 si4 gaau1 fo3.
english_sentence: We need to rush the work to be able to deliver on time.

english: To drive away customers; to be off-putting to customers.
cantonese_sentence: 啲嘢咁貴，梗係趕客啦！
jyutping_sentence: di1 je5 gam3 gwai3, gang2 hai6 gon2 haak3 laa1!
english_sentence: The things are so expensive, of course they drive customers away!

english: Rushing around frantically, often to the detriment of health
cantonese_sentence: 你唔好咁趕喉趕命啦，休息下啦！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 gam3 gon2 hau4 gon2 meng6 laa1, hiu1 sik1 haa5 laa1!
english_sentence: Don't rush around so frantically, take a rest!

english: Too late; won't make it in time; unable to catch
cantonese_sentence: 我驚趕唔切尾班車。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 geng1 gon2 m4 cit3 mei5 baan1 ce1.
english_sentence: I'm afraid I won't make the last bus/train.

english: Force someone to do something quickly, often without proper preparation. Literally, "chasing ducks".
cantonese_sentence: 佢老闆成日趕鴨子咁，要佢哋即刻交報告。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 lou5 baan2 sing4 jat6 gon2 aap3 zi2 gam2, jiu3 keoi5 dei6 zik1 hak1 gaau1 bou3 gou3.
english_sentence: His boss is always rushing them, forcing them to hand in reports immediately.

english: Hurry up; Get a move on; Stop dawdling.
cantonese_sentence: 你哋趕扯啲啦，唔係就嚟遲到喇！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 dei6 gon2 che2 di1 laa1, m4 hai6 zau6 lai4 ci4 dou3 laa3!
english_sentence: You guys hurry up, or you're going to be late!

english: Earthenware/Terracotta; often refers to things like flower pots or large jars.
cantonese_sentence: 我阿婆鍾意用缸瓦種花。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 aa3 po4 zung1 ji3 yung6 gong1 ngaa5 zung3 faa1.
english_sentence: My grandma likes to use earthenware pots to grow flowers.

cantonese: 缸瓦船打老虎——盡地一煲
jyutping: gong1 ngaa5 syun4 daa2 lou5 fu2 -- zeon6 dei6 jat1 bou1
english: All or nothing; going all out; putting everything on the line.
cantonese_sentence: 我哋已經冇晒其他辦法，唯有盡地一煲啦！
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 ji5 ging1 mou5晒 kèi4 taa1 baan6 faat3, wai4 jau5 zeon6 dei6 jat1 bou1 laa1!
english_sentence: We have no other options left, we can only go all out!

english: A swindler/hustler, someone involved in shady dealings, often associated with the "underworld" type. Has a somewhat negative connotation.
cantonese_sentence: 佢個樣十足十一個江湖佬，千祈唔好信佢呀。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 go3 joeng2 zuk1 zuk1 sap6 jat1 go3 gong1 wu4 lou2, cin1 kei4 m4 hou2 seon3 keoi5 aa3.
english_sentence: He looks exactly like a swindler, absolutely do not trust him!

english: Full of aggressive talk; Threatening violence.
cantonese_sentence: 佢哋成日講打講殺，但係就唔會真係郁手。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 seng4 jat6 gong2 daa2 gong2 saat3, daan6 hai6 zau6 m4 wui5 zan1 hai6 juk1 sau2.
english_sentence: They are always talking tough, but they never actually fight.

cantonese_sentence: 你成日講大話，冇人信你㗎。
jyutping_sentence: nei5 seng4 jat6 gong2 daai6 waa6, mou5 jan4 seon3 nei5 gaa3.
english_sentence: You always lie, no one believes you.

english: A person involved in triad societies or, more generally, a person considered a street hustler or rogue with a questionable moral compass.
cantonese_sentence: 佢個人好江湖佬，成日呃人錢。

english_sentence: I wash my hands with soap.

english: Nose as big as a boot
cantonese_sentence: 佢個鼻大到好似靴咁大個鼻，真係好誇張!
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 go3 bei6 daai6 dou3 hou2 ci5 hoe1 gam3 daai6 go3 bei6, zan1 hai6 hou2 kwaa1 zoeng1!
english_sentence: His nose is so big, it's like a boot, it's really exaggerated!

english: To know; to understand; to realize. Often used in a rhetorical question to express disbelief or sarcasm.
cantonese_sentence: 你咁都唔㗾？
jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam3 dou1 m4 te4?
english_sentence: You still don't get it? (Implying obviousness/disbelief)

cantonese_sentence: 風吹住啲樹葉，㗾㗾聲咁響。
jyutping_sentence: fung1 ceoi1 zyu6 di1 syu6 jip6, saa4 saa4 seng1 gam3 hoeng2.
english_sentence: The wind is blowing the leaves, making a rustling sound.

cantonese_sentence: 啲花好香啊！
jyutping_sentence: di1 faa1 hou2 hoeng1 aa3!
english_sentence: These flowers are so fragrant!

english: Incense and lamp offerings (at a temple or shrine), often referring to the monetary donations used to maintain the incense and lamps.
cantonese_sentence: 今日去觀音廟上香燈
jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 heoi3 gun1 jam1 miu2 soeng5 hoeng1 dang1
english_sentence: Today I'm going to the Kwan Yin temple to make an incense and lamp offering.

english: Banana baby (used to describe someone who is yellow on the outside but white on the inside - meaning someone of Asian descent who is very westernized in their thinking and behavior)
cantonese_sentence: 佢個人好似香蕉仔咁，完全唔識講中文。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 go3 jan4 hou2 ci5 hoeng1 jiu1 zai2 gam2, jyun4 cyun4 m4 sik1 gong2 zung1 man2.
english_sentence: He/She is like a banana baby, doesn't know how to speak Chinese at all.

english: Incense Master (Leader of a triad or secret society branch)
cantonese_sentence: 佢係嗰個堂口嘅香主，好有勢力㗎。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 go2 go3 tong4 hau2 ge3 hoeng1 zyu2, hou2 jau5 sai3 lik6 gaa3.
english_sentence: He's the Incense Master of that hall, very influential.

cantonese_sentence: 我想買舊香梘。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 soeng2 maai5 gau6 hoeng1 gaan2.
english_sentence: I want to buy a bar of soap.

cantonese_sentence: 佢今日戴咗個好靚嘅香笄。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam1 jat6 daai3 zo2 go3 hou2 leng3 ge3 hoeng1 gai1.
english_sentence: She wore a very pretty hairpin today.

english: Chicken feet (the part for steaming, braising, or deep frying. Not the entire leg of a chicken).
cantonese_sentence: 今晚飲茶，我哋叫咗籠香雞腳。
jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 jam2 cha4, ngo5 dei6 giu3 zo2 lung4 hoeng1 gai1 goek3.
english_sentence: Tonight, we are having dim sum and we ordered a basket of chicken feet.

cantonese_sentence: 我好鍾意去香江旅行。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hou2 zung1 ji3 heoi3 hoeng1 gong1 leoi5 hang4.
english_sentence: I really like to travel to Hong Kong.

cantonese_sentence: 香港地生活節奏快，壓力大。
jyutping_sentence: hoeng1 gong2 dei6 sang1 wut6 zit3 zau3 faai3, aat3 lik6 daai6.
english_sentence: Life in Hong Kong is fast-paced and stressful.

cantonese_sentence: 佢有香港腳，對腳好痕呀。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jau5 hoeng1 gong2 goek3, deoi3 goek3 hou2 han4 aa3.
english_sentence: He has athlete's foot; his feet are very itchy.

cantonese: 香 港 先 生
cantonese_sentence: 佢 想 參加 今 年 嘅 香 港 先 生 選 舉。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 soeng2 caam1 gaa1 gam1 nin4 ge3 hoeng1 gong2 sin1 saang1 syun2 geoi2.
english_sentence: He wants to participate in this year's Mr. Hong Kong competition.

cantonese_sentence: 我細個嗰陣時，每年都會睇香港小姐嘅選美。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 sai3 go3 go2 zan6 si4, mui5 nin4 dou1 wui5 tai2 hoeng1 gong2 siu2 je2 ge3 syun2 mei5.
english_sentence: When I was little, I watched the Miss Hong Kong beauty pageant every year.

english: Hong Kong Madam/Mrs. (usually implies a married woman of means or social standing)
cantonese_sentence: 佢成日去ball場，真係好似個香港太太咁。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 heoi3 ball coeng4, zan1 hai6 hou2 ci5 go3 hoeng1 gong2 taai3 taai2 gam2.
english_sentence: She goes to the ball so often, she's really like a Hong Kong Madam.

cantonese_sentence: 我想食香口膠。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 soeng2 sik6 hoeng1 hau2 gaau1.
english_sentence: I want to eat chewing gum.

cantonese_sentence: 落啲香油落碗麵度，會香啲㗎。
jyutping_sentence: lok6 di1 hoeng1 jau4 lok6 wun2 min6 dou6, wui hoeng1 di1 gaa3.
english_sentence: Add some sesame oil to the bowl of noodles, it will be more fragrant.

cantonese_sentence: 我唔食香肉㗎，覺得好殘忍。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 sik6 hoeng1 juk6 gaa3, gok3 dak1 hou2 caan4 jan2.
english_sentence: I don't eat dog meat, I think it's very cruel.

english: Temple Stool; someone who sits in a temple all day doing nothing. (Often implies laziness or being a hanger-on)
cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺間廟度坐，好似個香爐躉噉。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 hai2 gaan1 miu2 dou6 co5, hou2 ci5 go3 hoeng1 lou4 dan2 gam2.
english_sentence: He sits in the temple all day, like a temple stool. (He's always hanging around doing nothing.)

cantonese_sentence: 執啲香爐灰返屋企辟邪。
jyutping_sentence: zap1 di1 hoeng1 lou4 fui1 faan1 uk1 kei2 pik1 ce4.
english_sentence: Pick some incense ash to take home and ward off evil.

cantonese_sentence: 我琴日買咗幾隻香牙蕉返屋企。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 kam4 jat6 maai5 zo2 gei2 zek3 hoeng1 ngaa4 ziu1 faan1 uk1 kei2.
english_sentence: I bought a few Cavendish bananas and brought them home yesterday.

cantonese_sentence: 我想飲杯香片。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 soeng2 jam2 bui1 hoeng1 pin3.
english_sentence: I want to drink a cup of jasmine tea.

cantonese_sentence: 今晚我哋食香蕈炒菜。
jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 ngo5 dei6 sik6 hoeng1 seon3 caau2 coi3.
english_sentence: Tonight we're eating stir-fried mushrooms.

english: Gambiered Canton gauze (a type of silk dyed with yam juice)
cantonese_sentence: 我婆婆有一件香雲紗嘅衫。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 po4 po4 jau5 jat1 gin6 hoeng1 wan4 saa1 ge3 saam1.
english_sentence: My grandmother has a piece of clothing made of Gambiered Canton gauze.

cantonese_sentence: 我細個喺鄉下長大。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 sai3 go3 hai2 hoeng1 haa2 zoeng2 daai6.
english_sentence: I grew up in the countryside when I was little.

english: Countryman; fellow villager; person from one's hometown. Often carries a slightly negative connotation implying rural or unsophisticated.
cantonese_sentence: 呢個鄉里成日問啲好蠢嘅問題。
jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 hoeng1 lei5 seng4 jat6 man6 di1 hou2 ceon2 ge3 man6 tai4.
english_sentence: This country bumpkin keeps asking really stupid questions.

english: Very countrified; a bit naive or unsophisticated (but in an endearing way, often used with fondness or teasing)
cantonese_sentence: 佢講嘢鄉里鬼鬼咁，但係個人幾真誠㗎。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2 je5 hoeng1 lei5 gwai2 gwai2 gam2, daan6 hai6 go3 jan4 gei2 zan1 sing4 gaa3.
english_sentence: He speaks in a very countrified/unsophisticated way, but he's a very genuine person.

english: sound; to make a sound; echo; loud
cantonese_sentence: 電話響緊。
jyutping_sentence: din6 waa2 hoeng2 gan2.
english_sentence: The phone is ringing.

cantonese_sentence: 今晚屋企想煲響螺湯。
jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 uk1 kei2 soeng2 bou1 hoeng2 lo4 tong1.
english_sentence: Tonight, I want to make conch soup at home.

english: Go through the motions; do something perfunctorily; pay lip service.
cantonese_sentence: 佢只係虛應故事噉做, 根本就冇用心機。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zi2 hai6 heoi1 jing3 gu3 si6 gam2 zou6, gan1 bun2 zau6 mou5 jung6 sam1 gei1.
english_sentence: He's just going through the motions, he's not putting his heart into it at all.

cantonese_sentence: 我哋聽日去行墟啦。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 ting1 jat6 heoi3 haang4 heoi1 laa1.
english_sentence: Let's go to the market tomorrow.

english: Bustling, lively, crowded; often with a festive or chaotic atmosphere
cantonese_sentence: 新年花車巡遊好墟冚呀！
jyutping_sentence: san1 nin4 faa1 ce1 ceon4 jau4 hou2 heoi1 ham6 aa3!
english_sentence: The New Year's float parade is so bustling/lively!

english: To the fullest extent; to go all out; to push to the limit
cantonese_sentence: 今次去旅行我哋要玩到去到盡！
jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 heoi3 leoi5 hang4 ngo5 dei6 jiu3 waan2 dou3 heoi3 dou3 zeon6!
english_sentence: This time when we travel, we have to have as much fun as we can! (go all out with the fun!)

cantonese_sentence: 今晚我哋去夜街啦！
jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 ngo5 dei6 heoi3 je6 gaai1 laa1!
english_sentence: Let's go out tonight!

english: Go!/Let's go! (often used to initiate action, especially in games or gambling)
cantonese_sentence: 去馬啦！唔好諗咁多！
jyutping_sentence: heoi3 maa5 laa1! m4 hou2 nam2 gam3 do1!
english_sentence: Let's go! Don't think so much!

english: To remove pimples/blemishes (often using photo editing software or skincare products)
cantonese_sentence: 我用手機App去P咗啲相。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 jung6 sau2 gei1 app heoi3 pi1 zo2 di1 soeng3.
english_sentence: I used a phone app to remove pimples from the photos.

english: Show the clip/Let's roll the footage
cantonese_sentence: 頭先嘅畫面好精彩，去片睇多次！
jyutping_sentence: tau4 sin1 ge3 waa6 min6 hou2 zing1 coi2, heoi3 pin3 tai2 do1 ci3!
english_sentence: The footage from earlier was great, let's show the clip and watch it again!

cantonese_sentence: 佢哋去偷去搶啲嘢嚟賣。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 heoi3 tau1 heoi3 coeng2 di1 je5 lai4 maai6.
english_sentence: They steal and rob things to sell.

cantonese_sentence: 開門啦！
jyutping_sentence: hoi1 mun4 laa1!
english_sentence: Open the door!

cantonese_sentence: 呢個apps好開便。
jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 apps hou2 hoi1 bin6.
english_sentence: This app is very convenient.

cantonese_sentence: 我哋聽日要開標。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 ting1 jat6 jiu3 hoi1 biu1.
english_sentence: We are opening bids tomorrow.

english: To start (a game, a task, etc.)
cantonese_sentence: 聽日就開波喇，大家準備好未呀？
jyutping_sentence: ting1 jat6 zau6 hoi1 bo1 laa3, daai6 ga1 zeon2 bei6 hou2 mei6 aa3?
english_sentence: The game starts tomorrow, is everyone ready?

english: To undercharge (someone), to offer a low price intentionally. Often used in the context of businesses trying to lure customers with initially low prices that then increase significantly later.
cantonese_sentence: 佢哋間公司成日開底吸引啲客，之後就用其他名目收貴啲嘅錢。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 gaan1 gung1 si1 seng4 jat6 hoi1 dai2 kap1 jan5 di1 haak3, zi1 hau6 zau6 jung6 kei4 taa1 ming4 muk6 sau1 gwai3 di1 ge3 cin2.
english_sentence: That company often undercharges to attract customers, then uses other pretexts to charge them more money.

cantonese_sentence: 幫我開燈啦，我睇唔到嘢呀。
jyutping_sentence: bong1 ngo5 hoi1 dang1 laa1, ngo5 tai2 m4 dou2 je5 aa3.
english_sentence: Help me turn on the light, I can't see anything.

english: To set up shop; to start business (often used for stalls or small businesses)
cantonese_sentence: 佢喺廟街開檔賣小食。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 miu6 gaai1 hoi1 dong3 maai6 siu2 sik6.
english_sentence: He sets up shop selling snacks in Temple Street.

cantonese_sentence: 我哋今晚開齋，一齊食飯啦！
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 gam1 maan5 hoi1 zaai1, jat1 cai4 sik6 faan6 laa1!
english_sentence: We are breaking the fast tonight, let's have dinner together!

english: To elbow someone, to jostle aggressively.
cantonese_sentence: 佢喺巴士上面開踭，想逼埋嚟我隔離。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 baa1 si2 soeng6 min6 hoi1 zaang1, soeng2 bik1 maai4 lai4 ngo5 gaak3 lei4.
english_sentence: He/She elbowed someone on the bus, trying to squeeze next to me.

english: To branch out and spread one's leaves (i.e., to have many descendants, to have a large family and lineage)
cantonese_sentence: 我哋希望你哋快啲結婚，開枝散葉。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 hei1 mong6 nei5 dei6 faai3 di1 git3 fan1, hoi1 zi1 saan3 jip6.
english_sentence: We hope you get married soon and start a family (branch out and spread your leaves).

english: To open a port (for foreign trade); the opening of a port
cantonese_sentence: 香港開埠之後，發展得好快。
jyutping_sentence: hoeng1 gong2 hoi1 fau6 zi1 hau6, faat3 zin2 dak1 hou2 faai3.
english_sentence: After Hong Kong opened as a port, it developed very quickly.

english: To start cooking (a meal), to fire up the stove and begin cooking.
cantonese_sentence: 今晚我哋開伙爨，煮番幾味餸。
jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 ngo5 dei6 hoi1 fo2 cyun3, zyu2 faan1 gei2 mei6 sung3.
english_sentence: Tonight we're going to start cooking and prepare a few dishes.

english: To book a hotel room (often implying for a short stay, typically for romantic or sexual encounters)
cantonese_sentence: 我聽日要同男朋友開房慶祝生日。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ting1 jat6 jiu3 tung4 naam4 pang1 jau5 hoi1 fong2 hing3 zuk1 saang1 jat6.
english_sentence: I'm booking a hotel room with my boyfriend tomorrow to celebrate my birthday.

cantonese_sentence: 我哋聽日開鏡啦，好緊張啊！
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 ting1 jat6 hoi1 geng3 laa1, hou2 gan2 zoeng1 aa3!
english_sentence: We're starting filming tomorrow, I'm so nervous!

english: As the saying goes; People often say
cantonese_sentence: 開講有話，早起的鳥兒有蟲吃。
jyutping_sentence: hoi1 gong2 jau5 waa6, zou2 hei2 dik1 niu5 ji4 jau5 cung4 hek3.
english_sentence: As the saying goes, the early bird catches the worm.

english: To initiate a discussion/argument; to start a dispute.
cantonese_sentence: 你哋又想開槓呀？
jyutping_sentence: nei5 dei6 jau6 soeng2 hoi1 gong3 aa3?
english_sentence: Are you (plural) trying to start an argument again?

english: To start a story/conversation, to break the ice
cantonese_sentence: 佢唔知點樣開古好。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 m4 zi1 dim2 joeng2 hoi1 gu2 hou2.
english_sentence: He doesn't know how to start a conversation.

english: Start; Beginning (of a game, business venture, etc.)
cantonese_sentence: 今年開局唔錯，生意好好。
jyutping_sentence: gam1 nin4 hoi1 guk6 m4 co3, saang1 ji3 hou2 hou2.
english_sentence: The start of this year was good, business is doing very well.

english: To open (a business, establishment, etc. usually with some formality)
cantonese_sentence: 聽日佢哋間餐廳開館。
jyutping_sentence: ting1 jat6 keoi5 dei6 gaan1 caan1 teng1 hoi1 gun2.
english_sentence: Their restaurant is opening tomorrow.

cantonese_sentence: 聽日要開工，唔想咁快放完假啊！
jyutping_sentence: ting1 jat6 jiu3 hoi1 gung1, m4 soeng2 gam3 faai3 fong3 jyun4 gaa3 aa3!
english_sentence: I have to start work tomorrow, I don't want my holiday to end so soon!

english: Consecrate, bless (an object, usually a statue)
cantonese_sentence: 我哋今日去廟宇幫尊佛像開光。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 gam1 jat6 heoi3 miu6 yu5 bong1 zeon1 fat6 zoeng6 hoi1 gwong1.
english_sentence: We are going to the temple today to consecrate a Buddha statue.

english: To start a project/venture; to begin working on something (often used in the context of building or creation)
cantonese_sentence: 我哋準備開坑整網站。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 zeon2 bei6 hoi1 haang1 zing2 mong5 zaam6.
english_sentence: We're getting ready to start building a website.

english: to open one's mouth; to speak; to start talking
cantonese_sentence: 佢成日都唔開口講嘢。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 dou1 m4 hoi1 hau2 gong2 je5.
english_sentence: He/She rarely opens his/her mouth to speak.

cantonese_sentence: 我想食開口棗呀。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 soeng2 sik6 hoi1 hau2 zou2 aa3.
english_sentence: I want to eat smiling sesame balls.

english: to commit a gaffe; to say the wrong thing; to blurt something out
cantonese_sentence: 你唔好咁 開口夾着脷 啦!
jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 gam3 hoi1 hau2 gap3 zoek6 lei6 laa1!
english_sentence: Don't be so prone to blurting things out (and saying the wrong thing)!

english: Always, constantly, without fail (usually referring to mentioning a specific thing or person)
cantonese_sentence: 佢開口埋口都係講錢。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hoi1 hau2 maai4 hau2 dou1 hai6 gong2 cin2.
english_sentence: He always talks about money, without fail.

cantonese_sentence: 你又講開口夢啦，唔知講乜嘢。
jyutping_sentence: nei5 jau6 gong2 hoi1 hau2 mung6 laa1, m4 zi1 gong2 mat1 je5.
english_sentence: You were talking in your sleep again, I don't know what you were saying.

english: To warm up one's singing voice; to start singing/speaking (especially after a period of not doing so).
cantonese_sentence: 等我開下喉先，陣間唱歌好啲。
jyutping_sentence: dang2 ngo5 hoi1 haa5 hau4 sin1, zan6 gaan1 coeng3 go1 hou2 di1.
english_sentence: Let me warm up my voice first, so I can sing better later.

english: To have a good start/positive opening (usually in business or the stock market)
cantonese_sentence: 今年間公司開咗個紅盤，希望可以繼續賺大錢啦！
jyutping_sentence: gam1 nin4 gaan1 gung1 si1 hoi1 zo2 go3 hung4 pun4, hei1 mong6 ho2 ji5 gai3 zuk1 zaan6 daai6 cin2 laa1!
english_sentence: Our company had a good start this year, hopefully we can continue to make big bucks!

english: to start/prepare the deep fryer (usually in a restaurant context)
cantonese_sentence: 阿姐，開油鑊未呀？
jyutping_sentence: aa3 je1, hoi1 jau4 wok6 mei6 aa3?
english_sentence: Auntie, have you started the deep fryer yet?

english: Open and spacious; having a good view
cantonese_sentence: 間屋好開揚，望到成個海景。
jyutping_sentence: gaan1 uk1 hou2 hoi1 joeng4, mong6 dou2 seng4 go3 hoi2 ging2.
english_sentence: The apartment is very open and spacious, with a view of the entire sea.

english: Open (something) and bring it here / Bring it open
cantonese_sentence: 開嚟俾我睇下
jyutping_sentence: hoi1 lai4 bei2 ngo5 tai2 haa5
english_sentence: Open it and let me take a look.

english: To release (an animal from a cage); to liberate; to free. Can also figuratively mean to have a free and unrestricted conversation or to express oneself freely.
cantonese_sentence: 佢終於可以開籠雀咁講嘢喇！
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zung1 jyu1 ho2 ji5 hoi1 lung4 zoek3 gam2 gong2 je5 laa3!
english_sentence: He can finally talk freely like a released bird!

english: A bird that has been released from its cage; metaphorically, someone who is finally free from constraints or oppression and is now able to do whatever they want. It can also imply excessive freedom or lack of discipline.
cantonese_sentence: 佢放監之後好似開籠雀咁，日日去玩。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 fong3 gaam1 zi1 hau6 hou2 ci5 hoi1 lung4 zoek3 gam2, jat1 jat1 heoi3 waan2.
english_sentence: After he got out of prison, he was like a bird out of its cage, going out to play every day.

jyutping: hoi1 maai4 zing2 gwo3 jan4 sik6 seoi2
english: To exploit or take advantage of others for personal gain (literally, "to dig a well for others to drink from," but with a negative connotation)
cantonese_sentence: 佢成日開埋井過人食水，大家唔好信佢呀！
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 hoi1 maai4 zing2 gwo3 jan4 sik6 seoi2, daai6 ga1 m4 hou2 seon3 keoi5 aa3!
english_sentence: He always exploits people for his own benefit, don't trust him!

english: To shave (the face, usually referring to a man's face)
cantonese_sentence: 佢日日都要開面。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat6 jat6 dou1 jiu3 hoi1 min6-2.
english_sentence: He needs to shave his face every day.

english: To make a grand entrance with great fanfare; to create a spectacle. Often used ironically.
cantonese_sentence: 佢哋結婚要開明鑼鼓，擺一百圍酒席。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei63 git3 fan1 jiu3 hoi1 ming4 lo4 gu2, baai2 jat1 baak3 wai4 zau2 sik6.
english_sentence: They want to have a grand, showy wedding, throwing a hundred tables of banquet.

english_sentence: This house is very run-down; we need to tidy it up.

cantonese_sentence: 今日好凍，攞支寒暑表嚟睇下幾多度。
jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 hou2 dung3, lo2 zi1 hon4 syu2 biu2 lai4 tai2 haa5 gei2 do1 dou6.
english_sentence: It's very cold today, get the thermometer to see how many degrees it is.

cantonese: 寒天飲冰水，點滴在心頭
jyutping: hon4 tin1 jam2 bing1 seoi2, dim2 dik1 zoi6 sam1 tau4
english: Enduring hardship silently (literally: drinking cold water in winter, the feeling is in one's heart)
cantonese_sentence: 佢份人就係咁，寒天飲冰水，點滴在心頭，有咩唔開心都唔會講俾人聽。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 fan6 jan4 zau6 hai6 gam2, hon4 tin1 jam2 bing1 seoi2, dim2 dik1 zoi6 sam1 tau4, jau5 me1 m4 hoi1 sam1 dou1 m4 wui5 gong2 bei2 jan4 teng1.
english_sentence: That's just how he is. He endures hardship silently, and won't tell anyone if he's unhappy about something.

cantonese_sentence: 佢阿爺有份打韓戰。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 aa3 je4 jau5 fan6 daa2 hon4 zin3.
english_sentence: His grandfather participated in the Korean War.

cantonese_sentence: 今年旱天好耐，啲田都冇晒水。
jyutping_sentence: gam1 nin4 hon5 tin1 hou2 noi6, di1 tin4 dou1 mou5 saai3 seoi2.
english_sentence: This year the drought has lasted for a long time, all the fields have run out of water.

cantonese_sentence: 鄉下地方好多時都仲係用旱廁。
jyutping_sentence: heung1 ha5 dei6 fong1 hou2 do1 si4 dou1 zung6 hai6 yung6 hon5 chi3.
english_sentence: In rural areas, many places still use dry toilets.

cantonese_sentence: 細個嗰陣鄉下嘅旱廁好臭。
jyutping_sentence: sai3 go3 go2 zan6 hoeng1 haa2 ge3 hon5 ci3 hou2 cau3.
english_sentence: When I was a kid, the outhouses in the countryside smelled really bad.

english: Tinea versicolor (a common fungal infection of the skin that causes small, discolored patches)
cantonese_sentence: 我背脊好多汗斑，痕到死。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 bui3 zek3 hou2 do1 hon6 baan1, han4 dou3 si2.
english_sentence: I have a lot of tinea versicolor on my back, it's so itchy it's killing me.

english: Body hair, fine hair on the body
cantonese_sentence: 佢手臂好多汗毛。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sau2 bei3 hou2 do1 hon6 mou4.
english_sentence: He/She has a lot of body hair on their arms.

cantonese_sentence: 佢有汗宿嘅習慣，成日半夜起身周圍行。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jau5 hon6 suk1 ge3 zaap6 gwaan3, seng4 jat6 bun3 je6 hei2 san1 zau1 wai4 haang4.
english_sentence: He has a habit of sleepwalking, and often gets up in the middle of the night to walk around.

cantonese_sentence: 我想喺康文署嘅泳池學游水。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 soeng2 hai2 hong1 man4 syu5 ge3 wing6 ci4 hok6 jau4 seoi2.
english_sentence: I want to learn how to swim at an LCSD swimming pool.

english: LOHAS Park (a residential area in Hong Kong)
cantonese_sentence: 我住喺康城。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zyu6 hai2 hong1 sing4.
english_sentence: I live in LOHAS Park.

cantonese_sentence: 我今年好想去康城影展睇戲。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 nin4 hou2 soeng2 heoi3 hong1 sing4 jing2 zin2 tai2 hei3.
english_sentence: I really want to go to the Cannes Film Festival to watch movies this year.

cantonese_sentence: 唔好食咁多飯糠，對身體唔好。
jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 sik6 gam3 do1 faan6 hong1, deoi3 san1 tai2 m4 hou2.
english_sentence: Don't eat so much rice bran, it's not good for your health. (Contextually, this refers to polished white rice, implying that eating more brown rice with the bran is better.)

english: To measure rice with a specific tool (usually a small wooden container) to ensure it is accurately portioned. Can also mean to bump or hit against something.
cantonese_sentence: 我幫你䉺一䉺啲米，唔好咁多啦。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 bong1 nei5 deon6 jat1 deon6 di1 mai5, m4 hou2 gam3 do1 laa1.
english_sentence: Let me measure out some rice for you, don't take so much.

cantonese_sentence: 呢啲糠耳嘢唔好攞返屋企啦。
jyutping_sentence: ni1 di1 hong1 ji5 je5 m4 hou2 lo2 faan1 uk1 kei2 laa1.
english_sentence: Don't bring this rubbish home.

english: to walk, to go, to be okay
cantonese_sentence: 我哋一齊去行街。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 jat1 cai4 heoi3 haang4 gaai1.
english_sentence: Let's go shopping together.

cantonese_sentence: 我只會買行貨，有保養。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zi2 wui5 maai5 haang4 fo3, jau5 bo2 yeung5.
english_sentence: I only buy genuine products; they come with a warranty.

english: bake/dry over heat, warm up (especially referring to food)
cantonese_sentence: 我鐘意炕乾個麵包
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zung1 ji3 kong3 gon1 go3 min6 baau1
english_sentence: I like to bake/dry the bread until it's dry/crispy.

cantonese_sentence: 啲塵多到好似喺炕底摷出嚟咁
jyutping_sentence: di1 can4 do1 dou3 hou2 ci5 hai2 hong3 dai2 cau1 ceot1 lai4 gam2
english_sentence: The dust is so much it looks like it's been dragged out from under the bed.

english: Parched Throat (feeling dry and scratchy in the throat)
cantonese_sentence: 我把聲好似炕沙咁，講嘢都講唔出。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 baa2 seng1 hou2 ci5 hong3 saa1 gam3, gong2 je5 dou1 gong2 m4 chut1.
english_sentence: My voice feels so parched (dry and scratchy), I can't even speak.

english: to walk, to go, to be ok/alright (depending on context)
cantonese_sentence: 我行路返屋企。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 haang4 lou6 faan1 uk1 kei2.
english_sentence: I walk home.

english: Respected senior (in a profession, often used in triad societies but can be used generally in trades)
cantonese_sentence: 佢係呢個行業嘅行尊，經驗豐富。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 ni1 go3 hang4 jip6 ge3 hong4 zyun1, ging1 gim6 fung1 fu3.
english_sentence: He is a respected senior in this industry, with a wealth of experience.

english: genuine product, legitimate goods (often implying a warranty and after-sales service)
cantonese_sentence: 我買電器通常都買行貨，費事壞咗冇人整。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 maai5 din6 hei3 tung1 soeng4 dou1 maai5 hang4 fo3, fai3 si4 waai6 zo2 mou5 jan4 zing2.
english_sentence: I usually buy genuine products when I buy electronics, to avoid having no one to fix them if they break.

english: expert, professional, someone in the same trade
cantonese_sentence: 佢係呢行嘅行家，乜都識。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 ni1 hong4 ge3 haang4 gaa1, mat1 dou1 sik1.
english_sentence: He is an expert in this industry, he knows everything.

cantonese_sentence: 佢講嘢成日用行口，好難明。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2 je5 sing4 jat6 jung6 hang4 hau2, hou2 naan4 ming4.
english_sentence: He often uses industry jargon when he speaks, it's difficult to understand.

english: Outfit, attire; Profession, line of work
cantonese_sentence: 佢今日個行頭好型仔。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam1 jat6 ge3 haang4 tau4 hou2 jing4 zai2.
english_sentence: His outfit today is very stylish.

cantonese_sentence: 最近樓市行情光，好多人想買樓。
jyutping_sentence: zeoi3 gan6 lau4 si5 hong4 cing4 gwong1, hou2 do1 jan4 soeng2 maai5 lau2.
english_sentence: The property market outlook is good recently, and many people want to buy apartments.

cantonese_sentence: 間屋啲桁好粗
jyutping_sentence: gaan1 uk1 di1 hang4 hou2 cou1
english_sentence: The beams of that house are very thick.

cantonese_sentence: 我幫你絎幾針先啦。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 bong1 nei5 haang4 gei2 zam1 sin1 laa1.
english_sentence: I'll tack a few stitches for you first.

cantonese_sentence: 佢幫我哋張被絎針。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 bong1 ngo5 dei6 zoeng1 bei6 haang4 zam1.
english_sentence: She quilted our blanket for us.

cantonese_sentence: 我想喝水。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 soeng2 hot3 seoi2.
english_sentence: I want to drink water.

cantonese_sentence: 呢隻股票好渴市㗎，好多人想買。
jyutping_sentence: ni1 zek3 gu2 piu3 hou2 hot3 si5 gaa3, hou2 do1 jan4 soeng2 maai5.
english_sentence: This stock is very sought-after, many people want to buy it.

cantonese_sentence: 你好嗎？
jyutping_sentence: nei5 hou2 maa3?
english_sentence: How are you?

cantonese_sentence: 佢個人好辯駁，成日同人嘈交。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 go3 jan4 hou2 bin6 bok3, seng4 jat6 tung4 jan4 caau2 gaau1.
english_sentence: He is very argumentative, always arguing with people.

cantonese_sentence: 你都幾好膽，敢同老細嘈交！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 dou1 gei2 hou2 daam2, gam2 tung4 lou5 sai3 caau4 gaau1!
english_sentence: You're quite brave, daring to argue with the boss!

cantonese_sentence: 佢好地地企喺度，點解會跌低㗎？
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hou2 dei6 dei2 kei5 hai2 dou6, dim2 gaai2 wui5 dit3 dai1 gaa3?
english_sentence: He was standing there properly, why would he fall down?

english: Good/well-behaved boy (can also refer to a good son or a good/reliable man in general)
cantonese_sentence: 佢係一個好仔，好聽父母話。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 jat1 go3 hou2 zai2, hou2 teng1 fu6 mou5 waa6.
english_sentence: He is a good boy, he listens to his parents.

cantonese_sentence: 好在今日冇落雨，如果唔係就掃興啦。
jyutping_sentence: hou2 zoi6 gam1 jat6 mou5 lok6 jyu5, jyu4 gwo2 m4 hai6 zau6 sou3 hing3 laa1.
english_sentence: Luckily it didn't rain today, otherwise it would have ruined the fun.

jyutping: hou2 zou6 m4 zou6, nin4 saa1 maan5 ze6 zou3
english: If you had the chance to do it properly, you didn't; now it's the last day of the year and you're finally thanking the Kitchen God (implying a last-minute, inadequate effort).
cantonese_sentence: 你平時唔做好啲，好做唔做，年卅晚謝灶，咁遲嚟補鑊有咩用？
jyutping_sentence: nei5 ping4 si4 m4 zou6 hou2 di1, hou2 zou6 m4 zou6, nin4 saa1 maan5 ze6 zou3, gam2 ci4 lai4 bou2 wok6 jau5 me1 jung6?
english_sentence: If you don't do better normally, and leave it to the last minute like thanking the Kitchen God on the last day of the year, what use is it to fix things so late?

cantonese_sentence: 佢病咗好耐，終於好番喇！
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 beng6 zo2 hou2 noi6, zung1 jyu1 hou2 faan1 laa3!
english_sentence: He was sick for a long time, but he finally recovered!

cantonese_sentence: 你琴晚好唔好瞓啊？
jyutping_sentence: nei5 kam4 maan5 hou2 m4 hou2 fan3 aa3?
english_sentence: Did you sleep well last night?

jyutping: hou2 ge3 m4 ling4 cau2 ge3 ling4
english: "Good things don't work, bad things do" or "Misfortune comes readily, but good fortune is slow to arrive."
cantonese_sentence: 阿仔考試之前日日都唔溫書，點知真係肥佬，真係好嘅唔靈醜嘅靈。
jyutping_sentence: aa3 zai2 haau2 si5 zi1 cin4 jat6 jat6 dou1 m4 wan1 syu1, dim2 zi1 zan1 hai6 fei4 lou2, zan1 hai6 hou2 ge3 m4 ling4 cau2 ge3 ling4.
english_sentence: My son didn't study before the exam and unsurprisingly, he failed. Good things don't work, bad things do indeed.

cantonese_sentence: 佢個人好頸，講唔聽㗎。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 go3 jan4 hou2 geng2, gong2 m4 ting1 gaa3.
english_sentence: He's a very stubborn person, he won't listen to you.

english: Not that great; limited goodness; not exceptionally good.
cantonese_sentence: 佢份人好極有限，你唔好期望太高啦。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 fan6 jan4 hou2 gik1 jau5 haan6, nei5 m4 hou2 kei4 mong6 taai3 gou1 laa1.
english_sentence: His personality isn't that great, don't expect too much from him.

cantonese_sentence: 希望疫情之後，經濟可以好景翻身啦！
jyutping_sentence: hei1 mong6 yik6 ching4 zi1 hau6, ging1 zai3 ho2 yi5 hou2 ging2 faan1 san1 laa1!
english_sentence: Hopefully, after the pandemic, the economy can recover and have good times again!

english: Lucky Foot/Auspicious Entrance (often used to describe someone who brings good luck when they enter a place or start a project)
cantonese_sentence: 你真係好腳頭，你一嚟我哋就中咗獎！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 zan1 hai6 hou2 goek3 tau4, nei5 jat1 lai4 ngo5 dei6 zau6 zung3 zo2 zoeng2!
english_sentence: You really are a lucky charm, we won the lottery right after you came!

english: very, extremely (often used to emphasize a positive or negative adjective)
cantonese_sentence: 佢好鬼叻㗎!
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hou2 gwai2 lek1 gaa3!
english_sentence: He is extremely smart!

cantonese_sentence: 飲多啲水好過飲汽水。
jyutping_sentence: yam2 do1 di1 seoi2 hou2 gwo3 yam2 hei3 seoi2.
english_sentence: Drinking more water is better than drinking soda.

cantonese_sentence: 我今日好閒，唔知做咩好。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 jat6 hou2 haan4, m4 zi1 zou6 me1 hou2.
english_sentence: I'm very free today, I don't know what to do.

english: Easy to walk; Easy to navigate; Not crowded
cantonese_sentence: 呢條路好行好多，唔使逼。
jyutping_sentence: ni1 tiu4 lou6 hou2 haang4 hou2 do1, m4 sai2 bik1.
english_sentence: This road is much easier to walk, you don't have to squeeze.

cantonese_sentence: 你真係好口, 氹到佢哋好開心。
jyutping_sentence: nei5 zan1 hai6 hou2 hau2, tam5 dou3 keoi5 dei6 hou2 hoi1 sam1.
english_sentence: You're really good with words, you made them very happy.

cantonese_sentence: 你咁樣做好鬼好氣呀！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam2 joeng2 zou6 hou2 gwai2 hou2 hei3 aa3!
english_sentence: You doing it like that is really annoying!

cantonese_sentence: 你今日睇落好有氣色喎！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam1 jat6 tai2 lok6 hou2 jau5 hei3 sik1 wo3!
english_sentence: You look like you have a good complexion today!

english: To carefully examine, to have a good look
cantonese_sentence: 你好好睇睇份合約先簽名啦。
jyutping_sentence: nei5 hou2 hou2 tai2 tai2 fan6 hap6 joek3 sin1 cim1 ming4 laa1.
english_sentence: You should carefully examine the contract before you sign it.

english: Has a high tolerance for alcohol / Can drink a lot
cantonese_sentence: 佢好飲得，成晚都無醉。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hou2 jam2 dak1, seng4 maan5 dou1 mou5 zeoi3.
english_sentence: He can drink a lot, he wasn't drunk all night.

cantonese_sentence: 佢係好人好姐，唔會做出咁嘅事嘅。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 hou2 jan4 hou2 je1, m4 wui5 zou6 ceot1 gam2 ge3 si6 ge3.
english_sentence: She's a respectable woman/girl, she wouldn't do something like that.

english: Limits to how nice someone can be; there's a limit to someone's good nature; even nice people have their limits.
cantonese_sentence: 你唔好得寸進尺，好人有限㗎！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 dak1 cyun3 zeon3 cek3, hou2 jan4 jau5 haan6 gaa3!
english_sentence: Don't push your luck, even nice people have their limits!

cantonese_sentence: 你做咁多善事，好人有好報㗎！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 zou6 gam3 do1 sin6 si6, hou2 jan4 jau5 hou2 bou3 gaa3!
english_sentence: You do so much charity, good people get good rewards!

cantonese_sentence: 佢真係做咗件好人事。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zan1 hai6 zou6 zo2 gin6 hou2 jan4 si6.
english_sentence: He/She really did a good deed.

english: Good day; auspicious day; good times
cantonese_sentence: 希望你哋快啲過返好日子啦。
jyutping_sentence: hei1 mong6 nei5 dei6 faai3 di1 gwo3 faan1 hou2 jat6 zi2 laa1.
english_sentence: Hopefully you all will return to good times soon.

cantonese_sentence: 我哋係好好嘅好友。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 hai6 hou2 hou2 ge3 hou2 jau5.
english_sentence: We are very good friends.

cantonese_sentence: 你搞掂咗份報告啊？好嘢！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 gaau2 dim6 zo2 fan6 bou3 gou3 aa3? hou2 je5!
english_sentence: You finished the report? Good job!

english: To dress well; to be well-dressed
cantonese_sentence: 佢份人好識得好衣好着，成日都好靚。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 fan6 jan4 hou2 sik1 dak1 hou2 ji1 hou2 zoek3, sing4 jat6 dou1 hou2 leng3.
english_sentence: She knows how to dress well, she always looks beautiful.

english: Auspicious, Lucky (generally referring to good omens, positive connotations, or things that bring good fortune)
cantonese_sentence: 新年講啲好意頭嘅嘢啦！
jyutping_sentence: san1 nin4 gong2 di1 hou2 ji3 tau4 ge3 je5 laa1!
english_sentence: During the New Year, let's say auspicious things!

cantonese_sentence: 佢個人好耳，乜都信。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 go3 jan4 hou2 ji5, mat1 dou1 seon3.
english_sentence: He is very gullible and believes everything.

english: Good show; worthy; used to describe someone who's done something well, impressive, or sometimes sarcastically for someone who's messed up badly.
cantonese_sentence: 好樣嘅，你真係搞掂咗件事！
jyutping_sentence: hou2 joeng2 ge3, nei5 zan1 hai6 gaau2 dim6 zo2 gin6 si6!
english_sentence: Good show, you really handled the matter!

english: Easy to talk to; Chatty; Engaging in conversation
cantonese_sentence: 佢個人好鍾意同人哋好傾偈.
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 go3 jan4 hou2 zung1 ji3 tung4 jan4 dei6 hou2 king1 gai2.
english_sentence: He/She really likes chatting with people.

cantonese_sentence: 佢好力，搬得起個大雪櫃㗎。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hou2 lik6, bun1 dak1 hei2 go3 daai6 syut3 gwai2 gaa3.
english_sentence: He's strong, he can lift the big refrigerator.

cantonese: 好老怕爛佬，爛佬怕潑婦
jyutping: hou2 lou5 paa3 laan6 lou2, laan6 lou2 paa3 put3 fu5
english: "Good guys fear bad guys, bad guys fear shrewish women." (Implies that even the toughest guys can be undone by someone even more unruly or unreasonable.)
cantonese_sentence: 你對住啲客都要有禮貌啲㗎，唔好咁爛撻撻，唔係就真係好老怕爛佬，爛佬怕潑婦喇。
jyutping_sentence: nei5 deoi3 zyu6 di1 haak3 dou1 jiu3 jau5 lai5 maau6 di1 gaa3, m4 hou2 gam3 laan6 taat3 taat3, m4 hai6 zau6 zan1 hai6 hou2 lou5 paa3 laan6 lou2, laan6 lou2 paa3 put3 fu5 laa3.
english_sentence: You have to be more polite to the customers. Don't be so sloppy, otherwise, it's truly "good guys fear bad guys, bad guys fear shrewish women." (Meaning if you're not careful, you'll run into trouble with difficult people.)

english: Really bad, awful, not working out well.
cantonese_sentence: 佢份工好唔掂，日日俾老細鬧。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 fan6 gung1 hou2 m4 dim6, jat6 jat6 bei2 lou5 sai3 nau6.
english_sentence: His job is really awful; he gets scolded by the boss every day.

cantonese_sentence: 佢生得好眉好貌，好得人鍾意。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 saang1 dak1 hou2 mei4 hou2 maau6, hou2 dak1 jan4 zung1 ji3.
english_sentence: He/She is good-looking and very likeable.

english: Good luck/fortune (often referring to luck that stems from destiny)
cantonese_sentence: 佢真係好命水，買親都中。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zan1 hai6 hou2 ming6 seoi2, maai5 can1 dou1 zung3.
english_sentence: He really has good luck, he wins every time he buys (lottery/gambles).

english: Keen eyesight; good at noticing details.
cantonese_sentence: 你對眼咁好眼嘅？ 一眼就睇到有張污糟嘢喺枱面。
jyutping_sentence: nei5 deoi3 ngaan5 gam3 hou2 ngaan5 ge3? jat1 ngaan5 zau6 tai2 dou2 jau5 zoeng1 wu1 zou1 je5 hai2 toi2 min6.
english_sentence: Are your eyes so sharp? You noticed a dirty thing on the table with just one glance.

english: Good eye; discerning taste; perceptive judgment
cantonese_sentence: 你揀呢隻錶真係好眼界喎!
jyutping_sentence: nei5 gaan2 ni1 zek3 biu1 zan1 hai6 hou2 ngaan5 gaai3 wo3!
english_sentence: You really have good taste picking this watch!

cantonese: 好女兩頭瞞，唔好女兩頭搬

english_sentence: This plate of soy sauce chicken is very flavorful.

jyutping: jap6 uk1 giu3 jan4, jap6 miu2 baai3 san4
english: When entering a house, greet the people; when entering a temple, worship the gods. (It means to do what is appropriate for the place and situation.)
cantonese_sentence: 你入人地屋企梗係要入屋叫人，入廟拜神啦!
jyutping_sentence: nei5 jap6 jan4 dei6 uk1 kei2 gang2 hai6 jiu3 jap6 uk1 giu3 jan4, jap6 miu2 baai3 san4 laa1!
english_sentence: When you enter someone's house, of course you should greet the people, and when you enter a temple, worship the gods! (meaning you should do what is expected of you in a situation)

english: to resonate deeply, to touch the heart, to be deeply affected
cantonese_sentence: 佢講嘅嘢好入心。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2 ge3 je5 hou2 jap6 sam1.
english_sentence: What he said really resonated with me.

cantonese_sentence: 佢份工嘅入息唔錯。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 fan6 gung1 ge3 jap6 sik1 m4 co3.
english_sentence: His/Her job's income isn't bad.

cantonese_sentence: 我今年要交好多入息稅。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 nin4 jiu3 gaau1 ho2 do1 jap6 sik1 seoi3.
english_sentence: I have to pay a lot of income tax this year.

english: Deposit money; make a bank transfer/deposit.
cantonese_sentence: 我今日要入數去你個戶口。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 jat6 jiu3 jap6 sou3 heoi3 nei5 go3 wu6 hau2.
english_sentence: I need to deposit money into your account today.

cantonese_sentence: 記得攞返張入數紙啊。
jyutping_sentence: gei3 dak1 lo2 faan1 zoeng1 jap6 sou3 zi2 aa3.
english_sentence: Remember to take back the deposit slip.

english: To be jailed, to be put in the book (registry of prisoners)
cantonese_sentence: 佢衰咗搶嘢，俾人入冊喇。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seoi1 zo2 coeng2 je5, bei2 jan4 jap6 caak3 laa3.
english_sentence: He was arrested for robbery and got jailed.

english: To be admitted to a mental institution, literally "enter Green Mountain" (a euphemism)
cantonese_sentence: 佢嘅精神狀況好差，睇怕要入青山喇。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ge3 zing1 san4 zong6 fong3 hou2 caa1, tai2 paa3 jiu3 jap6 cing1 saan1 laa3.
english_sentence: His/her mental state is very bad, it seems likely he/she will have to be admitted to a mental institution.

cantonese_sentence: 我間房有個入牆櫃，擺好多衫。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gaan1 fong2 jau5 go3 jap6 coeng4 gwai6, baai2 hou2 do1 saam1.
english_sentence: My room has a built-in wardrobe where I keep lots of clothes.

cantonese_sentence: 我買咗兩張演唱會入場券。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 maai5 zo2 loeng5 zoeng1 jin2 coeng3 wui2 jap6 coeng4 gyun3.
english_sentence: I bought two concert tickets.

english: To be admitted to a hospital (or repair shop for vehicles)
cantonese_sentence: 佢琴日入咗廠，好似係盲腸炎。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 kam4 jat6 jap6 zo2 cong2, hou2 ci5 hai6 maang4 coeng2 jim4.
english_sentence: He was admitted to the hospital yesterday, it seems like it's appendicitis.

english: To be shortlisted; to make the cut; to be a finalist
cantonese_sentence: 佢參加選美入咗圍。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 caam1 gaa1 syun2 mei5 jap6 zo2 wai4.
english_sentence: She entered the beauty pageant and made the shortlist.

cantonese_sentence: 我有一個蘋果。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 jau5 jat1 go3 ping4 gwo2.
english_sentence: I have one apple.

english: All day long; From morning till night
cantonese_sentence: 佢一日到黑都喺度打機。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat1 jat6 dou3 hak1 dou1 hai2 dou6 daa2 gei1.
english_sentence: He plays video games all day long.

english: A fire (literally "one bundle fire"), but often implies anger or passion.
cantonese_sentence: 佢發咗一把火，乜都唔理就走咗。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 faat3 zo2 jat1 baa2 fo2, mat1 dou1 m4 lei5 zau6 zau2 zo2.
english_sentence: He got really angry and left without caring about anything.

english: once; a single time; just do something
cantonese_sentence: 我睇咗一便就明喇。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 tai2 zo2 jat1 bin6 zau6 ming4 laa3.
english_sentence: I understood after reading it just once.

english: carrying a load (on a shoulder pole)
cantonese_sentence: 一擔擔 | jat1 daam3 daam3 | loads and loads / a lot of things carried
jyutping_sentence: 佢攞住一擔擔嘢返屋企。
english_sentence: keoi5 lo2 zyu6 jat1 daam3 daam3 je5 faan1 uk1 kei2.

jyutping: jat1 daam6 saa1 tong4 jat1 daam6 si2
english: A mixture of good and bad; bittersweet; taking the good with the bad.
cantonese_sentence: 人生就係一啖砂糖一啖屎，冇可能事事順利。
jyutping_sentence: jan4 sang1 zau6 hai6 jat1 daam6 saa1 tong4 jat1 daam6 si2, mou5 ho2 nang4 si6 si6 seon6 lei6.
english_sentence: Life is a mixture of good and bad, it's impossible for everything to go smoothly.

english: First-class, top-notch, the best of the best
cantonese_sentence: 佢啲手藝一等一嘅，搵佢整嘢就啱晒。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 di1 sau2 ngai6 jat1 dang2 jat1 ge3, wan2 keoi5 zing2 je5 zau6 ngaam1 saai3.
english_sentence: His craftsmanship is top-notch, finding him to make things is perfect.

cantonese_sentence: 我識講一啲廣東話。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 sik1 gong2 jat1 di1 gwong2 dung1 waa2.
english_sentence: I know how to speak a little Cantonese.

english: A little bit; slightly; a tiny bit
cantonese_sentence: 我識講一啲啲廣東話。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 sik1 gong2 jat1 dik1 dik1 gwong2 dung1 waa2.
english_sentence: I know how to speak a little bit of Cantonese.

cantonese_sentence: 我肚餓呀，不如煮包一丁麵嚟食啦。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 tou5 ngo6 aa3, bat1 jyu4 zyu2 baau1 jat1 ding1 min6 lai4 sik6 laa1.
english_sentence: I'm hungry, why don't we cook a packet of Nissin Demae Ramen to eat?

english: Once; at one point; for a period of time
cantonese_sentence: 我一度諗住移民去加拿大。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 jat1 dou6 lam2 zyu6 ji4 man4 heoi3 ga3 naa4 daai6.
english_sentence: I once thought about immigrating to Canada.

english: Absolutely nothing; Not a single thing
cantonese_sentence: 我哋傾咗成晚，都一戙都冇搞掂。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 king1 zo2 seng4 maan5, dou1 jat1 dung6 dou1 mou5 gaau2 dim6.
english_sentence: We talked all night, and didn't accomplish a single thing.

english: A puff of smoke; a wisp of smoke; (figuratively) a brief moment, fleeting.
cantonese_sentence: 佢講嘢好似一朕煙噉，好快就唔記得咗。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2 je5 hou2 ci5 jat1 zam6 jin1 gam2, hou2 faai3 zau6 m4 gei3 dak1 zo2.
english_sentence: He speaks like a wisp of smoke, he forgets very quickly.

english: A little while, in a bit, later
cantonese_sentence: 我一陣間打俾你。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 jat1 zan6 gaan1 daa2 bei2 nei5.
english_sentence: I'll call you in a little while.

jyutping: jat1 zau6 jat1 ji6 zau6 ji6
english: Matter-of-fact; Taking things literally and rigidly; Strict adherence to rules.
cantonese_sentence: 佢做嘢一就一二就二，唔識變通嘅。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 je5 jat1 zau6 jat1 ji6 zau6 ji6, m4 sik1 bin3 tung1 ge3.
english_sentence: He is very rigid in his work, and doesn't know how to be flexible.

english: Number one female; leading lady; queen bee
cantonese_sentence: 佢係電視台嘅一姐嚟㗎。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 din6 si6 toi4 ge3 jat1 je1 lai4 ga3.
english_sentence: She's the leading lady of the TV station.

english: A game piece, token, or counter (often small and flat, used in board games or gambling games)
cantonese_sentence: 我輸咗好多隻積。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 syu1 zo2 hou2 do1 zek1.
english_sentence: I lost a lot of game pieces/tokens.

cantonese_sentence: 我見到一隻狗喺公園玩。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gin3 dou2 jat1 zek3 gau2 hai2 gung1 jyun2 waan2.
english_sentence: I saw a dog playing in the park.

english: A pair of wooden clogs/sandals. Note: While 一隻 normally means "one", in this context, it idiomatically refers to a *pair*.
cantonese_sentence: 我細個成日著住一隻屐周圍走。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 sai3 go3 seng4 jat6 zoek3 zyu6 jat1 zek3 gek6 zau1 wai4 zau2.
english_sentence: When I was little, I often wore wooden clogs/sandals everywhere.

cantonese_sentence: 佢成日一支公去飲嘢。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 jat1 ji1 gung1 heoi3 jam2 je5.
english_sentence: He often goes for drinks alone.

cantonese_sentence: 一自你走咗之後，我就好少出街喇。
jyutping_sentence: jat1 zi6 nei5 zau2 zo2 zi1 hau6, ngo5 zau6 hou2 siu2 ceot1 gaai1 laa1.
english_sentence: Ever since you left, I rarely go out.

cantonese_sentence: 我自細就住喺香港
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zi6 sai3 zau6 zyu6 hai2 hoeng1 gong2
english_sentence: I've lived in Hong Kong since I was young.

english: Very simple, easy to understand (literally, "as shallow as one character")
cantonese_sentence: 呢條問題一字咁淺，唔駛諗咁耐啦！
jyutping_sentence: ni1 tiu4 man6 tai4 jat1 zi6 gam3 cin2, m4 sai2 lam2 gam3 noi6 laa1!
english_sentence: This question is very simple, don't need to think for so long!

english: A right angle (literally "one character angle", referring to the shape of the Chinese character "一" being a straight line forming part of the angle)
cantonese_sentence: 呢個櫃嘅一字角爛咗。
jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 gwai6 ge3 jat1 zi6 gok3 laan6 zo2.
english_sentence: The right angle corner of this cabinet is broken.

cantonese_sentence: 佢嘅一字馬做得好靚。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ge3 jat1 zi6 maa5 zou6 dak1 hou2 leng3.
english_sentence: Her splits are done very beautifully.

cantonese_sentence: 佢條一字眉好粗呀。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 tiu4 jat1 zi6 mei4 hou2 cou1 aa3.
english_sentence: Her unibrow is very thick.

jyutping: jat1 zuk1 gou1 daa2 jat1 syun4 jan4
english: To punish or blame a whole group of people for the misdeeds of a few.
cantonese_sentence: 唔好一竹蒿打一船人，唔係個個都係咁嘅。
jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 jat1 zuk1 gou1 daa2 jat1 syun4 jan4, m4 hai6 go3 go3 dou1 hai6 gam2 ge3.
english_sentence: Don't punish everyone for the actions of a few, not everyone is like that.

cantonese_sentence: 我哋係夜瞓一族。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 hai6 je6 fan3 jat1 zuk6.
english_sentence: We are the night owl group.

english: Dim sum with tea (literally: one pot, two pieces)
cantonese_sentence: 今日飲茶，我哋叫咗一盅兩件。
jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 jam2 caa4, ngo5 dei6 giu3 zo2 jat1 zung1 loeng5 gin6.
english_sentence: Today we went for dim sum and ordered the standard tea and dim sum set.

jyutping: jat1 zyun1 dau6 fu6 hong6 sing1 sin1
english: Die very easily; an easy death. Figuratively, to be incredibly vulnerable and easily defeated or tricked. Think of it like being as fragile as a block of tofu.
cantonese_sentence: 佢咁蠢，呃佢咪一磚豆腐項升仙囉！
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam3 ceon2, aak1 keoi5 mai6 jat1 zyun1 dau6 fu6 hong6 sing1 sin1 lo1!
english_sentence: He's so stupid, tricking him would be like a block of tofu going to heaven! (He's so easy to trick!)

english: The whole family, including young children.
cantonese_sentence: 我哋一家大細去咗旅行。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 jat1 gaa1 daai6 sai3 heoi3 zo2 leoi5 hang4.
english_sentence: Our whole family went on a trip.

jyutping: jat1 gaa1 bin6 yi4 loeng5 gaa1 zoek3
english: One party benefits, both parties gain / A win-win situation.
cantonese_sentence: 不如大家讓一步，一家便宜兩家着啦。
jyutping_sentence: bat1 jyu4 daai6 gaa1 joeng6 jat1 bou6, jat1 gaa1 bin6 yi4 loeng5 gaa1 zoek3 laa1.
english_sentence: Why don't we all take a step back and make it a win-win situation for everyone?

jyutping: jat1 gai1 sei2 jat1 gai1 ming4
english: When one dies, another takes its place; There's always someone to replace them.
cantonese_sentence: 唔使咁擔心嘅，一雞死一雞鳴，佢唔做咪搵第二個做囉。
jyutping_sentence: m4 sai2 gam3 daam1 sam1 ge3, jat1 gai1 sei2 jat1 gai1 ming4, keoi5 m4 zou6 mai1 wan2 dai6 ji6 go3 zou6 lo1.
english_sentence: Don't worry so much, when one dies another takes its place. If he doesn't do it, then we'll just find someone else to do it.

english: A very small amount; a tiny bit; an insignificant sum of money.
cantonese_sentence: 佢真係孤寒到一雞士都唔肯俾。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zan1 hai6 gu1 hon4 dou3 jat1 gai1 si2 dou1 m4 hang2 bei2.
english_sentence: He's so stingy that he wouldn't even give a tiny bit.

cantonese_sentence: 你食咗一嚿飯未呀？
jyutping_sentence: nei5 sik6 zo2 jat1 gau6 faan6 mei6 aa3?
english_sentence: Have you eaten a portion of rice yet?

english: lump, a measure word for something lumpy, often money
cantonese_sentence: 一嚿水 | jat1 gau6 seoi2 | A grand (one thousand dollars, HKD)
jyutping_sentence: 我爭佢一嚿水呀。
english_sentence: ngo5 zaang1 keoi5 jat1 gau6 seoi2 aa3.

english: A lump of cloud; also used figuratively to mean clueless or dazed.
cantonese_sentence: 佢成日一嚿雲咁，唔知佢諗緊乜。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 jat1 gau6 wan4 gam2, m4 zi1 keoi5 lam2 gan2 mat1.
english_sentence: He's always so clueless/dazed, I don't know what he's thinking.

english: Covered in blood (literally "a neck full of blood"), often implies being in deep trouble or heavily involved in a situation where you are likely to suffer consequences.
cantonese_sentence: 你再唔收手，到時一定搞到一頸血。
jyutping_sentence: nei5 zoi3 m4 sau1 sau2, dou3 si4 jat1 ding6 gaau2 dou3 jat1 geng2 hyut3.
english_sentence: If you don't stop, you'll definitely end up in deep trouble.

english: Big Brother; Top dog; Number One
cantonese_sentence: 佢喺警隊係一哥。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 ging2 deoi2 hai6 jat1 go1.
english_sentence: He's the top dog in the police force.

english: One or two; a small number; few
cantonese_sentence: 我仲有啲嘢要執，你哋一個半個走先啦。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zung6 jau5 di1 je5 jiu3 zap1, nei5 dei6 jat1 go3 bun3 go3 zau2 sin1 laa1.
english_sentence: I still have some things to pack up; you guys can leave one or two at a time.

cantonese_sentence: 我哋係一對情侶。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 hai6 jat1 deoi3 cing4 leoi5.
english_sentence: We are a couple.

english: One word; in short; to put it simply
cantonese_sentence: 總之，一個字：正！
jyutping_sentence: zung2 zi1, jat1 go3 zi6: zeng3!
english_sentence: Basically, in short: Awesome!

cantonese_sentence: 等我一個鐘
jyutping_sentence: dang2 ngo5 jat1 go3 jung1
english_sentence: Wait for me for an hour

english: Bone (often used as a single rib bone in Cantonese cuisine)
cantonese_sentence: 我想叫一個骨食吓。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 soeng2 giu3 jat1 go3 gat1 sik6 haa5.
english_sentence: I want to order a bone (rib) to eat.

cantonese_sentence: 我哋一人一個開，咁就公平喇!
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 jat1 jan4 jat1 go3 hoi1, gam2 zau6 gung1 ping4 laa3!
english_sentence: Let's each take one portion, then it's fair!

english: One by one, one or two, a few
cantonese_sentence: 佢一個兩個咁走咗去玩。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat1 go3 loeng5 go3 gam2 zau2 zo2 heoi3 waan2.
english_sentence: They left to play one by one.

english: A foot of cow dung; Figuratively, something very undesirable or problematic, a mess, a load of trouble.
cantonese_sentence: 呢單嘢真係一腳牛屎。
jyutping_sentence: ni1 daan1 je5 zan1 hai6 jat1 goek3 ngau4 si2.
english_sentence: This matter is really a load of trouble.

english: To do everything oneself, one-man show
cantonese_sentence: 呢間鋪頭佢一腳踢晒㗎。
jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 pou3 tau2 keoi5 jat1 goek3 tek3 saai3 gaa3.
english_sentence: He does everything in this shop himself.

english: To summarize in one sentence/to cut to the chase
cantonese_sentence: 一句講晒，即係我哋冇錢。
jyutping_sentence: jat1 geoi3 gong2 saai3, zik1 hai6 ngo5 dei6 mou5 cin2.
english_sentence: To cut to the chase, we have no money.

jyutping: jat1 geoi3 hei2 loeng5 geoi3 zi2
english: Quickly starting and quickly stopping; to be fickle; inconsistent; short-lived (enthusiasm).
cantonese_sentence: 佢做嘢一句起兩句止，無乜恆心嘅。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 je5 jat1 geoi3 hei2 loeng5 geoi3 zi2, mou5 mat1 hang4 sam1 ge3.
english_sentence: He starts things quickly and stops quickly, he doesn't have much perseverance.

jyutping: jat1 haai5 bat1 jyu4 jat1 haai5
english: Each crab is worse than the last. (Things are getting progressively worse.)
cantonese_sentence: 而家啲電視劇真係一蟹不如一蟹。
jyutping_sentence: ji4 gaa1 di1 din6 si6 kek6 zan1 hai6 jat1 haai5 bat1 jyu4 jat1 haai5.
english_sentence: These days, TV dramas are really getting worse and worse.

cantonese_sentence: 一係你聽我講，一係我就走。
jyutping_sentence: jat1 hai6 nei5 ting1 ngo5 gong2, jat1 hai6 ngo5 zau6 zau2.
english_sentence: Either you listen to me, or I'll leave.

cantonese_sentence: 呢件衫一口價三百蚊，唔講價㗎。
jyutping_sentence: ni1 gin6 saam1 jat1 hau2 gaa3 saam1 baak3 man1, m4 gong2 gaa3 gaa3.
english_sentence: This shirt is a fixed price of three hundred dollars, no bargaining.

english: In one go; in one breath; without stopping
cantonese_sentence: 我一氣飲晒杯嘢
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 jat1 hei3 jam2 saai3 bui1 je5
english_sentence: I drank the whole drink in one go.

english: A face full of tears; on the verge of tears; ready to burst into tears
cantonese_sentence: 佢俾人鬧到一殼眼淚。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 bei2 jan4 naau6 dou3 jat1 hok3 ngaan5 leoi6.
english_sentence: He/She was scolded to the point of being on the verge of tears.

english: Methodically; carefully; in detail; one thing at a time
cantonese_sentence: 你一一二二講畀我聽啦。
jyutping_sentence: nei5 jat1 jat1 ji6 ji6 gong2 bei2 ngo5 ting1 laa1.
english_sentence: Tell me about it in detail.

cantonese_sentence: 佢哋喺酒吧識咗，發生咗一夜情。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 hai2 jau5 baa1 sik1 zo2, faat3 sang1 zo2 jat1 je6 cing4.
english_sentence: They met in a bar and had a one-night stand.

english: A small amount of money; loose change
cantonese_sentence: 我冇帶銀包，得返一二角係身。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 mou5 daai3 ngan4 baau1, dak1 faan1 jat1 ji6 gok3 hai6 san1.
english_sentence: I didn't bring my wallet, I only have a little loose change on me.

english: Might as well; Let's just; Decidedly
cantonese_sentence: 一於咁樣做啦！
jyutping_sentence: jat1 jyu1 gam2 joeng2 zou6 laa1!
english_sentence: Let's just do it this way! / Might as well do it this way! / We're doing it this way! (Decisively)

cantonese_sentence: 聽日有個一元拍賣，你想唔想去睇吓？
jyutping_sentence: ting1 jat6 jau5 go3 jat1 jyun4 paak3 maai6, nei5 soeng2 m4 soeng2 heoi3 tai2 haa5?
english_sentence: There's a dollar auction tomorrow, do you want to go take a look?

cantonese_sentence: 你咁細個唔好睇一級片啦！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam3 sai3 go3 m4 hou2 tai2 jat1 gap1 pin3 laa1!
english_sentence: You're so young, you shouldn't watch pornographic films!

english: messy, dishevelled (referring to hair or appearance)
cantonese_sentence: 佢個頭成日都一纊掕咁嘅
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 go3 tau4 sing4 jat6 dou1 jat1 kwong3 laang6 gam2 ge3
english_sentence: Her hair is always so messy.

cantonese_sentence: 嗰度好多一樓鳳，夜晚好嘈。
jyutping_sentence: go2 dou6 hou2 do1 jat1 lau2 fung6, je6 maan5 hou2 cou4.
english_sentence: There are many one-floor brothels there; it's very noisy at night.

jyutping: jat1 lei5 tung1 bak1 lei5 ming4
english: Once you understand one principle, you'll understand hundreds.
cantonese_sentence: 你明咗基本嘅語法，咁學其他語言就一理通百理明㗎啦。
