english: If you stop working, you stop eating. (Literally: Hand stop, mouth stop)
cantonese_sentence: 我哋手停口停，唔做嘢就冇錢開飯㗎喇。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 sau2 ting4 hau2 ting4, m4 zou6 je5 zau6 mou5 cin2 hoi1 faan6 gaa3 laa3.
english_sentence: We live hand-to-mouth; if we don't work, we won't have money for food.

english: To pilfer, pocket something small, or take a small advantage (often implying something done quickly and subtly).
cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺公司手抽啲文具返屋企用。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 hai2 gung1 si1 sau2 cau1 di1 man4 geoi6 faan1 uk1 kei2 yung6.
english_sentence: He often pilfers stationery from the company to use at home.

cantonese_sentence: 你件衫嘅手袖太長啦。
jyutping_sentence: nei5 gin6 saam1 ge3 sau2 zau6 taai3 coeng4 laa1.
english_sentence: The sleeves of your shirt are too long.

cantonese_sentence: 佢俾法官判咗守行為一年。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 bei2 faat3 gun1 pun3 zo2 sau2 hang4 wai4 jat1 nin4.
english_sentence: He was given a good behaviour bond of one year by the judge.

cantonese_sentence: 我每個星期日都守禮拜。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 mui5 go3 sing1 kei4 jat6 dou1 sau2 lai5 baai3.
english_sentence: I attend church service every Sunday.

english: To remain a widow/widower and celibate (typically implying forced circumstance, e.g., due to husband's disappearance or imprisonment). It literally means "to guard/maintain living widowhood."
cantonese_sentence: 佢老公失蹤咗十年，佢一直守生寡。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 lou5 gung1 sat1 zung1 zo2 sap6 nin4, keoi5 jat1 zik6 sau2 sang1 gwaa2.
english_sentence: Her husband has been missing for ten years, she has been remaining a celibate widow all along.

cantonese_sentence: 呢個係我嘅首本好戲。
jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 hai6 ngo5 ge3 sau2 bun2 hou2 hei3.
english_sentence: This is my signature performance.

cantonese_sentence: 佢係公司嘅首席執行官。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 gung1 si1 ge3 sau2 zik6 zik1 hang4 gun1.
english_sentence: He is the chief executive officer of the company.

cantonese_sentence: 犯首罪嘅人通常會判處死刑。
jyutping_sentence: faan6 sau2 zeoi6 ge3 jan4 tung1 soeng4 wui5 pun3 cyu2 sei2 ying4.
english_sentence: People who commit capital crimes are usually sentenced to death.

cantonese_sentence: 我哋要俾咗首期先可以買到呢間屋。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 jiu3 bei2 zo2 sau2 kei4 sin1 ho2 ji5 maai5 dou2 ni1 gaan1 uk1.
english_sentence: We need to pay the down payment first before we can buy this house.

english: beginning and end; from start to finish
cantonese_sentence: 呢件事嘅首尾我都唔知道。
jyutping_sentence: ni1 gin6 si6 ge3 sau2 mei5 ngo5 dou1 m4 zi1 dou3.
english_sentence: I don't know the beginning and end of this matter. / I don't know this matter from beginning to end.

english: Skinny and frail, like a bundle of firewood; very thin and weak
cantonese_sentence: 佢瘦骨瀨柴咁，行兩步都喘氣。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sau3 gwat1 laai6 caai4 gam2, haang4 loeng5 bou6 dou1 cyun2 hei3.
english_sentence: He's so skinny and frail that he gets breathless after walking only a few steps.

english: Skinny; bony; excessively thin (often used in a derogatory or teasing manner)
cantonese_sentence: 佢瘦骨仙咁，真係要食多啲嘢喇。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sau3 gwat1 sin1 gam2, zan1 hai6 jiu3 sik6 do1 di1 je5 laa3.
english_sentence: He/She is so skinny, really needs to eat more!

cantonese_sentence: 佢瘦蜢蜢咁，好似冇乜力咁嘅。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sau3 maang1 maang1 gam2, hou2 ci5 mou5 mat1 lik6 gam2 ge3.
english_sentence: He is so skinny and lanky, he seems like he doesn't have much strength.

cantonese_sentence: 我諗住去gym room做運動瘦身。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 nim2 zyu6 heoi3 gym room zou6 wan6 dung6 sau3 san1.
english_sentence: I'm thinking of going to the gym to exercise and slim down.

cantonese_sentence: 我驚佢會搵仇家嚟報仇
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ging1 keoi5 wui5 wan2 cau4 gaa1 lai4 bou3 cau4
english_sentence: I'm afraid he will find his enemies to take revenge.

cantonese_sentence: 佢哋兩個之間有仇口。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 loeng5 go3 zi1 gaan1 jau5 cau4 hau2.
english_sentence: There's a feud between those two.

english: to receive; to bear; to suffer
cantonese_sentence: 我受唔到咁大壓力呀!
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 sau6 m4 dou2 gam3 daai6 aat3 lik6 aa3!
english_sentence: I can't take this much pressure!

cantonese_sentence: 廣告嘅受眾主要係年輕人。
jyutping_sentence: gwong2 gou3 ge3 sau6 zung3 zyu2 jiu3 hai6 nin4 ging1 jan4.
english_sentence: The target audience of the advertisement is mainly young people.

english: To be at someone's beck and call; to be bossed around
cantonese_sentence: 佢成日受人二分四，真係慘。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 sau6 jan4 ji6 fan1 sei3, zan1 hai6 caam2.
english_sentence: He's always at someone's beck and call, it's really miserable.

english: Yields to soft approach, not to hard approach (or: responds to gentleness, not to force)
cantonese_sentence: 佢呢個人受軟唔受硬㗎，你好好聲同佢講，佢就會聽你講喇。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ni1 go3 jan4 sau6 jyun5 m4 sau6 ngaang6 gaa3, nei5 hou2 hou2 seng1 tung4 keoi5 gong2, keoi5 zau6 wui5 ting1 nei5 gong2 laa1.
english_sentence: This person responds to gentleness, not to force. If you speak nicely to him, he will listen to you.

english: To bear force/stress, to be subjected to a force.
cantonese_sentence: 棟大廈受力好大。
jyutping_sentence: dung6 daai6 haa6 sau6 lik6 hou2 daai6.
english_sentence: This building bears a lot of force/stress.

english: Well-received, to go down well with, to be popular
cantonese_sentence: 佢啲爛gag好受落㗎。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei1 laan6 gag1 hou2 sau6 lok6 gaa3.
english_sentence: His bad jokes are very well-received (people like them a lot).

cantonese_sentence: 我真係受唔住佢嘅嘈吵聲。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zan1 hai6 sau6 m4 zyu6 keoi5 ge3 cou4 caau2 seng1.
english_sentence: I really cannot stand/bear his/her noise.

english: Can't afford; unable to bear (emotionally or financially)
cantonese_sentence: 我受唔起咁貴嘅嘢.
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 sau6 m4 hei2 gam3 gwai3 ge3 je5.
english_sentence: I can't afford such expensive things.

english: Tea ceremony reception/Accepting the tea ceremony (traditionally, to officially welcome a new family member, often a daughter-in-law)
cantonese_sentence: 佢哋聽日會受茶禮，正式成為一家人。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 ting1 jat6 wui5 sau6 caa4 lai5, zing3 sik1 sing4 wai4 jat1 gaa1 jan4.
english_sentence: They will have the tea ceremony tomorrow, officially becoming a family.

cantonese_sentence: 我喺呢間公司受薪三年喇。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hai2 ni1 gaan1 gung1 si1 sau6 san1 saam1 nin4 laa3.
english_sentence: I have been employed by this company for three years.

cantonese_sentence: 祝你生日快樂，身體健康，長命百歲。
jyutping_sentence: zuk1 nei5 saang1 jat6 faai3 lok6, san1 tai2 gin6 hong1, coeng4 ming6 baak3 seoi3.
english_sentence: Happy birthday to you, good health, and may you live to a hundred years.

english: Coffin (usually referring to one for elderly people, implying longevity)
cantonese_sentence: 佢哋準備咗副壽板俾阿嫲
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 zyun2 bei6 zo2 fu3 sau6 baan2 bei2 aa3 po4
english_sentence: They prepared a coffin for Grandma.

cantonese_sentence: 阿婆生日，我哋買咗好多壽包慶祝。
jyutping_sentence: aa3 po4 saang1 jat6, ngo5 dei6 maai5 zo2 hou2 do1 sau6 baau1 hing3 zuk1.
english_sentence: We bought a lot of longevity peach buns to celebrate Grandma's birthday.

english: A term of endearment for a young person (often a child), implying cuteness or cherubic features; sometimes used sarcastically for a slightly older, mischievous child.
cantonese_sentence: 個壽仔真係得意。
jyutping_sentence: go3 sau6 zai2 zan1 hai6 dak1 ji3.
english_sentence: That little darling is really adorable.

cantonese_sentence: 過身嘅時候要著壽衣
jyutping_sentence: gwo3 san1 ge3 si4 hau6 jiu3 zoek3 sau6 ji1
english_sentence: When someone passes away, they need to wear burial clothes.

cantonese_sentence: 我想食壽司。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 soeng2 sik6 sau6 si1.
english_sentence: I want to eat sushi.

english: God of Longevity; an old man, especially one who is jovial and has a long white beard.
cantonese_sentence: 個壽星公笑得好開心。
jyutping_sentence: go3 sau6 sing1 gung1 siu3 dak1 hou2 hoi1 sam1.
english_sentence: That old man (God of Longevity) is smiling very happily.

jyutping: sau6 sing1 gung1 diu3 geng2 — him4 ming6 coeng4
english: A God of Longevity hanging himself - complaining that his life is too long. (Similar to "biting the hand that feeds you" or "not appreciating your blessings")
cantonese_sentence: 你咁樣做咪即係壽星公吊頸——嫌命長囉！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam2 joeng2 zou6 mai1 zik1 hai6 sau6 sing1 gung1 diu3 geng2 — him4 ming6 coeng4 lo1!
english_sentence: Doing it like that is just like a God of Longevity hanging himself - complaining his life is too long! (You're asking for trouble!)

cantonese_sentence: 你真係個壽頭嚟㗎！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 zan1 hai6 go3 sau6 tau4 lai4 gaa3!
english_sentence: You are really an idiot!

cantonese_sentence: 你咁壽頭壽腦，點做嘢㗎？
jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam3 sau6 tau4 sau6 nou5, dim2 zou6 je5 gaa3?
english_sentence: You're so scatterbrained, how can you get anything done?

english: A little bit, a small amount
cantonese_sentence: 畀啲錢我買嘢食啦，就算些少都好。
jyutping_sentence: bei2 di1 cin2 ngo5 maai5 je5 sik6 laa1, zau6 syun3 se1 siu2 dou1 hou2.
english_sentence: Give me some money to buy food, even if it's just a little bit.

cantonese_sentence: 我哋頭痕就係啲客成日要賖數。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 tau4 han4 zau6 si6 di1 haak3 sing4 jat6 jiu3 se1 sou3.
english_sentence: What makes us worried is that the customers always want to buy on credit.

cantonese_sentence: 我寫包單佢一定會幫你。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 se2 baau1 daan1 keoi5 jat1 ding6 wui5 bong1 nei5.
english_sentence: I guarantee that he will definitely help you.

english: Photography, photo album, pin-up photo (depending on context)
cantonese_sentence: 我買咗本寫真集。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 maai5 zo2 bun2 se2 zan1 gap6.
english_sentence: I bought a photo album.

cantonese_sentence: 我喺寫字樓返工。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hai2 se2 zi6 lau2 faan1 gung1.
english_sentence: I work in an office.

cantonese_sentence: 我張寫字枱好亂呀!
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zoeng1 se2 zi6 toi2 hou2 lyun6 aa3!
english_sentence: My desk is so messy!

cantonese_sentence: 我尋日食咗唔乾淨嘅嘢，依家不停咁瀉。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 cam4 jat6 sik6 zo2 m4 gon1 zing6 ge3 je5, ji1 ga1 bat1 ting4 gam2 se3.
english_sentence: Yesterday I ate something unclean, and now I have constant diarrhea.

english: To shirk responsibility, to pass the buck
cantonese_sentence: 佢成日卸膊，乜嘢都唔肯做。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 se3 bok3, mat1 je5 dou1 m4 hang2 zou6.
english_sentence: He always shirks responsibility and refuses to do anything.

cantonese_sentence: 我間房嘅舍監好nice㗎。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gaan1 fong2 ge3 se3 gaam1 hou2 nice gaa3.
english_sentence: The dormitory warden for my room is very nice.

cantonese_sentence: 我驚蛇呀！
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 geng1 se4 aa3!
english_sentence: I'm afraid of snakes!

english: Snake pit; den of iniquity; a place where bad people gather.
cantonese_sentence: 嗰度成個蛇竇咁，千祈唔好行埋去！
jyutping_sentence: go2 dou6 sing4 go3 se4 dau3 gam2, cin1 kai4 m4 hou2 haang4 maai4 heoi3!
english_sentence: That place is like a snake pit, definitely don't go near it!

english: Absolutely, definitely; To an extreme degree (negative connotation). Literally, even snakes would die.
cantonese_sentence: 佢嬲到蛇都死
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 nau1 dou3 se4 dou1 si2
english_sentence: He's so angry he could kill. (lit. He's so angry, even snakes would die.)

english: small snake; specifically used to describe a "cold sore" or herpes labialis
cantonese_sentence: 我嘴唇生咗蛇仔呀。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zeoi2 seon4 saang1 zo2 se4 zai2 aa3.
english_sentence: I have a cold sore on my lip.

cantonese_sentence: 佢份人好蛇呱，小心啲好啲。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 fan6 jan4 hou2 se4 gwaa1, siu2 sam1 di1 hou2 di1.
english_sentence: He's a very devious person, you'd better be careful.

cantonese_sentence: 我想買兩個蛇果。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 soeng2 maai5 loeng5 go3 se4 gwo2.
english_sentence: I want to buy two Red Delicious apples.

cantonese_sentence: 地下有條蛇殼
jyutping_sentence: dei6 haa6 jau5 tiu4 se4 hok3
english_sentence: There's a snakeskin on the ground.

jyutping: se4 jau5 se4 lou6, syu2 jau5 syu2 lou6
english: Snakes have snake paths, rats have rat paths. (Everyone has their own way of getting by/succeeding.)
cantonese_sentence: 唔使擔心佢，蛇有蛇路，鼠有鼠路，佢自然會搞掂。
jyutping_sentence: m4 sai2 daam1 sam1 keoi5, se4 jau5 se4 lou6, syu2 jau5 syu2 lou6, keoi5 zi6 jin4 wui2 gaau2 dim6.
english_sentence: Don't worry about him, everyone has their own way of getting by, he'll naturally figure it out.

english: Shifty-eyed; having a sneaky or untrustworthy look in one's eyes
cantonese_sentence: 佢成日蛇喱眼咁望住人，唔知諗乜嘢。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 se4 lei1 ngaan5 gam2 mong5 zyu6 jan4, m4 zi1 lam2 mat1 je5.
english_sentence: He's always looking at people with a shifty look in his eyes, I don't know what he's thinking.

english: A den of snakes and rats; birds of a feather (negative connotation, implying a group of bad people colluding)
cantonese_sentence: 佢哋蛇鼠一窩，專門呃人嘅錢。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 se4 syu2 jat1 wo1, zyun1 mun4 aak1 jan4 ge3 cin2.
english_sentence: They are birds of a feather, specializing in swindling people out of their money.

english: Snakehead, used to refer to a human smuggler.
cantonese_sentence: 唔好信啲蛇頭，佢哋好多都係呃人嘅。
jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 seon3 di1 se4 tau4, keoi5 dei6 hou2 do1 dou1 hai6 aak1 jan4 ge3.
english_sentence: Don't trust those human smugglers, many of them are con artists.

cantonese_sentence: 佢個樣蛇頭鼠眼，唔知諗緊乜嘢衰嘢。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 go3 joeng2 se4 tau4 syu2 ngaan5, m4 zi1 naam2 gan2 mat1 je5 seoi1 je5.
english_sentence: He looks shifty-eyed, I wonder what kind of bad things he's thinking.

cantonese_sentence: 佢成日蛇王，所以俾老細鬧。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 se4 wong4-2, so2 ji5 bei2 lou5 sai3 naau6.
english_sentence: He's always slacking off, so his boss scolds him.

cantonese_sentence: 我哋需要社工嘅協助。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 seoi1 jiu3 se5 gung1 ge3 hip3 zo6.
english_sentence: We need the help of a social worker.

cantonese_sentence: 阿婆成日去社署問拎援助金。
jyutping_sentence: a3 po4 seng4 jat6 heoi3 se5 cyu5 man6 ling1 jyun4 zo6 gam1.
english_sentence: The old woman often goes to the Social Welfare Department to ask for social security allowance.

cantonese_sentence: 佢已經死咗喇。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ji5 ging1 sei2 zo2 laa3.
english_sentence: He/She is already dead.

english: Do something drastic to prove a point, often self-destructive or overly dramatic, to show someone how wrong they are. Figuratively "die for you to see".
cantonese_sentence: 佢激到話要跳樓死畀你睇！
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gik1 dou3 waa6 jiu3 tiu3 lau2 sei2 bei2 nei5 tai2!
english_sentence: He was so angry that he said he would jump off a building to die for you to see! (Meaning: He was so angry that he threatened to commit suicide to prove you wrong/show you what you've done.)

english: A lot of people died; a lot of casualties
cantonese_sentence: 今次交通意外死得人多，真係好慘。
jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 gaau1 tung1 ji3 ngoi6 si2 dak1 jan4 do1, zan1 hai6 hou2 caam2.
english_sentence: This traffic accident had a lot of casualties; it's really tragic.

english: Best friend, die-hard friend, close buddy
cantonese_sentence: 我哋係死黨，咩都講！
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 hai6 sei2 dong2, me1 dou1 gong2!
english_sentence: We are best friends, we tell each other everything!

english: Facing imminent death/Facing a desperate situation
cantonese_sentence: 你都死到臨頭，仲咁囂張！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 dou1 sei2 dou3 lam4 tau4, zung6 gam3 hiu1 zoeng1!
english_sentence: You're facing imminent death and you're still so arrogant!

cantonese_sentence: 你個死仔包，又偷食我啲嘢！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 go3 sei2 zai2 baau1, jau6 tau1 sik6 ngo5 di1 je5!
english_sentence: You little rascal, you stole my things again!

english: Dead straight; completely unresponsive; "dead as a doornail"
cantonese_sentence: 部電腦死咗機，死直咗。
jyutping_sentence: bou6 din6 nou5 si2 zo2 gei1, si2 zik6 zo2.
english_sentence: The computer crashed, it's completely unresponsive.

english: All talk and no action; big talker but doesn't deliver
cantonese_sentence: 佢死剩把口，講就天下無敵，做就無能為力。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sei2 sing6 baa2 hau2, gong2 zau6 tin1 haa6 mou4 dik1, zou6 zau6 mou4 nang4 wai4 lik6.
english_sentence: He's all talk and no action, talks like he's invincible, but is completely incapable when it comes to doing anything.

english: Remnant of a dead/disgraced family; "last seed" (very derogatory)
cantonese_sentence: 你條死剩種，梗係冇好嘢啦!
jyutping_sentence: nei5 tiu4 sei2 sing6 zung2, gang2 hai6 mou5 hou2 je5 laa1!
english_sentence: You, you last seed, of course you're no good! (You wouldn't amount to anything!)

cantonese_sentence: 如果唔保護啲動物，佢哋好快就會死絕種㗎啦。
jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 m4 bou2 wu6 di1 dung6 mat6, keoi5 dei6 hou2 faai3 zau6 wui5 sei2 zyut6 zung2 gaa3 laa1.
english_sentence: If we don't protect these animals, they will become extinct very quickly.

english: Stalled, broken down (usually referring to vehicles), "dead fire"
cantonese_sentence: 架車突然死咗火。
jyutping_sentence: gaa3 ce1 dat6 jin4 sei2 zo2 fo2.
english_sentence: The car suddenly stalled.

english: To stubbornly defend a hopeless situation; to double down on a lost cause.
cantonese_sentence: 佢明知自己錯咗，但係都重要死雞撐飯蓋。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ming4 zi1 zi6 gei2 co3 zo2, daan6 hai6 dou1 zung6 jiu3 sei2 gai1 caang3 faan6 goi3.
english_sentence: He clearly knows he's wrong, but he's still stubbornly defending his position.

english: Extremely, excessively, to a deadly degree (emphasizing intensity)
cantonese_sentence: 佢死咁捱夜，搞到個人殘哂。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sei2 gam2 ngaai4 je2, gaau2 dou3 go3 jan4 caan4 saai3.
english_sentence: He stayed up all night working extremely hard, making him look totally exhausted.

cantonese_sentence: 聽日考試，我乜都未溫，今次死梗！
jyutping_sentence: ting1 jat6 haau2 si5, ngo5 mat1 dou1 mei6 wan1, gam1 ci3 sei2 gang2!
english_sentence: Tomorrow is the exam and I haven't studied anything, I'm definitely screwed this time!

english: to guess wildly; to make a blind guess
cantonese_sentence: 唔好死估估啦，諗清楚先啦！
jyutping_sentence: m4 ho2 sei2 gu2 gu2 laa1, nam2 cing1 co2 sin1 laa1!
english_sentence: Don't guess wildly, think carefully first!

english: You rascal! / You little devil! (term of endearment, often between lovers or close family)
cantonese_sentence: 死鬼，你又唔聽我講！
jyutping_sentence: sei2 gwai2, nei5 jau6 m4 teng1 ngo5 gong2!
english_sentence: You rascal, you never listen to me!

english: (expression of near-death experience) barely survived; almost died; got a scare
cantonese_sentence: 啱啱差啲死過，架車突然衝出嚟!
jyutping_sentence: ngaam1 ngaam1 caa1 di1 sei2 gwo3, gaa3 ce1 dat6 jin4 cung1 chut1 lai4!
english_sentence: I almost died just now, a car suddenly rushed out!

english: A narrow escape from death; to come back from the brink.
cantonese_sentence: 我琴日差啲死過翻生，架車差啲撞落嚟。

english: Don't waste food; eat it all.

english: To be nosy, to stick one's nose into other people's business
cantonese_sentence: 你唔好咁鍾意食井水啦！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 gam3 zung1 ji3 sik6 zeng2 seoi2 laa1!
english_sentence: Don't be so nosy! / Stop sticking your nose into other people's business!

english: to have one's appetite aroused; to be tempted to eat something delicious
cantonese_sentence: 我見到碟燒鵝，即刻食指大動。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gin3 dou2 dip6 siu1 ngo2, zik1 hak1 sik6 zi2 daai6 dung6.
english_sentence: When I saw the plate of roast goose, my appetite was immediately aroused.

english: To take advantage of oneself; to shoot oneself in the foot; to cannibalize one's own resources/efforts.
cantonese_sentence: 你咁樣做咪即係食自己囉!
jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam2 joeng2 zou6 mai1 zik1 hai6 sik6 zi6 gei2 lo1!
english_sentence: Doing it this way is just shooting yourself in the foot!

english: Fuck you; Go fuck yourself. (Extremely rude and vulgar)
cantonese_sentence: 你再嘈我就叫你食蕉！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 zoi3 cou4 ngo5 zau6 giu3 nei5 sik6 jiu1!
english_sentence: If you make any more noise, I'll tell you to fuck off!

cantonese_sentence: 我唔小心食咗人隻車，好內疚。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 siu2 sam1 sik6 zo2 jan4 zek3 ce1, hou2 noi6 gau3.
english_sentence: I accidentally ate someone's rook, I feel really guilty.

cantonese_sentence: 唔好食咗草龍啦，跌親啫，唔係咩大件事。
jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 sik6 zo2 cou2 lung4 laa1, dit3 can1 ze1, m4 hai6 me1 daai6 gin6 si6.
english_sentence: Don't exaggerate, you just fell, it's not a big deal.

jyutping: sik6 zuk1 sik6 faan6 kaau3 saai3 nei5
english: My livelihood depends entirely on you (lit. whether I eat congee or rice depends entirely on you).
cantonese_sentence: 以後我哋食粥食飯靠晒你喇！
jyutping_sentence: ji5 hau6 ngo5 dei6 sik6 zuk1 sik6 faan6 kaau3 saai3 nei5 laa1!
english_sentence: From now on, our livelihoods depend entirely on you!

cantonese_sentence: 佢係一個出名嘅食家，對食物嘅要求好高。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 jat1 go3 ceot1 ming4 ge3 sik6 gaa1, deoi3 sik6 mat6 ge3 jiu1 kau4 hou2 gou1.
english_sentence: He/She is a famous food connoisseur, with very high standards for food.

english: To overcharge, to inflate prices (often surreptitiously), to price gouge.
cantonese_sentence: 間餐廳成日食價，都唔知點解咁多人去。
jyutping_sentence: gaan1 caan1 ting1 sing4 jat6 sik6 gaa3, dou1 m4 zi1 dim2 gaai2 gam3 do1 jan4 heoi3.
english_sentence: That restaurant always overcharges, I don't know why so many people go.

english: To exploit someone (often by taking a disproportionate cut of money or resources)
cantonese_sentence: 咪成日食夾棍啦，分啲利益俾大家啦！
jyutping_sentence: mai5 sing4 jat6 sik6 gaap3 gwan3 laa1, fan1 di1 lei6 jik1 bei2 daai6 gaa1 laa1!
english_sentence: Don't always exploit people, share some of the profits with everyone!

cantonese_sentence: 佢食嘢成日食夾搦，搞到周圍都係。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sik6 je5 seng4 jat6 sik6 gaap3 nik1, gaau2 dou3 zau1 wai4 dou1 hai6.
english_sentence: He always eats so greedily and messily, getting food everywhere around him.

jyutping: sik6 gei2 do1 zoek3 gei2 do1 zing2 ding6 ge3
english: What you eat and wear is predetermined (by fate/karma).
cantonese_sentence: 人生就係食幾多着幾多整定嘅，唔使太過強求。
jyutping_sentence: jan4 sang1 zau6 hai6 sik6 gei2 do1 zoek3 gei2 do1 zing2 ding6 ge3, m4 sai2 taai3 gwo3 koeng5 kau4.
english_sentence: Life is predetermined in terms of what you eat and wear, so don't force things too much.

english: Culinary experience/expertise, advice on food and dining
cantonese_sentence: 佢啲食經好豐富，成日帶我去啲好正嘅餐廳。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 sik6 ging1 hou2 fung1 fu3, seng4 jat6 daai3 ngo5 heoi3 di1 hou2 zeng3 ge3 caan1 teng1.
english_sentence: His culinary experience is very rich, he often takes me to some really good restaurants.

english: Rigidly following tradition, unable to adapt
cantonese_sentence: 阿哥都唔識變通，成日食古不化。
jyutping_sentence: aa3 go1 dou1 m4 sik1 bin3 tung1, seng4 jat6 sik6 gu2 bat1 faa3.
english_sentence: My older brother doesn't know how to be flexible and is always rigidly following tradition.

english: To be lazy and unproductive, living off one's savings or inherited wealth; literally "eating the seeds".
cantonese_sentence: 佢成日遊手好閒，食穀種咁款。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 jau4 sau2 hou2 haan4, sik6 guk1 zung2 gam2 kwan2.
english_sentence: He is always idle and doing nothing, like he's just living off his savings.

english: Once tasted, always wanting more; a dish so delicious you want to keep eating it.
cantonese_sentence: 呢間餐廳啲點心真係食過翻尋味，我哋下次一定要再嚟！
jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 caan1 teng1 di1 dim2 sam1 zan1 hai6 sik6 gwo3 faan1 cam4 mei6, ngo5 dei6 haa6 ci3 jat1 ding6 jiu3 zoi3 lai4!
english_sentence: This restaurant's dim sum is truly addictive, we definitely have to come again next time!

english: To have learned martial arts (literally: to have eaten overnight congee)
cantonese_sentence: 佢都識功夫，睇嚟都食過夜粥嘅。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dou1 sik1 gung1 fu1, tai2 lai4 dou1 sik6 gwo3 je6 zuk1 ge3.
english_sentence: He knows kung fu, looks like he's trained in martial arts.

jyutping: sik6 je5 daa2 bui3 zek3 gwat1 lok6
english: To be disgusted or repulsed by food.
cantonese_sentence: 佢一見到啲肥膏，就食嘢打背脊骨落。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat1 gin3 dou2 di1 fei4 gou1, zau6 sik6 je5 daa2 bui3 zek3 gwat1 lok6.
english_sentence: As soon as he saw the fatty parts, he was disgusted by the food.

english: To be skilled, often associated with martial arts training. Literally "to have eaten overnight congee".
cantonese_sentence: 你睇佢咁打得，都知佢食過夜粥啦。
jyutping_sentence: nei5 tai2 keoi5 gam3 daa2 dak1, dou1 zi1 keoi5 sik6 gwo3 je6 zuk1 laa1.
english_sentence: Look how well he fights, you know he has some training.

jyutping: sik6 je5 daa2 bui3 zek3 gwat1 lok6
english: To be so full that the food seemingly reaches your spine; to eat one's fill; to eat until one is very full.
cantonese_sentence: 我今日肚餓到死，食嘢打背脊骨落！
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 jat6 tou5 ngo6 dou3 sei2, sik6 je5 daa2 bui3 zek3 gwat1 lok6!
english_sentence: I was so hungry today that I ate until I was stuffed!

cantonese: 食嘢唔做嘢，做嘢打爛嘢
jyutping: sik6 je5 m4 zou6 je5, zou6 je5 daa2 laan6 je5
english: Eats without working, works and breaks things.
cantonese_sentence: 佢真係食嘢唔做嘢，做嘢打爛嘢，老細好唔鍾意佢。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zan1 hai6 sik6 je5 m4 zou6 je5, zou6 je5 daa2 laan6 je5, lou5 sai3 hou2 m4 zung1 ji3 keoi5.
english_sentence: He really eats without working, and when he works, he breaks things. The boss doesn't like him at all.

jyutping: sik6 jim4 do1 gwo3 nei5 sik6 mai5
english: To have eaten more salt than you've eaten rice (to have more experience than you)
cantonese_sentence: 你唔好同佢爭辯啦，佢食鹽多過你食米呀。
jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 tung4 keoi5 zaang1 bun6 laa1, keoi5 sik6 jim4 do1 gwo3 nei5 sik6 mai5 aa3.
english_sentence: Don't argue with him, he's much more experienced than you.

english: To live off someone else, typically a woman, without contributing equally to the relationship. Often carries a negative connotation of being lazy or a freeloader.
cantonese_sentence: 佢乜都唔做，靠老婆養，擺明食軟飯。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 mat1 dou1 m4 zou6, kaau3 lou5 po2 joeng5, baai2 ming4 sik6 jyun5 faan6.
english_sentence: He doesn't do anything, relies on his wife to support him, clearly living off her.

cantonese_sentence: 我好鍾意食蓮子羹，尤其係夏天嘅時候。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hou2 zung1 ji3 sik6 lin4 zi2 gang1, jau4 kei4 hai6 haa6 tin1 ge3 si4 hau2.
english_sentence: I really like eating lotus seed sweet soup, especially in the summertime.

cantonese_sentence: 我阿媽好注重食療，成日煲啲養生湯水。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 aa3 maa1 hou2 zyu3 zung6 sik6 liu4, seng4 jat6 bou1 di1 joeng5 sang1 tong1 seoi2.
english_sentence: My mother pays a lot of attention to dietary therapy, and often boils nourishing soups.

english: To fumble one's words, to have a slip of the tongue.
cantonese_sentence: 佢講嘢成日食螺絲。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2 je5 seng4 jat6 sik6 lo4 si1.
english_sentence: He often fumbles his words.

english: Getting married more than once, with the implication of being a "second-hand" spouse
cantonese_sentence: 佢都唔介意佢老婆食兩家茶禮，最緊要兩個人開心。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dou1 m4 gaai3 ji3 keoi5 lou5 po4 sik6 loeng5 gaa1 caa4 lai5, zeoi3 gan2 jiu3 loeng5 go3 jan4 hoi1 sam1.
english_sentence: He doesn't mind that his wife has been married before, the most important thing is that they are both happy.

jyutping: sik6 lung4 juk6 dou1 mou5 mei6
english: Nothing tastes good (even dragon meat). Describes a lack of appetite or interest in anything.
cantonese_sentence: 我今日唔舒服，食龍肉都冇味。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 jat6 m4 syu1 fuk6, sik6 lung4 juk6 dou1 mou5 mei6.
english_sentence: I don't feel well today, nothing tastes good to me.

english: To sulk; to be in a bad mood
cantonese_sentence: 佢成日食貓面，都唔知做乜
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 sik6 maau1 min6, dou1 m4 zi1 zou6 mat1
english_sentence: He/She is always sulking, I don't even know why.

jyutping: sik6 mai5 m4 zi1 mai5 gwai3
english: To not appreciate the value of things; to be out of touch with the struggles of everyday life.
cantonese_sentence: 佢屋企咁有錢，梗係食米唔知米貴啦！
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 uk1 kei2 gam3 jau5 cin2, gang2 hai6 sik6 mai5 m4 zi1 mai5 gwai3 laa1!
english_sentence: His family is so rich, of course he doesn't appreciate the value of things!

english: To win the final round (in Mahjong) and be the overall winner. Often used figuratively to mean achieving a last-minute victory.
cantonese_sentence: 佢一路都輸緊，點知最後食尾糊，贏晒！
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat1 lou6 dou1 syu1 gan2, dim2 zi1 zeoi3 hau6 sik6 mei5 wu2, wing4 saai3!
english_sentence: He was losing all along, who knew he would win the final round and win everything!

english: Palatability; Taste (referring to how good something tastes)
cantonese_sentence: 呢間餐廳嘅嘢食幾好食味㗎。
jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 caan1 teng1 ge3 je5 sik6 gei2 hou2 sik6 mei6 gaa3.
english_sentence: The food at this restaurant tastes pretty good.

english: To eat so much that it makes you stupid/dazed. Often implies being overwhelmed by good food.
cantonese_sentence: 你唔好食咁多啦，食懵你㗎！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 sik6 gam3 do1 laa1, sik6 mung2 nei5 gaa3!
english_sentence: Don't eat so much, you'll get dazed/stupid from eating so much!

english: To eat up one's allowance/budget; to overspend. It often implies spending it quickly and foolishly.
cantonese_sentence: 佢份人工唔高，成日都食額，好難儲到錢。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 fan6 jan4 gung1 m4 gou1, seng4 jat6 dou1 sik6 ngaak2, hou2 naan4 chyu5 dou2 chin2.
english_sentence: His salary isn't high, he always overspends, it's hard to save money.

cantonese_sentence: 我哋十二點半去食晏啦。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 sap6 ji6 dim2 bun3 heoi3 sik6 aan3 laa1.
english_sentence: Let's go have lunch at 12:30.

english: To be rejected, turned down, or given the cold shoulder (literally "eat lemon")
cantonese_sentence: 佢同阿May表白，結果食咗檸檬。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 tung4 aa3 Mei6 biu2 baak6, git3 gwo2 sik6 zo2 ning2 mung1.
english_sentence: He confessed to May, but ended up getting rejected.

english: Brainy; requiring intelligence; using your brain
cantonese_sentence: 佢好食腦，次次考試都考第一。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hou2 sik6 nou5, ci3 ci3 haau2 si5 dou1 haau2 dai6 jat1.
english_sentence: He's very brainy; he always comes first in exams.

english: Make a living through unconventional or illicit means (often involving gambling, scams, or minor illegal activities).
cantonese_sentence: 佢份人好懶, 成日諗住食偏門搵快錢.
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 fan6 jan4 hou2 laan5, sing4 jat6 lam2 zyu6 sik6 pin1 mun4 wan2 faai3 cin2.
english_sentence: He's very lazy and always thinking about making quick money through unconventional means.

english: To be a piece of cake; very easy.
cantonese_sentence: 呢條數好食生菜啫，你一定計到嘅。
jyutping_sentence: ni1 tiu4 sou3 hou2 sik6 saang1 coi3 ze1, nei5 jat1 ding6 gai3 dou2 ge3.
english_sentence: This calculation is a piece of cake, you can definitely do it.

english: To have nothing to eat; to be penniless; to live on air.
cantonese_sentence: 冇錢開飯，聽日食西北風囉！
jyutping_sentence: mou5 cin2 hoi1 faan6, ting1 jat6 sik6 sai1 bak1 fung1 lo1!
english_sentence: Don't have money to buy food, tomorrow we'll be living on air!

english: Good-for-nothing, useless person, literally "eat rice to block (yourself/others)"
cantonese_sentence: 你真係食塞米，乜都做唔好！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 zan1 hai6 sik6 sak1 mai5, mat1 dou1 zou6 m4 hou2!
english_sentence: You're really useless, you can't do anything right!

english: God of Cookery, Culinary God (often refers to someone with exceptional cooking skills)
cantonese_sentence: 佢煮嘢真係好有食神!
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zyu2 je5 zan1 hai6 hou2 jau5 sik6 san4!
english_sentence: He/She really has the touch of the God of Cookery when cooking!

english: To be made a scapegoat, to be wrongly blamed for something.
cantonese_sentence: 明明係佢唔記得熄燈，點解要我食死貓？
jyutping_sentence: ming4 ming4 hai6 keoi5 m4 gei3 dak1 sik1 dang1, dim2 gaai2 jiu3 ngo5 sik6 sei2 maau1?
english_sentence: Clearly he forgot to turn off the lights, why do I have to be the scapegoat?

english: Ungrateful; Bites the hand that feeds you (literally: eat shit, defecate rice)
cantonese_sentence: 你真係食屎屙飯，人哋幫咗你咁多，你仲要咁樣對佢！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 zan1 hai6 sik6 si2 o1 faan6, jan4 dei6 bong1 zo2 nei5 gam3 do1, nei5 zung6 jiu3 gam2 joeng2 deoi3 keoi5!
english_sentence: You're really ungrateful. People helped you so much, and you still treat them like this!

cantonese_sentence: 我哋今晚去邊間食肆食飯好呀？
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 gam1 maan5 heoi3 bin1 gaan1 sik6 si3 sik6 faan6 hou2 aa3?
english_sentence: Which restaurant should we go to for dinner tonight?

english: Exorbitant profit margin; ripping someone off.
cantonese_sentence: 呢間餐廳食水好深，啲嘢又貴又唔好食。
jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 caan1 teng1 sik6 seoi2 hou2 sam1, di1 je5 jau6 gwai3 jau6 m4 hou2 sik6.
english_sentence: This restaurant has a huge profit margin, the food is expensive and not tasty.

cantonese_sentence: 你食咗飯未呀？
jyutping_sentence: nei5 sik6 zo2 faan6 mei6 aa3?
english_sentence: Have you eaten yet?

english: henpecked/living under the thumb of one's wife
cantonese_sentence: 佢成日俾佢老婆鬧，食拖鞋飯咁款。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 bei2 keoi5 lou5 po2 naau6, sik6 to1 haai4 faan6 gam2 kwan2.
english_sentence: He always gets scolded by his wife; he's totally henpecked.

cantonese_sentence: 我今日想去茶餐廳食叉燒飯。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 jat6 soeng2 heoi3 caa4 caan1 teng1 sik6 caa1 siu1 faan6.
english_sentence: Today, I want to go to a cha chaan teng (Hong Kong-style cafe) to eat char siu rice.

english: To eat like a glutton; to eat very messily and greedily
cantonese_sentence: 你食嘢唔好食七咁食啦，好核突呀！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 sik6 je5 m4 hou2 sik6 cat1 gam2 sik6 laa1, hou2 hat6 dat6 aa3!
english_sentence: Don't eat like a glutton, it's disgusting!

english: To be on long-term government assistance/welfare
cantonese_sentence: 佢唔做嘢，淨係識食長糧。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 m4 zou6 je5, zing6 hai6 sik1 sik6 coeng4 loeng4.
english_sentence: He doesn't work, he only knows how to live off welfare.

cantonese_sentence: 我今日要去超級市場買食材煮晚餐。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 jat6 jiu3 heoi3 ceoi1 gei1 si5 coeng4 maai5 si4 coi4 zyu2 maan5 caan1.
english_sentence: Today I need to go to the supermarket to buy ingredients to cook dinner.

cantonese_sentence: 唔好亂拋垃圾，食環會罰錢㗎！
jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 lyun6 paau1 laap1 saap3, sik6 waan4 wui5 fat6 cin2 gaa3!
english_sentence: Don't litter, the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department will fine you!

english: To live or work in vain; to be a parasite; to freeload; to be useless and a waste of resources (literally, to eat rice for nothing/in vain)
cantonese_sentence: 你喺度淨係識得食枉米，都唔做嘢！
jyutping_sentence: nei5 hai2 dou6 zing6 hai6 sik1 dak1 sik6 wong2 mai5, dou1 m4 zou6 je5!
english_sentence: You just freeload here and don't do any work!

english: to be in prison (literally, "to eat the royal/government's rice")
cantonese_sentence: 佢衰咗偷嘢，而家要食皇家飯咯。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seoi1 zo2 tau1 je5, ji4 gaa1 jiu3 sik6 wong4 gaa1 faan6 lok3.
english_sentence: He messed up by stealing things, now he has to go to prison.

english: To be employed by the government, especially in law enforcement or the military; "eating the king's/government's rice"
cantonese_sentence: 佢讀完警校就去咗食皇家飯
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 duk6 jyun4 ging2 haau6 zau6 heoi3 zo2 sik6 wong4 gaa1 faan6
english_sentence: After finishing police academy, he went to "eat the king's/government's rice" (became a police officer).

cantonese_sentence: 我聽日要同啲朋友打牌，希望可以食糊啦！
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ting1 jat6 jiu3 tung4 di1 pang4 jau5 daa2 paai2, hei1 mong6 ho2 ji5 sik6 wu4 laa1!
english_sentence: I'm playing Mahjong with friends tomorrow, I hope I can win!

jyutping: sik6 wun2 min6 faan2 wun2 dai2
english: Ungrateful; biting the hand that feeds you; turning against someone who has helped you.
cantonese_sentence: 佢攞咗公司咁多着數，轉頭就跳槽去競爭對手公司，真係食碗面反碗底。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 lo2 zo2 gung1 si1 gam3 do1 zoek6 sou3, zyun3 tau4 zau6 tiu3 cou4 heoi3 ging6 zang1 deoi3 sau2 gung1 si1, zan1 hai6 sik6 wun2 min6 faan2 wun2 dai2.
english_sentence: He took so many benefits from the company, and then immediately jumped ship to a competitor company, he's really ungrateful (biting the hand that feeds him).

cantonese_sentence: 佢閃得好快。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sim2 dak1 hou2 faai3.
english_sentence: He dodged very quickly.

cantonese_sentence: 啱啱落狗屎嗰陣，我見到好大嘅閃電。
jyutping_sentence: ngaam1 ngaam1 lok6 gau2 si2 go2 zan6, ngo5 gin3 dou2 hou2 daai6 ge3 sim2 din6.
english_sentence: Just now when it was raining cats and dogs, I saw very big lightning.

cantonese_sentence: 佢對耳環閃閃炩，好靚呀！
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 deoi3 ji5 waan4 sim2 sim2 ling4, hou2 leng3 aa3!
english_sentence: Her earrings are sparkling and glittering, so beautiful!

english: Skittish, furtive, sneaky, lacking confidence (often describing someone who tries to avoid attention or responsibility)
cantonese_sentence: 佢個人好閃縮，有咩事都唔敢出頭。
jyutping_sentence: keoi5 go3 jan4 hou2 sim2 suk1, jau5 mat1 je5 dou1 m4 gam2 ceot1 tau4.
english_sentence: He's a very skittish person, he doesn't dare to take the lead in anything.

cantonese_sentence: 落雨喇，快啲去簷篷下面避雨啦！
jyutping_sentence: lok6 jyu5 la3, faai3 di1 heoi3 jim4 pung4 haa6 min6 bei6 jyu5 laa1!
english_sentence: It's raining, quickly go under the eaves to take shelter from the rain!

cantonese_sentence: 我哋食咗飯先啦。
jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 sik6 zo2 faan6 sin1 laa1.
english_sentence: Let's eat first.
